# short.win — Architecture and Implementation Blueprint

*Design document **v0.4.1** ("v4.1", fourth review round), 2026-09-27. Supersedes v0.4 of the same day. Baseline: [`docs/SPEC.md`](../SPEC.md) v0.3, including owner decisions **D1–D4** (owner-approved; this document does not change it). Economics: [`docs/design/ECONOMICS.md`](ECONOMICS.md) **v0.4.1** and its reference models [`sim/pool_model.py`](sim/pool_model.py) v0.4.1, [`sim/shortwin_sim.py`](sim/shortwin_sim.py) v0.4.1, the attack scripts in [`sim/attacks/`](sim/attacks/), the parameter gate [`sim/config_check.py`](sim/config_check.py) and the keeper cost model [`sim/keeper_cost.py`](sim/keeper_cost.py). Research inputs: every file in [`docs/research/`](../research/). Review input: the 33 first-round findings `C0-1` … `C1-15`, the 27 second-round findings `V1-1` … `V2-14`, the 25 third-round findings `R3A-1` … `R3A-13` and `R3B-1` … `R3B-12` with their two simplification lists, and the 20 fourth-round findings `R4A-1` … `R4A-10` and `R4B-1` … `R4B-10`; [Appendix A](#appendix-a-review-resolution) records the outcome of each one.*

This is the blueprint that the protocol, application and security work is built from. It turns SPEC, ECONOMICS and the research notes into accounts, instructions, byte layouts, checks, budgets, tests and milestones. You should be able to implement from this document without re-reading the research. Derivations are in ECONOMICS and in the research notes, and are referenced by section.

**Where ECONOMICS and this document meet, they agree exactly** (both v0.4.1; ECON's Raydium pool rules were synced to the program as built after M4 on 2026-09-28 — its changelog #91–#95 carries the M4 security review's eligibility floor and adoption liquidity rewrite and their verification's window floor, two-sample adoption liquidity and price warm-up, changelog 43 and 45 here, owner item O18; ECON #96 and row 46 here carry the PROPOSED post-change confirmation that replaces the adoption liquidity, M4R; ECON #98 and row 48 its keeper coverage and reference cap, M4F-1; ECON #99 and row 49 the owner's rule of 2026-09-29 that a switch carries open positions only if every one fits the new pool's opening caps, which reverts row 48's liquidity bursts; ECON #100 and row 50 its verification's resolutions: the carried fee-scaled caps at `min(φ_inc, φ_cand)`, the first fix's lows bound and `refresh_max_q` withdrawn; ECON #101 and row 51 the owner's decisions on that round's verification, FITS: the carried fee caps at most 25 bps, the liquidation spot leg at `max(L_live, L_ema')`, the keeper's per-second liquidity-anomaly coverage; ECON #103 and row 54 the doc sync after M5: the curve's caps on its reserves at the EMA price, M5-SEC-3; ECON #104 and row 55 the doc sync after M6: PumpSwap and the graduation as built, the negative-VQR tier inputs built, OWNER-M6R-1's third-party LP on canonical pools; ECON #105 and row 56 the M6 security review's fixes and the owner's decisions of 2026-09-30: PumpSwap's locked depth from its burned LP with the Raydium liquidity-push protections, the warm-up seed bounded downward, curve opens refused while PumpSwap's pool creation is disabled, the post-graduation exit delay accepted; ECON #106 and row 57 the owner's decision on M6D-1: PumpSwap credited on its burned LP only, `PUMPSWAP_LOCK_MIN_BPS` in sizing, the tier and — since its verification's M6E-1 — the exit reference's cap; ECON #107 and rows 58–59 M7: `set_coverage_pause`, the keeper's automatic degraded mode and budget as built under O17, ECON §5.8's cost model on the keeper's measured transactions). Parameter names, defaults, bounds and formulas are the ones in ECON §15 and ECON §2–§10. Numerics (type, scale, rounding, order of operations) are ECON §2.1, which is normative for the math crate. Architecture-only items (no economic effect) are marked as such. Where this document places a piece of ECON's logical market state in a particular account, it says so (for example the lock state on `MarketVault`, §2.3.6).

The per-second coverage while `ema_guard = 1`, the cap and the regressions stand.)* **M4F-1: post-switch keeper coverage and the reference cap** (PROPOSED with rows 46–47; owner items O17, O18; ECON #98, §5.8, §8.2, §12.12 (4)). The reference guard and M4X-2's input guard read `L_mlo`, the lower median of the ring's bucket liquidity lows. They hold only while every second carries an honest observation: a deposit sets the whole low of a second nobody else observed, and 5 such buckets of 8 move `L_mlo`. As built, `decide::market_needs` kept a healthy carried position per second only while `ema_warm > 0`, then every `idle_interval_s` (30 s), and `coverage::check_foreign` compared bucket prices only. A `[deposit k·LP counter, crank_price, withdraw]` every second then owned 29 of every 30 seconds after the gate: the guard cleared at ≈ +15 s, `L_ema` froze at the deposit's depth, and a genuine pump ended in S1 (the fork: lenders −10.056 SOL on a q/x 3.12 % position, the borrower zeroed; ECON §12.12 (4), `switch_warmup.py` part 4d: −12.553 to −14.092 SOL). **Keeper** (§7.1 duties 2 and 5): per second also while `ema_guard = 1` on a market with open positions (`MarketNeeds.guarded`); `record_view` keeps the venue depth `√(X·Y)` it read each second (dropped on a venue change), and `check_foreign` also starts a burst on a bucket whose `llo` / `lhi` deviates from it by more than `burst_dev_bps`. The last completed bucket's liquidity extremes come from the ring entry that integrated it. **Program, defense in depth** (§3.6, §3.7): `L_b = max(L_live, min(max(L_ema', L_slow), cap))` with `cap = engine::bounds::ref_depth_cap` = `⌊pool_d·10⁴/pool_lock_min_bps⌋` on a Raydium market, `None` elsewhere. `pool_d` is the locked depth the exit's own prologue refreshed, and `bounds::ref_liquidity` gains its `depth_cap` argument. The reference then credits the pool with no more depth than sizing does: a push lifts it by at most `λ/λ_min` of the depth, which liquidates ECON §12.12 (4)'s q 2.9 % rows under the old keeper but not its q 5.9 % rows. The keeper's `decide::project` computes the same cap (`Projection.depth_cap`). Regressions `m4r_it::m4f1_*` (§8.2 ★T-SWITCH-CONFIRM); I18 (d) checks `b_ref` at the capped `L_b`. ## Conventions

- **SPEC §x**: taken from `docs/SPEC.md` v0.3.
- **D1–D4**: the owner decisions recorded in SPEC v0.3 §0 and §14 on 2026-09-27. Binding.
- **ADOPTED Qn**: a first-pass owner question whose recommended default the owner adopted (revision brief). Still a configurable parameter with compiled bounds.
- **ECON §x / ECON Gnn / ECON Nn / ECON I-xx**: taken from `docs/design/ECONOMICS.md` v0.4 (section, register item, or invariant).
- **An (PROPOSED)**: an architecture decision that is not in SPEC, introduced or made concrete here. Every An is listed in §11. **OWNER** marks the few items that still need owner confirmation; they are collected in §10.
- **UNVERIFIED**: could not be confirmed against a primary source. Each one has a test gate (§12).
- Citations are in brackets and resolved in §13. `[V1]`–`[V20]` are checks run for this document on 2026-09-26/27.
- Amounts: lamports (u64), raw token units (u64), bps (1 bp = 0.01 %), ppm for venue fee rates (ECON §2.1). `WAD` = 10¹⁸. `PodU128` / `PodI128` are 16-byte little-endian wrappers with alignment 1 (§2.3).

## 0. Summary

**What gets built (MVP).** One Anchor 1.2.0 program (`shortwin`), a `no_std` math crate and a `no_std` venue-state crate that the program, the Rust keeper and the WASM frontend all share (until pump-final P6 also a tiny stateless helper program, `complete-curve`, used only by straddle bundles; retired, owner decision D2, A66). Venues (D1, D2; SPEC §3):

| Venue kind | Used for | Adapter (CPI) | SPEC tier |
|---|---|---|---|
| `PumpCurve` | pump.fun coins on the live bonding curve (★1.0.1: not a live cashback coin, D1 (a)) | `sell_v2` / `buy_v2` to 1.0.0; ★since 1.0.1 (pump-final) `sell_v3` / `buy_v3`, an exit past `rT` completing the curve by pump's synthetic migration | D |
| `PumpMigrating` | completed curve, canonical pool not yet created | none: exits pause, S3 after the migration pause (★1.0.1: FV on the pool `migrate_v2` creates, ρ-scaled after a synthetic pool part, §4.5) | D |
| `PumpSwap` | pump.fun graduates on their canonical pool (D1) | `sell` / `buy` (exact base out) | A / B / C |
| `RaydiumV4` | tokens whose adopted SOL pool is Raydium AMM v4 (D2) | `swap_base_in_v2` / `swap_base_out_v2` (tags 16 / 17) | A / B / C |
| `RaydiumCpmm` | tokens whose adopted SOL pool is Raydium CPMM (D2) | `swap_base_input` / `swap_base_output` | A / B / C |
| `None` (list-only) | no eligible constant-product SOL pool: tokens only on Orca Whirlpools, Meteora DLMM or Raydium CLMM, tokens with no pool, ineligible pools | none: deposits and withdrawals only | — |

Jupiter is a v1.1 price-improvement path, bounded by the on-chain pool quote (D1, ADOPTED Q20).

**Key structural choices.**

1. **One external signer per market.** A system-owned, zero-data `trader` PDA is the only key the program ever signs with towards a venue. The program never forwards a user's signature to a venue; the straddle's curve completion therefore lives in a separate helper program (§5.4).
   - Lender tokens sit in a PDA-addressed `pool_vault` whose authority is the `market` PDA. Position SOL sits on the `ShortPosition` account itself. Lender SOL, the lender pot and protocol fees sit on `MarketVault`.
   - Anyone can donate to the trader or create accounts for it. Every venue leg therefore **normalises** trader state first and measures against the post-normalisation baseline (§2.4).
2. **Pricing uses exact on-chain venue math.** All four venues are constant-product pools. Their quotes are reproduced to the raw unit against mainnet trades [R-PUMP §4.1; R-VEN §2.4; R-RAY §3.4]. CR, caps, tiers, S1/S2 and fair value use that math on live reserves and on EMA reserves. A keeper or frontend quote is never trusted.
3. **Manipulation resistance comes from the observation layer, not from the venue** (ECON §5): per-second observation buckets with directional aggregation, a one-second lag, an 8-entry EMA ring whose entries cache their reprojected reserves, liquidation persistence on the newest ring entries, a fixed 2 % bound over a manipulation-resistant reference on every keeper-initiated buyback — a liquidation reserves nothing below it, so it never waits while the buyback fits (ECON §8.2) — and **one rule for every settlement decision**: the decision must come out the same on the box spanned by the EMA state and the medians of the ring's bucket lows and highs, which only 5 attacker-only seconds of 8 can move (v0.4.1; ECON §5.6).
4. **Venue state machine per market:** `None ⇄ {PumpCurve → PumpMigrating → PumpSwap}` for pump coins, `None ⇄ {RaydiumV4 ⇄ RaydiumCpmm}` for Raydium tokens. Pump pools are derived from the mint; Raydium pools are adopted by a permissionless rule that changes a pool with open positions only when it fails (§2.6).
5. **Rent is O(1)** with three per-market basis indices; each position's rate curve and protocol share are locked at open (§4.5).
6. **Lender SOL is live and bounded** (ECON §9.4): continuous entitlement, claims from each lender's realised allocation plus a pot capped at its own deficit, lumps (and the premium of a settlement's take over market value: S2/S3, and S1 since ★AIR-21) vested over 6 h with a value-weighted end, locks that expire with the positions they stand for — S3 tail included — and stop counting for every lender at that moment, through a day-bucket calendar (v0.4.1).
7. **Admin powers**: timelocked parameters inside compiled bounds, proposals gated by the ECON liveness battery; a no-timelock Emergency multisig that can pause opens, disable a venue for opens, flag a route as broken (S3 evidence only) and publish bounded trailing-account templates for venue CPIs (both gated by owner item O6). No instruction lets any admin move pool or position funds, and venue program IDs cannot be changed without a program upgrade (SPEC §9–§11; C0-8).
8. **Venue guard (ADOPTED Q13).** New opens are refused once a venue program the market uses has been upgraded and not yet re-validated. A permissionless latch records the upgrade (§3.1). Exits never check it.
9. **Keepers are an operating cost with a visible failure mode.** The in-house keeper observes near thresholds every second, batches cranks, and when it cannot cover a market that market's opens pause and the program emits `CoverageGap` (§7.1; ECON §5.8).

**Verified today.** Venue deploy slots are unchanged at slot 450,944,934 (re-checked for v0.4.1), including Raydium AMM v4 (445,763,204) and CPMM (445,763,504) [V9]. The per-writable-account block limit is **40 M CU** on mainnet: Agave's `MAX_WRITABLE_ACCOUNT_UNITS` (24 M) scaled ×100/60 under `raise_block_limits_to_100m`, active since slot 435,888,000, in Agave master and Firedancer alike (★M10 re-check; v0.4.1 read the bare 24 M constant) [V10]. ★M10 re-read (2026-10-03): Raydium CPMM was redeployed at 452,376,460, Jupiter at 451,957,263, and pump, PumpSwap and pump-fees at 452,654,932 / 452,654,882 / 452,655,002 (2026-10-02, after the M10 fixtures were dumped) [V21]. In the pinned pump IDLs, `claim_cashback` needs no signature from the user, and PumpSwap puts no ATA constraint on the user's token accounts [V11]. Token-2022, like p-token, clears a delegate when its allowance reaches zero [V12]. The math crate's primitives were measured on SBF v3 with platform-tools v1.57 (for example a u128 `mul_div` costs ≈ 690 CU and its 256-bit fallback ≈ 780 CU) [V18]; Agave charges 946 CU per CPI and 1,500 CU per PDA derivation [V19]; `align_of::<u128>()` is 8 on sbpfv3 and 16 on x86_64 and wasm32 [V20].

## 2. Program design

### 2.1 Module structure and responsibilities

| Module | Responsibility | Depends on |
|---|---|---|
| `state/*` | Account structs (§2.3), sizes, PDA seeds, `PodU128`/`PodI128`, compile-time layout assertions (A67) | — |
| `constants.rs` | Compile-time venue program IDs, static venue PDAs and authorities, WSOL, `T_CLAMP`, `EMA_TAU_S`, `RING_LEN`, `S3_OBS_GAP_S`, `COVERAGE_GAP_S`, `P_ACC_MAX`, `P_OPEN_MAX`, the compiled parameter bounds of §2.3.3 (C0-8) | — |
| `engine/prologue.rs` | Shared market prologue (§3.0): params-version sync → accrue (vest release, rent) → observation roll → venue sync → observation record → route chains | math, venue-state |
| `engine/observe.rs` | Observation buckets, EMA integration (and, PROPOSED since M4R, its post-change warm-up branch and reference-guard check), ring push with the cached reprojection, ring rewrite on venue change, `CoverageGap` (ECON §5) | math |
| `engine/settle.rs` | Settlement box, S1/S2/refutation/not-liquidatable predicates, arming state machine, amount check (§3.8; ECON §5.6) | math |
| `engine/bounds.rs` | Exit reference prices and liquidity (M4R: `ref_liquidity` with the post-change guard; M4F-1: `ref_depth_cap`, the cap `⌊pool_d·10⁴/λ_min⌋` on its EMA terms, Raydium's `λ_min` = `pool_lock_min_bps`, PumpSwap's 100 % — `VenueKind::lock_min_bps`, row 57, M6E-1), fixed δ, `max_in` (liquidation: no reserve; expiry: rent and the expiry fee senior; v0.4.1, §3.6, §3.7) (ECON §8.2) | math |
| `engine/route.rs` | Per-venue `venue_executable`; `s3_no_route` and the S3 chain; `pool_fail` and the fast-path chain (§5.3) | venue-state |
| `engine/guard.rs` | Pause flags (incl. coverage pause), `VenueGuard` latch, venue fee caps, mint guard (entry/exit), account denylist | mint_filter |
| `engine/trader.rs` | Trader normalisation, ephemeral WSOL account lifecycle, grief-proof PDA creation (§2.4) | lamports |
| `engine/pool_select.rs` | Raydium pool selection (§2.6): what a proposal does (`decide`), the collection window and its arming rule, the adoption, its ring rewrite to the anchor and the restart of the observation state (`adopt`; M4R, PROPOSED); the candidate's verification and `eligible()` are the Raydium adapters' (`venues::raydium::check_eligible`), `D`, the floor and the margins the math crate's (M4) | math, venue-state |
| `engine/lender.rs` | Lender pool: touch, epochs, pro-rata allowance and locks, pot, vesting, realised claims (ECON §9) | math |
| `engine/caps.rs`, `engine/tier.rs`, `engine/waterfall.rs` | SPEC §4 caps and tiers (#99, row 49: also the carried-position fit of a window's candidate, `caps::carried_fit` on the `X₀` an open on it would have right after the adoption, §2.6 rule 3, §4.6; #100, row 50: its fee-scaled caps at `caps::carried_phi(min_open_fee_ppm, φ_cand)`, and `waterfall::add_position` / `remove_position` keep `min_open_fee_ppm` with `max_q_hwm`); applies pure `math::waterfall` results as lamport/token moves | math, lamports |
| `venues/mod.rs` | `VenueKind`, per-venue `ReadSet` / `TradeExtras` parsers (strict, all mandatory), bounded extras (§3.0), `VenueState` | venue-state |
| `venues/pump_curve.rs`, `venues/pump_amm.rs` | Pump `sell_v2`/`buy_v2` (★`sell_v3`/`buy_v3` since 1.0.1); PumpSwap `sell`/`buy` | engine/trader |
| `venues/raydium_v4.rs`, `venues/raydium_cpmm.rs` | AMM v4 tags 16/17; CPMM `swap_base_input`/`swap_base_output` | engine/trader |
| `venues/jupiter.rs` | v1.1: hardened route wrapper [R-JUP §7.2] | — |
| `mint_filter.rs` | Allowlist filter [R-MINT §9.2] | anchor-spl token_2022 interface |
| `lamports.rs` | `move_lamports(from_program_owned, to, amount)` with checked math and a rent-floor assertion on `from` | — |

The program never uses `pump-rust-client` [R-TOOL §1.4] or any Raydium SDK crate. CPIs are built by hand as `Instruction { program_id, accounts, data }` with discriminators from the vendored IDLs (pump, PumpSwap, CPMM) or the one-byte tags of AMM v4 [R-PUMP §3; R-VEN §2.1; R-RAY §3.1–3.2]. `declare_program!` may generate discriminator constants, but its account types are never used to decode state (A31).

### 2.2 Numeric conventions (shortwin-math)

**Normative: ECON §2.1** (the numerics table: type, scale, rounding and order of operations for every quantity the sims compute) and ECON §2.2 (where 256-bit intermediates are needed). Rounding always favours the pool and lenders: quotes, fees, rent, penalties, margin, FV and locks up; shares, payouts, credits and claims down. This section adds only the implementation rules (A30 as amended by A68, R3B-3, decision 8):

- **`mul_div` takes the u128 path whenever `a.checked_mul(b)` succeeds**; only then does it build a 256-bit product and divide by limbs (Knuth's Algorithm D on 64-bit digits). A bit-by-bit 256-bit divider is forbidden. `shortwin-math` already does both [V18].
- **256-bit intermediates only where ECON §2.2 says a product can exceed 2¹²⁸**: the rent products `Q·coef·ΔJ`, `A_j·δJ_j`, `Q·P_ema·r·T_min`; share and accumulator products `a·(S + VS)`, `s·(T + B + VA)`, `shares·Δacc`, `lock·Π`; and, as a fallback only, σ's `Q·P` and the κ/g products at prices above ≈ 2·10³⁴, σ's numerator `n·WAD·10⁴` above `n ≈ 3.4·10¹⁶` lamports, the impact caps' `X²·(10⁴ + ι)` above `X ≈ 1.8·10¹⁷` (their square root stays u128) and the tier threshold's comparison (§4.7). Quotes (`Q·Y < 1.1·10³⁷`), `reprice`, fees, CR, the fee-scaled caps, FV, the EMA and the box check fit u128.
- **Square roots are u128 only.** `L = isqrt(X·Y)` with `X·Y < 2¹²⁸` (ECON §2.2 bounds); `reprice` uses the ceiling root `isqrt⁺(P)` with `X = ⌊L·10⁹/sp⌋`, `Y = ⌈L·sp/10⁹⌉`, so `Y/X ≥ P` and every reprojected quote is an upper bound (R3B-7 c). There is no U256 square root on-chain.
- **Division is what costs CU on SBF, not width.** Measured on sbpfv3 [V18]: a u128 `mul_div` ≈ 690 CU, its Knuth-D 256-bit fallback ≈ 780 CU, the crate's `mul_div_u64` ≈ 270 CU, a native u64 multiply-and-divide ≈ 75 CU. M0b may add a bit-identical u64 fast path (taken when the product fits u64) for fee components and splits; it changes no result.
- **Ring medians** (v0.4.1): the **lower** median of the ring's 8 bucket lows `lo` (`llo`) — the 4th smallest, index `⌊(n − 1)/2⌋` of the sorted values — and the **upper** median of the 8 bucket highs `hi` (`lhi`), index `⌊n/2⌋` (ECON §2.1).
- **Price clamps** (ECON §2.2): rent accrual uses `P̃ = min(P_ema, P_ACC_MAX)` with `P_ACC_MAX = 10²⁹`, which keeps the `J` indices below 2¹²⁸ for 100 years; opens are refused while `P_ema > P_OPEN_MAX = 10²⁷`.
- **Order of operations inside one instruction** (ECON §2.1; §3.0): rent accrues on `P_ema` **before** this instruction's roll; the completed bucket is then integrated; the instruction's own pre-trade observation is recorded; the body reads the **post-roll** EMA state, including the D4 margin's EMA leg, which quotes on the newest ring entry's cached `(x, y)` (R3A-12).
- Every function is `pub fn … -> Result<T, MathError>` (quotes: `Option`) with checked arithmetic. `#![deny(clippy::arithmetic_side_effects, clippy::cast_possible_truncation, clippy::cast_sign_loss, clippy::unwrap_used)]` [R-TOOL §5.1]. ★The program additionally denies `clippy::expect_used`, `clippy::panic` and `unsafe_code` (AUD-10, M10; so did the `complete_curve` helper until 1.0.0); `unsafe_code` does not fire inside Anchor's or `security_txt!`'s external macro expansions, and test modules allow them where they use them, as they allow `unwrap_used`.
- **Math types are not account layouts.** The crate's structs (`Ema`, `Ring`, `RingEntry`, `Bucket`, `Pool`, `Lender`) hold native `u128`/`i128`. The program converts to and from its zero-copy layouts (`PodU128`, §2.3) at load and store and never casts account bytes to a math type (R3B-4).
- **Normative references** (R3A-3): the ECON v0.4.1 formulas; `sim/pool_model.py` v0.4.1 for lender accounting; `sim/shortwin_sim.py` v0.4.1 for quotes, observation, exit bounds, settlement and waterfalls; `shortwin_sim.validate_params()` for the parameter checks. v0.4 removed every known deviation of the sims from the program's formulas (ECON "Sim deviations of v0.3, all fixed") and v0.4.1 the last one found (the S2/S3 lump, R4A-5), so the differential suites (§8.1) run **without tolerance or exception**. The sims' analysis-only switches (`box_obs`, `pprime_raw`, `ref_cap_lo = False`, `liq_reserve ≠ "none"`, …) exist only for comparison rows; vectors are generated with the defaults.

### 2.3 Accounts

All PDAs are under the short.win program id. Bumps are stored and re-used with `create_program_address`; `find_program_address` is never called on hot paths. **As built (M5; row 54):** the venue-side keys a trade checks are cached or tabled rather than derived — the curve's `ATA(trader, WSOL)` and pump's pool authority are `Market` fields written at listing (§2.3.4, M5-SEC-6), the fee and buyback recipients' WSOL ATAs come from a 16-entry table of pump's live recipients (`pump_curve::RECIPIENT_WSOL_ATAS`, slot 451,675,432; a recipient pump adds later is derived as a fallback, §3.12), and the creator vault and its ATA are re-derived only when the curve's creator changed (R-PUMP §8). Two derivations remain per open, borrower-grindable and paid by the borrower itself: Anchor derives the `ShortPosition` and `WalletExposure` PDAs by search in `open_short` (§3.4 names a client-passed bump; not built). Pump's own mint-dependent derivations on every v2 trade are outside short.win's control (§6.1, O17).

**Zero-copy layout rule (A67; R3B-4).** `align_of::<u128>()` is 8 on sbpfv3 but 16 on x86_64 (rustc ≥ 1.77) and on wasm32 [V20], so a `#[repr(C)]` struct with raw 128-bit fields has different padding, size and offsets on the program, the keeper and the WASM frontend (v0.3's 88-byte `RingEntry` is 96 bytes on the host). Every zero-copy account (`GlobalConfig`, `VenueGuard`, `VenueExtras`, `Market`, and since v0.4.1 `MarketVault`) and every type nested in one therefore:

- stores 128-bit values as `PodU128` / `PodI128`: `#[repr(transparent)]` newtypes over `[u8; 16]` (little-endian, alignment 1, `bytemuck::{Pod, Zeroable}` through Anchor's re-export, `get()` / `set()`), declared in `state/pod.rs` so that the IDL — and hence Codama and `declare_program!` — describes them as 16-byte arrays; no raw `u128`/`i128` field is allowed (CI lint over `state/`);
- has every field at an offset that is a multiple of its alignment (≤ 8) **with all padding written out** as `_padN: [u8; k]`, and a size that is a multiple of 8;
- carries compile-time assertions of `size_of` and of every field's `offset_of!` in `state/layout_asserts.rs`, compiled for sbpfv3 (`anchor build`), x86_64 (`cargo test`) and wasm32 (the WASM build). A difference fails the build on the target that differs (T-LAYOUT).

Borsh accounts (`ShortPosition`, `LenderPosition`, `ShareEpoch`, `WalletExposure`, `OracleCache`) serialise 128-bit values as 16 little-endian bytes with no alignment, so the rule does not apply to them.

#### 2.3.1 Overview

Sizes include the 8-byte discriminator. Rent-exempt minimum = `(len + 128)·5,080` lamports [V5].

Raydium markets need no trader ATA, no UVA and no venue-side accounts at all [R-RAY §4.1].

**A4: vault topology.** SPEC §10 names a "pool vault (tokens)", a "pool SOL vault" and "vault SOL" per position:

- **Position SOL = extra lamports on the `ShortPosition` account.** Invariant `lamports ≥ rent_min(len) + position.v`. The program owns the account and debits it directly, with no CPI. It is never passed to an external program.
- **Lender SOL + protocol fees = `MarketVault` lamports.** Invariant `lamports ≥ rent_min + vault.lender_sol + vault.protocol_fees`. The pot `unmatched` and the unreleased vest `vest_bal` are parts of `lender_sol`, not extra lamports. Protocol fees accrue per market and are swept by a permissionless instruction (A9).
- **Pool tokens = PDA-addressed token account** (`["pool_vault", market]`), not an ATA: a pre-created ATA would permanently block `init` [R-MINT §8.2].

#### 2.3.2 `GlobalConfig`, `VenueGuard`, `VenueExtras` (zero-copy)

`GlobalConfig`:

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `version` | u16 | Layout version |
| `bump` | u8 | |
| `flags` | u8 | bit0 `paused_opens_global` |
| `venue_enabled` | u32 bitmask | bit0 pump curve, bit1 PumpSwap, bit2 Raydium AMM v4, bit3 Raydium CPMM, bit4 Jupiter (v1.1). Enabling is timelocked; disabling is immediate (`disable_venue`) and affects opens only, and it cancels a pending `EnableVenues` change that would set the bit again (AIR-24: `apply_config` is permissionless, so such a change otherwise undid the disable once its `not_before` passed; the whole change is cancelled, `ConfigCancelled`, and Governance proposes the other bits again). **Enableable set (M5-SEC-4, a hard gate; row 54):** a build may hold venue bits it cannot let Governance enable, `constants::VENUE_BITS_UNFINISHED` — a venue whose markets it can open positions on but whose lifecycle it cannot finish; `initialize_config` and `EnableVenues` (propose and apply) refuse them (`InvalidParams`), so every open on such a venue fails `VenueDisabled` while listing, lending and cranking stay available. In the M5 build the set is the pump-curve bit (without the `→ PumpSwap` transition a migrated curve market stayed `PumpMigrating` for good, §2.5, §5.4); **M6 emptied it** with that transition (as built: `VENUE_BITS_UNFINISHED = 0`, every known bit enableable; the mechanism stays for a later unfinished venue; row 55) |
| `venue_route_broken` | u32 bitmask | Same bits. Set/cleared by Emergency (`set_route_broken`, O6). Refuses opens and is S3 evidence (`s3_no_route`, §5.3). Never an input to a quote, a leg, an exit or `pool_fail` (A40, V2-1, V1-7) |
| `timelock_s` | u32 | Default 172,800. Compiled bounds `MIN_TIMELOCK_S = 86,400` ≤ `timelock_s` ≤ `MAX_TIMELOCK_S = 2,592,000` (30 d; the ceiling keeps a unit slip or a hostile `Timelock` change from freezing every later change, key rotations included; M1-SEC-4) (A8) |
| `governance` | Pubkey | Squads Governance vault (48 h Squads time_lock) [R-TOOL §5.3]. ★Owner layout (Q4, 2026-10-02): the **vault 0** of an autonomous Squads v4 **3-of-5** multisig with `time_lock` 172,800 s, which also holds both programs' **upgrade authority** |
| `pause_authority` | Pubkey | Squads Emergency vault (time_lock 0). ★Owner layout: the vault 0 of an autonomous **2-of-4** multisig, `time_lock` 0 |
| `coverage_authority` ★ | Pubkey | Keeper-held key that can only set/clear a market's `paused_coverage` flag (degraded mode, A69). `Pubkey::default()` = disabled, the default until the owner decides O17; set through a timelocked `Authorities` change. ★Owner layout: a separate hot key on the keeper's designated pauser (§7.1), installed at `initialize_config` or by an `Authorities` change |
| `fee_recipient` | Pubkey | Destination of `sweep_protocol_fees`. ★Owner layout: the Governance multisig's **vault 1** (a System account, pre-funded to its rent-exempt minimum) |

**★Authority layout and SQ-G8 (owner decision Q4, 2026-10-02; M10 WP-6 batch 2, WP-7).** `governance`, `pause_authority`, `fee_recipient` and an installed `coverage_authority` must be **pairwise distinct** (`config::check_authorities`, `AuthoritiesNotDistinct` = 6105; an unset `coverage_authority` is no key and is skipped), so one key never holds two roles: the Emergency 2-of-4 can never act as the timelocked 3-of-5, nor the keeper's hot key as either. Checked by `initialize_config` and, for an `Authorities` change, at `propose_config` (early refusal) and again at `apply_config` (§3.1). A parameter change therefore takes **96 h** end to end: 48 h of Squads `time_lock` from the threshold approval, then 48 h of `timelock_s` (T-SQ-2). The multisigs themselves are created on mainnet in M11 (they need the owner's member keys); `squads_gov_it` builds this exact layout on the dumped Squads ELF (§8.2) and `shortwin-gov` stages and verifies it (§7.4, §8.5).

Venue program IDs, their static PDAs (pump `global` `4wTV1Ymi…`, `event_authority` `Ce6TQqeH…`, GVA `Hq2wp8uJ…`, fee config `8Wf5TiAh…`; pAMM `global_config` `ADyA8hde…`, `event_authority` `GS4CU59F…`, GVA `C2aFPdEN…`, fee config `5PHirr8j…`; AMM v4 authority `5Q544fKrFoe6tsEbD7S8EmxGTJYAKtTVhAW5Q5pge4j1`; CPMM authority `GpMZbSM2GgvTKHJirzeGfMFoaZ8UR2X7F4v8vHTvxFbL`; the ProgramData addresses) and the Pyth receiver id are **compile-time constants** in `constants.rs`, verified by a unit test that re-derives each PDA. No config path can change them; only an audited program upgrade can (C0-8) [R-PUMP §3.1; R-VEN §1.1; R-RAY §1.1].

Only governance writes after a timelock; Emergency writes the flags (and `VenueExtras`, `VenueGuard` through `revalidate_venue`). `GlobalConfig` is **never written on a hot path or by a permissionless instruction**, and it is read (zero-copy `load()`) by every instruction.

**`VenueGuard` (A7; decision 4; hardened in v0.4.1, R4B-7).** `version` u16, `bump` u8, `_pad0` u8, `upgraded` u32 (one bit per venue program: pump, pAMM, pfee, AMM v4, CPMM, Jupiter), `guard_slot [u64;6]` (last validated ProgramData deploy slot; validated 2026-09-27 as 449,734,335 / 446,462,733 / 446,465,969 / 445,763,204 / 445,763,504 / 449,280,566 [V9], `constants::VENUE_GUARD_SLOTS_2026_09_27`; ★M10: CPMM was redeployed at 452,376,460 and Jupiter at 451,957,263, `VENUE_GUARD_SLOTS_2026_10_02`, the newest test and `dump-fixtures.py check --live` baseline — the tests run CPMM on the 452,376,460 ELF, `fork::FIXTURE_GUARD_SLOTS`; on 2026-10-03 pump, pAMM and pfee had moved again, to 452,654,932 / 452,654,882 / 452,655,002 [V21]; `initialize_config` takes the live slots as arguments, so no constant is ever written on chain), `flagged_slot [u64;6]` (the latest deploy slot seen while flagged), `flagged_at [i64;6]`, ★AIR-01 `guard_len [u32;4]` @160 and `guard_elf [[u8;12];4]` @176 (from `_reserved [u8;64]`; one slot each for pump-fees, AMM v4, CPMM and Jupiter, the venues whose ProgramData can still grow: the ProgramData's data length at the last revalidation with a hash, and the first 12 bytes of the sha256 of the reviewed trimmed ELF; `guard_len = 0` means no fingerprint) = 224 B. The permissionless `flag_venue_upgraded` sets a bit when a ProgramData deploy slot differs from `guard_slot` **and the change is an upgrade**, and — while the bit is set — refreshes `flagged_slot` / `flagged_at` whenever the deploy slot changes again (a second upgrade during review is visible; the program cannot tell an extension of the unreviewed ELF from another upgrade there). **An extension is not an upgrade (AIR-01).** The loader's `ExtendProgram` is permissionless (Agave 4.2): it appends zeros, keeps the ELF and moves the deploy slot, so the slot alone let anyone latch a venue for ≈ 0.052 SOL of rent a time (10 KiB at mainnet's 5,080 lamports/byte; the loader charges only the shortfall below rent exemption, so on AMM v4, whose dumped ProgramData holds ≈ 1.76 SOL above it, the first ≈ 34 extensions cost only the fee). With a fingerprint recorded, a moved slot latches only if the ProgramData kept the recorded length (`Upgrade` never resizes it; `ExtendProgram` always grows it) or if its trimmed ELF (`shortwin_venue_state::program_data::trimmed_elf`) no longer hashes to the fingerprint (a trimmed ELF above 2 MiB is not hashed and counts as an upgrade, fail-safe); a grown account with the same ELF fails `VenueNotUpgraded`. Without a fingerprint — pump and PumpSwap, whose ProgramData sit at the loader's 10 MiB cap so that only `Upgrade` moves their slot, and every venue until its first revalidation with a hash — the slot alone decides. Emergency `revalidate_venue(venue, expected_slot, expected_elf_hash)` requires the ProgramData's current deploy slot to equal `expected_slot`, the slot its reviewers validated — or, for a fingerprinted venue and a non-zero hash, its current trimmed ELF to hash to `expected_elf_hash` (the reviewed deploy, only extended since; the sha256 `solana-verify get-program-hash` prints) — then records the current slot as `guard_slot`, records the fingerprint (cleared without a hash; with the slot unchanged the hash is recorded as given, unchecked, so a wrong one can only make a later extension count as an upgrade) and clears the bit, so an upgrade that lands between review and execution cannot be validated silently and an extension cannot make the revalidation fail. After `initialize_config` one revalidation with a hash per fingerprinted venue records its fingerprint; until then one extension can still latch it (operations; `shortwin-ops revalidate-venue` prints and stages the hash). `open_short` reads the account and refuses while a bit of its venue's **mask** is set: `PumpCurve` = pump + pfee + **pAMM** (a curve position exits on PumpSwap after graduation), `PumpSwap` = pAMM + pfee, `RaydiumV4` and `RaydiumCpmm` = **both** Raydium programs (the fast path can move a market between them). A Raydium listing (`create_market` with a hint) waits for the same combined mask (M3-SEC-2). **Pool selection latches on the candidate's own program only** (M4-SEC-8, `guard::candidate_latch`): `propose_pool` refuses a candidate while the bit of *its* program is set, since that program's compiled reader verifies it, and `execute_pool_switch` treats such a window candidate as not adoptable now and cancels the window (`guard::candidate_latched`; M4V-4: a revert kept the window and froze every other proposal until the review); an upgrade of the other Raydium program — typically the incumbent's, whose pools then fail `pool_fail` — does not hold the fast path up, and a cancellation is not latched. It is kept out of `GlobalConfig` so that a permissionless writer never write-locks the account every instruction reads (the lesson of V1-11).

**`VenueExtras` (A41, V2-6; gated by O6; `stable` since M2-SEC-2).** Per venue: for each instruction kind (sell, buy, claim) three sets — `current`, `previous` and `stable` — of up to 4 entries, a `version` per set, and the time `current` was written. An entry is either a fixed key or a **derivation template** `{program: Pubkey, seeds: [SeedPart; ≤ 4], writable: bool}` where a `SeedPart` is constant bytes (≤ 32) or a placeholder among `{mint, pool, trader, bonding_curve, coin_creator}`; the caller passes each derived account plus its bump, and the parser re-derives it with `create_program_address` and accepts only the **canonical** bump — every higher bump must fail to derive (M2-SEC-3: otherwise a caller, such as the keeper on `liquidate` / `expire` whose venue CPI spends the borrower's SOL, could pass a second, non-canonical PDA of the template's program; no `find_program_address` search, only the bumps above the caller's, 0–2 extra derivations in practice). `set_venue_extras` moves `current` to `previous` and writes the new set; callers choose `none`, `current`, `previous` or `stable` in the instruction data (§3.0), so one hostile or wrong Emergency write can never brick exits. **`stable`** (M2-SEC-2): `previous` survives one write only, so two quick writes by a compromised or twice-mistaken Emergency key could push a working set out of both, and a venue that requires its new trailing accounts would refuse every exit until Governance re-published the set. Only two things write `stable`: a write that displaces a `current` which has stood for at least `EXTRAS_STABLE_S` (7 d, §2.3.3) first copies it into `stable`, and a **Governance** write also pins its new set as `stable` (the slow, reviewed path ratifies an Emergency publication at once). The Emergency key can displace `stable` only by keeping a set of its own `current`, unchallenged, for 7 days — longer than Governance needs to re-publish the working set or to rotate the Emergency key through a timelocked `Authorities` change. Layout as built (M1, grown by M2-SEC-2; T-LAYOUT; M1-FID-13; layout `version` 2): `version` u16, `bump` u8, `venue` u8, `_pad0 [u8;4]`, `sets [IxExtras;3]` (sell, buy, claim), `_reserved [u8;64]` = **6,512 B** (rent 33,731,200 lamports each, four accounts; 4,352 B in M1); `IxExtras` = `{current, previous, stable}` `ExtrasSet`, `current_since` i64 (unix s when `current` was written; 0 = never) (2,144 B); `ExtrasSet` = `version` u32, `count` u8, `_pad [u8;3]`, `entries [ExtraEntry;4]` (712 B); `ExtraEntry` = `kind` u8 (none / fixed / template), `writable` u8, `n_seeds` u8, `_pad [u8;5]`, `key` Pubkey (the fixed key or the template's program), `seeds [SeedPart;4]` (176 B); `SeedPart` = `kind` u8 (none / constant / placeholder), `len` u8 (constant length or placeholder id), `bytes [u8;32]` (34 B).

#### 2.3.3 Parameters (`Params`, `TierParams`)

Names, defaults and hard bounds are **identical to ECON §15**. Scope: G global; T per tier; P snapshot into each position at open; M market-level (a market adopts a new value while it has no open position; the EMA fields also after `ema_force_delay_s`, A59; the kink has its own version); C compile-time constant. `validate_params()` rejects any value outside its hard bounds and checks the relational bounds below the table (A8). **One source of truth:** on every parameter `shortwin_sim` models it is the same function as `shortwin_sim.validate_params()` — `shortwin_math::params::validate`, which accepts exactly what the sim accepts (T-CONFIG), including the penalty split's parts and every per-tier bound — and the bounds of the parameters the sim does not model (`min_notional`, `market_max_notional`, `market_creation_fee`, `boost_dust_lamports`, `boost_window_s`, `market_warmup_s`, `ema_force_delay_s`, `lump_vest_s`, `lock_grace_s`, `theta_A` / `theta_B`, the four oracle limits, `pool_min_real_sol`, `pool_switch_margin_bps`, `pool_list_window_s`, `pool_list_margin_bps`, `pool_fast_min_bps`) are `params::validate_econ`, transcribed from ECON §15; the program runs both (§3.1). Every `Params` / `TierParams` / `EmaParams` proposal must also pass `sim/config_check.py` (the ECON §5.7 liveness battery, 1,655 runs since v0.4.1) before governance signs it (A73; R3B-6, R4A-4). **Bold** = changed in v0.4 or v0.4.1. **Since 2026-10-09** (the owner's eleventh round; O18, §10; SPEC §14) the PROPOSED parameters and constants of this table, those tagged "owner item O18" among them, are adopted as the v1.0.0 design; the tags are left as written. **Removed in v0.4** (ECON §15): `ema_tau_s` as a parameter, `delta_liq_min_bps`, `delta_liq_slope_bps`, `delta_liq_max_bps`, `liq_persist_s`, `settle_persist_s`, `fv_liq`, `settle_s2_first`, `margin_ema_own_sale`, `pool_switch_delay_s`, and the ARCH-only `venue_sync_max_age_slots`.

**Relational checks in `validate_params()`** (= ECON §15; v0.4 additions marked ★, v0.4.1 ★★; `market_warmup_s ≥ 10·EMA_TAU_S` and `theta_B < theta_A` involve parameters the sim does not model and are `params::validate_econ`'s, every other one is `params::validate`'s):

- `cr_open_bps ≥ cr_liq_bps + 2,000`; `cr_liq_bps ≥ 10,500`; ★★ per tier, `cr_open_bps` and `cr_liq_bps` ≥ their SPEC §4 values; `util_kink_bps ≤ util_cap_bps ≤ 9,500`; penalty split sums to 10,000;
- `market_warmup_s ≥ 10·EMA_TAU_S`; `venue_fee_cap_bps < venue_fee_hard_cap_bps`; `settle_keeper_fixed ≤ settle_keeper_cap`; `expiry_keeper_fixed ≤ expiry_keeper_cap`; `theta_B < theta_A`;
- ★ `kappa_base_bps ≤ kappa_liq_bps`; ★ `delta_liq_bps ≥ delta_exp_bps`; ★ `fee_size_cap_x100 ≤ fee_oi_cap_x100`; v0.4's `liq_persist_n + kappa_growth_n ≤ 7` is implied by the v0.4.1 bounds and dropped;
- ★ `pool_fast_route_s + pool_fast_window_s ≤ 540`, checked against the **compiled minimum** of `s3_wait_s` (600) minus `S3_OBS_GAP_S`, so no position — whatever `s3_wait_s` it snapshot — reaches S3 before the fast path can complete (R3A-11 b);
- `RING_LEN ≥ max(liq_persist_n, kappa_growth_n + 1)` (holds for every compiled value; asserted at compile time).

**What "simulated-safe" covers (v0.4.1, R4A-4).** The ECON §5.7 battery has 1,655 runs: the 65 core rows, the same rows with ±0.3 % and ±1 % per-second price noise (3 seeds each), the reviewer's 960-cell genuine-pump grid and 240 aged-position runs. Every corner of the core box (κ, persistence, growth window, `dt_max`, clamp, bucket age, δ: 128 configurations that pass the relational checks) passes all of it; every other parameter with a liveness effect passes at each of its compiled extremes alone (the scan; sizing parameters compared at equal position size), except those whose only effect is lower lender income (penalty, expiry fee, rates), which the gate reports as warnings for the owner; and a stress corner with every scanned parameter at its adverse extreme together passes. Combinations beyond the core box are not enumerated. Governance can move a value only inside the bounds; the fuzz harness proposes adversarial in-bound configs (§8.4).

| **locked execution and settlement terms** | `exec_tol_bps` u16 (the expiry bound's ε, v0.4.1); `ert` u64 (effective: 0 on Raydium); `ref_max_age_s` u8; `fv_dev_bps` u16; `venue_fee_hard_cap_bps` u16; `s3_wait_s`, `grad_grace_s`, `max_migration_pause_s` u32 | 27 | V1-5; v0.4 removals: `fv_liq`, `settle_s2_first`; the three timers also feed `Market.max_release` at open (v0.4.1) |
| **settlement arming state** | `s_armed` u8 (0/1); `s_count` u64 (`ema_count` at arm); `s_since`, `s_last` i64 | 25 | One clock for S1 and S2; §3.8 |
| `_reserved` | `[u8;32]` | 32 | Room for the O1/O2 terms if the owner ever signs them off (they are not built, R3A-8 c) |

Rent-exempt minimum 2,600,960 lamports. **A26: what "locked at open" covers, and what governance can still affect (V1-5; amended R3A-4, R3A-5).** Everything in the four **locked** groups plus `deadline` and `r_min` never changes for the life of the position; the rent rate **and the protocol's share of it** are locked exactly through the basis indices and `A_j` (§4.5). What a timelocked governance change can still reach while a position is open, always inside compiled bounds:

- **market-level observation parameters** (`ema_dtmax_s`, `ema_clamp_bps`, `liq_slow_*`): adopted when the market has no open position, or after `ema_force_delay_s` (≥ 1 day, default 7 days); their compiled ranges keep a forced adoption inside the simulated-safe region (ECON §2.4). `util_kink_bps` only when the market has no open position;
- **the global `venue_fee_hard_cap_bps`** as it enters the route predicates: the S3 chain (`s3_no_route`, at `min(global, Market.min_open_hard_cap_bps)`), a position's "no route now" in `sol_settle` (at `min(global, the position's locked cap)`) and `pool_fail` (the fast path, at the global value): a change inside [300, 2,000] bps can move S3 and fast-path timing for open positions; it never changes their quotes, bounds or FV, which use the locked value (R3A-4 c), and since AIR-19 a raised global cap no longer leaves a fee above a position's own locked cap counted as a route for it (the chain runs and that position settles S3);
- **Raydium pool-selection parameters** (`pool_*`): they decide which eligible pool an open position exits on after an incumbent failure (§2.6); no exit term reads one (AIR-23: the exit reference's cap is the pool's locked depth `D` itself since AIR-14, where it read `pool_lock_min_bps` live at every liquidation and expiry);
- **Emergency flags**: the route-broken flag and the venue-extras sets, which never change a quote or an exit bound (A40, A41).

Liquidation thresholds, penalties, splits, the protocol's rent share, keeper rewards, exit bounds, persistence and arming rules, fee and tolerance ceilings, fair-value rules and S3 timing terms are all per-position (C0-8).

#### 2.3.6 `LenderPosition`, `ShareEpoch`, `MarketVault`, `WalletExposure`, `OracleCache` (Borsh)

- **`LenderPosition` (241 B)**: `owner`, `market` Pubkey; `shares` u128; `snap` i128 (acc snapshot); `pending` i64 (entitlement not yet paid; can go negative after a shortfall debit, ECON §9.4); `snap_r` u128 (acc_r snapshot); `real` u64 (cumulative realised SOL allocated to this lender, including pot draws) and `claimed` u64 (cumulative SOL paid to it) (V2-2); `epoch` u32; `lock` u128, `lock_pi` u128, `lock_epoch` u32, `lock_term` u128 (ECON §9.3); ★`lock_until` i64 (R3B-1); `bump` u8; `_reserved [u8;32]`.
- **`ShareEpoch` (127 B)** (A39): `market` Pubkey; `epoch` u32; `acc_end` i128; `acc_r_end` u128; `s_old` u128 (shares at the roll) and `carry` i128, `carry_r` u128 (top-up remainders); `num` u8 (0 or 1); `den_log1000` u8 (den = 1,000^k); `bump`. Immutable once written, except the full-wipe case of §3.3 (V2-12).
- **`MarketVault` (zero-copy, 2,200 B; v0.4 was 77 B Borsh)** (A9, C0-17; amended A70, A75): `lender_sol` u64 (ECON `sol_vault`: realised lender SOL, including the pot and the unreleased vest); ★`unmatched` u64 (the pot, R3A-2); `protocol_fees` u64; the lock state `pi` PodU128 (Π, WAD), `lock_norm` PodU128 (Σ of the live calendar buckets), `b_min` u64, `pi_epoch` u32, `bump` u8, `_pad0` [u8;3]; ★★the **lock expiry calendar** `cal_day` i64 (the oldest day not yet dropped) and `lock_cal [PodU128; 128]` (bucket `d mod 128` holds the lock terms whose `lock_until` ends day `d`); `_reserved [u8;64]`. Rent-exempt minimum 11,826,240 lamports. Its lamports are the SOL float. **Calendar (A75; R4A-2, R4B-3):** every instruction that reads or writes the lock state first runs `cal_advance(now)`: for each day `d` from `cal_day` to `⌊now/86,400⌋` (at most 128 iterations; a longer gap clears every bucket), `lock_norm −= lock_cal[d mod 128]`, `lock_cal[d mod 128] = 0`; then `cal_day = max(cal_day, ⌊now/86,400⌋ + 1)` (never backwards, should the clock go back). `lock_until` is always a day end, so a bucket leaves `lock_norm` at exactly the second its locks expire for their holders — no lender has to be touched. A Π-epoch roll clears every bucket; a rebase scales every bucket by `num/den`. ECON §9.1 lists the lock state with the market's logical state; ARCH stores it here because every instruction that changes it (withdrawals, exits, settlements, lender touches) already write-locks `MarketVault`, which lets `claim_sol`, `cover_deficit` and `sync_lender` run pool_model's full `touch` without write-locking `Market` (C0-17). v0.4.1 makes the account zero-copy because the calendar (2 KB) would cost a Borsh round trip on every claim. **The isolation is from `Market` only** (V1-6): exits, opens and lender instructions all write-lock `MarketVault`, so lender claims and liquidations still share its per-writable-account block budget (★M10: 40 M CU on mainnet, U16; v0.4.1 assumed 24 M); the mitigation is the keeper's CU and priority policy and T-CASCADE (§6.6).
- **`WalletExposure` (81 B)**: `market`, `wallet` Pubkey; `q_open` u64; `bump`.
- **`OracleCache` (45 B)**: `price` i64, `conf` u64, `expo` i32, `publish_time` i64, `updated_slot` u64, `bump` [R-VEN §5].

### 2.4 Funds, vaults and signer-authority isolation

```
                      (signs transfer_checked / approve_checked(Q) only)          (never sign; program-owned lamports)
 lender ATA ──transfer_checked──► pool_vault [authority = market PDA]            ShortPosition.lamports = rent + V
                                    │  ▲   ▲                                      MarketVault.lamports   = rent + lender_sol + protocol_fees
     pump venues: open Q out ───────┘  │   │── Raydium buy: venue delivers Q straight into pool_vault
     pump venues: exit Q in ◄──────────┘   │── Raydium sell: trader spends Q as delegate of pool_vault (approve Q, auto-cleared at 0)
                                    │
                         trader_base_ATA (pump venues only) ◄── owner = trader PDA (system-owned, 0 data, 0 lamports after every ix)
                                                                   │  ▲
         pump sell_v2 credits lamports / pump buy_v2 debits them ──┘  │── direct lamport credit from ShortPosition (budget), System sweep back
                                    trader_wsol (ephemeral, PDA address, owner = trader): PumpSwap and Raydium SOL leg,
                                    created with allocate/assign + InitializeAccount3 and closed in the same instruction
                                         VENUE PROGRAM (compile-time constant): the ONLY program that receives the trader signature
```

**Isolation rules** (A4, A33; implement [R-JUP §4.3], [R-MINT §8.5], [R-RAY §9.3]).

1. **Signers are fixed per program.**
   - The `market` PDA signs only Token `transfer_checked` out of `pool_vault` (withdraw; open leg on pump venues) and `approve_checked(pool_vault → trader, Q)` (Raydium sell leg).
   - The `trader` PDA signs only: the CPI into the market's venue program (a compile-time constant for the venue kind); System transfers of its own lamports; Token `transfer_checked` from its base ATA to `pool_vault`; `CloseAccount` of `trader_wsol` or of a stray `ATA(trader, WSOL)`; pump/PumpSwap `claim_cashback` (§3.9).
   - The `trader_wsol` PDA signs only System `transfer` (sweeping pre-funded lamports), `allocate` and `assign` of itself.
   - `ShortPosition`, `MarketVault`, `Market` and `ShareEpoch` never sign and are never passed to a venue program.
2. **Normalise before measuring** (A33; C0-3, C1-3). Anyone can credit the system-owned trader (a System transfer checks only `from`), create token accounts for it (the ATA program checks only the address), or pre-fund the `trader_wsol` address [R-PUMP §9.2; R-RAY §4.2]. At the start of every venue leg, before any funding:
   - require `trader.owner == System ∧ trader.data_len == 0` (only short.win can sign `allocate`/`assign` for it, so this cannot be griefed);
   - if `trader.lamports > 0`: System-transfer all of it to `market_vault` (trader signs) and credit it to lenders as a lump (`lender_sol += x`, `pool::sweep(x)`: it vests over `lump_vest_s`; while `S = 0` it tops up the live wipe record or goes to `protocol_fees`, §3.3); emit `TraderSwept`;
   - pump venues: if `trader_base_ata.amount > 0`: `transfer_checked` all of it to `pool_vault` (a donation; `T` is unchanged); require `owner == trader`, `delegate == None`, `close_authority == None` (only the trader could set them);
   - WSOL venues: if the `trader_wsol` address holds lamports, System-transfer them to `market_vault` (signed with the `trader_wsol` seeds) and credit lenders the same way; require `owner == System ∧ data_len == 0`;
   - `ATA(trader, WSOL)` is never used by a trading leg; if a third party creates it, `sweep_trader` (§3.9) closes it later. Pump ignores it for SOL coins [R-PUMP §6.3].

   `S` and `B` are measured against this post-normalisation baseline. Post-conditions assert **deltas and authorities**, never that an account a third party can create does not exist.
3. **Exact funding and balance-delta accounting** (A19, A48; C0-14, C1-4, C1-9). `ert` = `exec_rent_tol` on pump venues, 0 on Raydium.
   - **Buy legs**: fund the leg with `max_in + ert` (pump curve: native lamports on the trader; PumpSwap: `max_in` as WSOL in `trader_wsol` plus `ert` native on the trader; Raydium: `max_in` as WSOL in `trader_wsol`). The source is the `ShortPosition` itself (direct lamport debit, no CPI), capped at its total lamports. Rent state is checked once per transaction [V4], so briefly using the position's rent reserve is safe. After the CPI, everything left returns to the position in the same instruction.
     - `B = position.lamports_before − position.lamports_after`. Require `B ≤ max_in + ert` and `tokens_received ≥ Q` (measured on `trader_base_ata` for pump venues, on `pool_vault` for Raydium). Under-delivery reverts; **over-delivery** (a venue rounding or semantics change) is accepted: the surplus goes to `pool_vault` as a donation (`T` unchanged, I1 already tolerates it) and is emitted, so a harmless venue change cannot freeze exits (A62; V2-10).
   - **Sell legs (open)** — one baseline for both pump venues (V1-13). Pump venues fund the trader with `ert` from the borrower **before** the CPI, because `sell_v2` may top up the creator vault, the curve account and the UVA from `user`, and PumpSwap `sell` may create missing fee accounts (C1-4; T-RENT). **Measured on the curve (M5; R-PUMP Update U6, U10):** an empty creator vault is topped up to `Rent.minimum_balance(0)` = 650,240 from `user` on every buy and sell, on a sale **before** the proceeds are credited; a curve shorter than 125 B grows to 125 B on its first v2 trade and `user` tops its rent reserve up to `minimum_balance(125)` (0 on every listable curve of the M5 dump); a missing UVA (1,346,200) is taken before the proceeds too, which is why the UVA is created at listing. Which PumpSwap `sell` items debit `user` was verified in M6 (U6): a missing fee ATA is created from `user` on sells as on buys (1,488,440) and a pool under 271 B grows with its rent topped up from `user`; the existence requirement of §3.12 leaves only the growth (`pamm_it::gates::t_rent_*`). The baseline is the post-normalisation, post-funding state: trader lamports = `ert`, no `trader_wsol` balance.
     - `S = trader.lamports_after + trader_wsol.amount_after − ert` on both pump venues (curve: lamports only; PumpSwap: WSOL plus lamports). Any venue-side rent `r` the venue took from the trader is therefore netted inside `S`, and the borrower is refunded exactly `ert`. The borrower bears `r` through a smaller `S`, and hence a larger margin. On PumpSwap `r = ert − trader.lamports_after` is reported in the `Open` event; on the curve `r` cannot be separated from the proceeds.
     - The venue's own slippage argument (`min_sol_output` / `min_quote_out`) is `min_out` and applies to the venue's gross credit. short.win then requires the **net** `S ≥ min_out`, with `min_out = max(min_proceeds, ⌊S_exp·(10⁴ − ε)/10⁴⌋)`, so the borrower's `min_proceeds` bounds what is actually credited to the position.
     - Raydium: `ert = 0` and `S = trader_wsol.amount`; the borrower funds and gets back only the `trader_wsol` rent.
     - Require the pool-vault base delta to be exactly `−Q` (short.win's own transfer or approval).
4. **Account denylist.** A remaining account must never equal `config`, `venue_guard`, `market`, `market_vault`, `pool_vault` (except where the venue list names it: Raydium source/destination), any `ShortPosition`, `LenderPosition`, `ShareEpoch` or `OracleCache` (O(n) key scan). CPI metas set `is_signer = true` only for `trader` (or `swap_auth` in v1.1). Top-level signer flags are never forwarded [R-JUP T8]. Extra trailing accounts (A41) must also not be owned by short.win. ★**As built since M10 batch 3 (the owner's decision of 2026-10-03; `391aed3`):** an extra also never equals the **position's borrower** (on `open_short`, `close_short`, `liquidate` and `expire`) or the **adopted pool's own accounts** — the pool and the two accounts holding its reserves (mock / AMM v4 / CPMM: the pool and its two vaults; PumpSwap: the canonical pool and its base / quote vaults; the curve: `bonding_curve`, `curve_base_ata`, `curve_quote_ata`; `venues::pool_denylist`, read from the market's cache, no derivation), refused `DeniedAccount`. The check runs on the resolved key after a template entry is re-derived, so a template that derives one of them from the `pool` / `mint` / `bonding_curve` placeholders (an ATA of the pool or the curve, a CPMM `pool_vault` PDA; AMM v4's vaults are not derivable) is refused too. A set naming one of them could only hand the venue a second, writable copy of its own reserves, or name a wallet the keeper's exit spends for. The pool-vault exception above concerns the adapter's own list, never an extra. Callers then select the next set (§3.0; the keeper and the web fall back after `DeniedAccount`). Residuals (disclosed, §8.5; ★accepted by the owner on 2026-10-03, KI-54 … KI-57): a borrower that is itself a venue-wide fixed extra of the buy set can be keeper-exited only through another set or S3; a venue change that genuinely needs one of the pool's own accounts as a trailing account needs a program upgrade; other venue-owned accounts (fee recipients, creator vaults, the CPMM observation, the PumpSwap boost-vault ATA, LP mints, other pools) stay nameable — they arrive as non-signers, and the Emergency key cannot sign for them; a denied set costs one extra simulation per exit or trade until it is replaced (nothing pre-filters it off chain).
5. **Post-conditions at the end of every instruction that ran a leg** (invariant I7): `trader.lamports == 0`; `trader_base_ata.amount == 0` with owner/delegate/close-authority unchanged; `trader_wsol` closed (`owner == System ∧ data_len == 0 ∧ lamports == 0`) after a **WSOL** leg (PumpSwap, Raydium, the mock), which normalises the address (rule 2) and closes what it opened; after a **pump-curve** leg, which never names the address (the curve trades native lamports, §2.4.1), `trader_wsol` is untouched — `owner == System ∧ data_len == 0` and its lamports unchanged by the leg, so a third party's pre-funding there waits for `sweep_trader` (§3.9) or the first WSOL leg after the graduation (★M7, FUZZ-M7-1: the fuzzer's `[donate trader_wsol, curve open]` failed the hook's literal "closed" clause; the program was already rule 2's; the clause is a delta, as rule 2 requires of every post-condition); `pool_vault.delegate == None` [V12]; `pool_vault.amount ≥ T`; the vault lamport invariants of §2.3.1.
6. **Token movements use `transfer_checked` / `approve_checked`** through `anchor_spl::token_interface`, with `market.token_program` [R-MINT §8.3].

**Why a per-market trader** (A4): pump and PumpSwap each need a pre-created UVA per `user` (1,346,200 lamports) [R-PUMP §2.4]; the trader holds nothing at rest, so there is no cross-position exposure. The v1.1 Jupiter adapter uses a per-position `swap_auth`, because a Jupiter route passes the signature on to arbitrary AMMs.

#### 2.4.1 Leg flows per venue

Trace entries are counted per leg (C1-1): the short.win instruction itself is 1; every CPI and every CPI it makes is 1 more. Normalisation adds 0–3 entries (only when something was donated). Venue counts are measured on mainnet [R-PUMP §6.9; R-RAY §4.3].

|---|---|---|
