Every instruction adds its own `emit_cpi!` event (1 entry) and its margin/fee transfers (open: 2). §6.2 has the per-instruction totals.

**The ephemeral WSOL account (A5).** `trader_wsol` lives at `PDA(short.win, ["trader_wsol", market])`, and its token owner is `trader`.

- **Grief-proof creation** (C0-3): a third party can only pre-fund the address. `System::create_account` would then fail with `AccountAlreadyInUse`, but `allocate` and `assign` only require empty data and the System owner [R-RAY §4.2, agave `system_processor.rs` L75–170]. The helper `create_pda_account(addr, seeds, space, owner)` therefore (1) sweeps any pre-funded lamports to `market_vault`, (2) funds exactly the needed lamports, (3) `allocate(space)` and `assign(owner)` signed with the PDA seeds. `ShareEpoch` records use the same helper.
- `InitializeAccount3` on the native mint sets `amount = lamports − rent`, so no `SyncNative` is needed [R-RAY §4.2].
- A `CloseAccount` on a native account sends all lamports to the destination, which can be the program-owned `ShortPosition` (any writable account can be credited).
- **PumpSwap acceptance is a test gate (T-ATA).** The pAMM IDL puts no ATA seed constraint on `user_quote_token_account` / `user_base_token_account`, and its `claim_cashback` docs say the user's WSOL account "may be any token account of `quote_mint` owned by `user`" [V11]. If the fork test shows PumpSwap nevertheless requires the ATA address, the PumpSwap adapter uses `ATA(trader, WSOL)` instead: `create_idempotent` (payer trader), and if it already existed, close it to the trader first and normalise (so a pre-created account is harmless, C0-3). **Resolved (M6, R-VEN Update H6; `pamm_it::gates::t_ata_and_t_pda_user_*`):** the dumped ELF accepts the non-ATA `trader_wsol` (and non-ATA base accounts) on `buy`, `sell` and `buy_exact_quote_in`, as 285 of 661 sampled mainnet trades do; the fallback is not built.

**Raydium specifics (A47).** Both Raydium venues need an SPL-Token WSOL account on the SOL side and pay no native SOL [R-RAY §4.2]. No ATA, UVA or fee recipient exists on Raydium, so no venue-side rent and no keeper-chosen accounts (C0-14 does not apply there) [R-RAY §4.1]. The sell source is the lending vault itself, with the trader as delegate for exactly `Q`; the delegate clears automatically when the allowance reaches 0 in both p-token and Token-2022 [R-RAY §4.2; V12]. Whether AMM v4 and CPMM accept a delegate as the transfer authority for the source is verified by the Token program, not by the venue: **verified on the dumped ELFs** (U10, T-RAY-PDA: `ray_it::pda`, Token-2022 CPMM pools included; M3, and re-run on the 2026-10 CPMM redeploy in M10); a mainnet example comes with M11.

### 2.5 Venue state machine

**A1.** This implements D1/D2 and fixes C0-15 (no terminal `None`, no optional detection accounts).

```
enum VenueKind { None = 0, PumpCurve = 1, PumpMigrating = 2, PumpSwap = 3, RaydiumV4 = 4, RaydiumCpmm = 5 }
                 // None = list-only: deposits/withdrawals only, no opens (SPEC §3: CLMM/DLMM-only tokens, no pool, ineligible pool)
                 // TEST-ONLY Mock = 6, only in the test-venue build (A49, §3.12); never stored by a release build

classify_pump(bc, cp):                       // bc = PDA(pump, ["bonding-curve", mint]); cp = canonical PumpSwap pool PDA
                                             // BOTH keys are always derived on-chain and required (key-checked) — C0-15
  if bc.owner == pump && bc.disc == BondingCurve:
      require the curve parses (else PumpVenuePrecedence: a Raydium adoption needs proof that no pump venue applies)
      require !curve.is_mayhem_mode && curve.quote_mint == Pubkey::default()      // ADOPTED Q6
      require bc.data_len ≥ 115 (else CurveNeedsExtend; client prepends pump extend_account)
      if !curve.complete:                       // ★1.0.1 (pump-final §6.3), on the live branch only (C2):
          require !curve.is_cashback_coin (else CurveCashbackCoin 6109: v3 refuses one, 6094; D1 (a))
          require curve.depth == 0 (else CurveQuoteNotSol)
                                                -> PumpCurve
                                                // a complete cashback curve classifies as below, so a graduated
                                                // cashback coin lists on PumpSwap (T-LISTING-CASHBACK)
      match canonical_pool(cp):                 // three states (M5-SEC-5; A63)
        Valid                                   -> PumpSwap           (graduated_at = now; A12)
        Unreadable                              -> PumpPoolUnreadable // a pump venue for D1, not executable
        Absent if curve.virtual_token_reserves > 0 -> PumpMigrating   (migration_seen_at = now)
        Absent                                  -> GraduatedElsewhere // complete, reserves 0, no canonical pool (e.g. Fartcoin [V3])
  else                                          -> NotPump

create_market(venue_hint ∈ {Auto, RaydiumV4, RaydiumCpmm}):
  k = classify_pump(bc, cp)
  if k ∈ {PumpCurve, PumpMigrating, PumpSwap, PumpPoolUnreadable}:
                                                require venue_hint == Auto (else PumpVenuePrecedence; D1);
                                                venue = k (PumpPoolUnreadable -> None, never graduated_elsewhere;
                                                M5 listed PumpSwap -> None; M6 as built: PumpSwap on its pool,
                                                the pAMM init set, no price at listing, §3.2)
  elif venue_hint == Auto:                      venue = None     (graduated_elsewhere flag set if k == GraduatedElsewhere)
  else:                                         candidate accounts mandatory; require eligible(candidate) (§2.6);
                                                venue = hint; adopt candidate; graduated_at = age_start(candidate)

sync_venue (prologue of every instruction that carries a ReadSet):
  PumpCurve     : complete ? (cp Valid ? PumpSwap : (cp Absent ∧ vT == 0 ? None* : PumpMigrating)) : stay
  PumpMigrating : cp Valid ? PumpSwap : (cp Absent ∧ vT == 0 ? None* : stay)
                  // cp Unreadable (M5-SEC-5): a pool short.win cannot read, never "no pool" — the market keeps its
                  // pump kind, not executable, the migration pause intact (A63). M5 kept a valid pool
                  // PumpMigrating (M5-SEC-4); M6 built the `cp Valid ? PumpSwap` arm, in ONE step from either
                  // curve kind (a completion and a migration in one transaction included): "On → PumpSwap" below
  PumpSwap      : stay
  RaydiumV4/Cpmm: stay (changes only through the pool-selection path, §2.6)
  None          : crank_price re-runs classify_pump (always passed): pump venue found -> that venue (C0-15;
                  M5 built the curve kinds: the curve cache is derived, the price starts at the curve's spot or,
                  on a priced market, L is rewritten to the curve's √(vT·vQ) (A72), tier D, both route chains and
                  a collection window (fp_*) are cleared; no account is created — the keeper creates the trader's
                  base ATA and pump UVA, §7.1; PumpPoolUnreadable stays None; a detection that cannot classify changes
                  nothing, a crank never reverts on venue state; M6: a valid canonical pool -> PumpSwap —
                  the pool cache, graduated_at = now, tier C, both chains and fp_* cleared; a priced market is
                  rewritten to lp_supply and restarted as a graduation, an unpriced one starts its price at its
                  first PumpSwap observation, marked for the warm-up; no account is created, the keeper
                  creates the trader's base ATA and pAMM UVA, §7.1);
                  a Raydium pool is adopted only through propose_pool (§2.6; never by crank_price):
                    open_positions == 0 : propose_pool adopts any eligible candidate at once (kind listing)
                    open_positions  > 0 : (M4-SEC-4; reachable from M5, *) propose_pool opens / improves a collection window
                                          of pool_fast_window_s (no arming: the market has no route at all), execute_pool_switch
                                          after it adopts the deepest candidate seen (kind fast), or cancels if the detection
                                          set now shows a pump venue (D1); #99: only a candidate whose opening caps every
                                          open position fits (§2.6 rule 3), else CarriedPositionsTooLarge / cancelled
  * A live curve market whose curve completes with zeroed reserves and no canonical pool (the address System-owned)
    means pump changed its migration target: venue = None, graduated_elsewhere = 1, emit VenueStateChanged. The market
    has no route, so the S3 chain runs (§5.3; M2-SEC-5's None path, built in M5: the detection set is sol_settle's
    ReadSet and FV takes the cap-only view, §3.8); a Raydium pool can then be adopted through the collection window
    above (built in M5 on M4's path), never first-come: every later non-fast change of that pool needs
    open_positions == 0 (§2.6 rule 2).

canonical_pool(cp) (M5-SEC-5; as built `detect::canonical_pool`):
    Absent     : cp.owner == System (nothing there, or lamports anyone can send)
    Valid      : canonical_pool_valid(cp)
    Unreadable : anything else — pAMM-owned but not a valid canonical pool (a layout or discriminator change, a bool
                 byte other than 0/1, fields a shifted layout moved, a mayhem pool), or an owner that cannot have
                 created it. The address is pAMM's PDA of ["pool", 0, pool_authority(mint), mint, WSOL], so only pAMM
                 can create an account there and any pool it creates there is this mint's by construction: a field
                 mismatch can only come from a layout shift that kept the discriminator, the M5-SEC-5 failure mode.
                 Reading it as "no pool" turned a migrated curve into "graduated elsewhere" (-> None, open to a Raydium
                 adoption against D1) whenever pAMM changed its Pool layout
canonical_pool_valid(cp) := cp.owner == pAMM && disc == Pool && pool.index == 0
    && pool.creator == pump_pool_authority && pool.base_mint == mint
    && pool.quote_mint == WSOL && !pool.is_mayhem_mode                     (the address is derived, so it is unspoofable)
    // pump_pool_authority = PDA(pump, ["pool-authority", mint]), cached in Market at listing (M5-SEC-6, §2.3.4)

On → PumpSwap (M6 as built, row 55; decided by the owner on 2026-09-30, rows 56 and SPEC §14 M6R-1, M6-SEC-1, M6R-4;
venues::pump_amm::{graduate, restart_observation, start_price}; ECON §5.2, §10.1, #104, #105):
  in the prologue's venue sync of any instruction whose curve ReadSet reads a Valid canonical pool
  (PumpCurve or PumpMigrating, one step; the pool is derived, never passed):
  cache: the pool's vault keys; the pool-v2 marker, boost vault and its ATA, the trader's pAMM UVA and its
    WSOL ATA, the coin-creator pair were derived at the curve's listing (§2.3.4); the pair re-derived only
    if the pool's coin_creator differs (a market re-detected onto the curve derives them all here);
    trader_base_ata exists since the listing
  venue = PumpSwap, graduated_at = now, both route chains and a collection window cleared, tier C,
    pool_d = 0 (the transition reads no LP mint; the first PumpSwap observation writes D, below)
  observation: the anchor is the pool's lp_supply (Pool @203) — its isqrt(X·(Y + VQR)) at creation, read
    from the pool account the curve's ReadSet already carries (no vault sample; 4,193,388,282,654 on ECON's
    pools, equal to the sim's) — rewrite_liquidity(anchor, RaydiumLocked{slow_cap: anchor}): L_ema and every
    ring entry's l, llo, lhi = anchor, (x, y) recomputed, L_slow = min(L_slow, anchor) (never raised: the
    curve's √(vT·vQ) is ≈ 1.35× a standard pool's), the bucket cleared; then mark_restart (ema_warm = 8,
    ema_guard = 1): P_ema carries over and the pool's own next 8 buckets re-seed it (at most one v0.4.1
    step each way per integration: M4X-1 up, M6-SEC-1 down, §4.4), so keeper exits, settlements (§3.8
    step 1b) and opens (§3.4) wait for them
  the transitioning instruction records no observation and runs no route chain on the curve's ReadSet;
    an open or exit whose own prologue transitions refuses VenueMigrating (reverting the transition with it);
    a crank or sol_settle keeps it (sol_settle evaluates nothing in it); VenueStateChanged is emitted
  a market without a price (a PumpSwap listing, a re-detection) starts it at its first executable PumpSwap
    observation (pump_amm::start_price, as a Raydium price start since #105): Observation::new_raydium(now,
    P_spot, √(X·(Y + VQR)), cap = ⌊D·10⁴/λ_min⌋) — P_ema = P_spot, L_ema = L_slow = min(√(X·(Y + VQR)), cap),
    one ring entry — marked (8, 1); λ_min = PUMPSWAP_LOCK_MIN_BPS (VenueKind::lock_min_bps: row 57, the anchor
    since its verification's M6E-1; pool_lock_min_bps at row 56), so cap = D <= √(X·(Y + VQR)): L_ema starts at
    the burned depth, and the first warm-up integration re-seeds it from the pool's own bucket

On every executable PumpSwap observation (M6R-1, row 56; prologue step 6, as a Raydium market's pool_d refresh):
  D = pool_select::locked_depth(Pool.lp_supply, lp_mint.supply, X, Y + VQR)
    = ⌊λ_bps·isqrt(X·(Y + VQR))/10⁴⌋,  λ_bps = ⌊(lp_supply − lp_mint.supply)·10⁴/lp_supply⌋   (0 if lp_supply = 0
      or lp_mint.supply > lp_supply; the LP mint is the ReadSet's P6, §3.12)
  pool_d = D
  if ema_warm > 0:  L_slow = min(L_slow, D)          (the warm-up after the transition or a price start: the
                                                      Raydium adoption's L_slow = min(L_slow, D), taken at the
                                                      first instruction that reads D)
```

**Why `lp_supply` and a restart (M6; decided 2026-09-30, row 56).** The anchor lets the curve's ReadSet stay as it is (T-SIZE; the transition needs no vault and no LP mint of the pool) and makes the one-step `PumpCurve → PumpSwap` possible when a completion and `migrate_v2` land in one transaction (M5-SEC-4). The restart is the post-change confirmation of a Raydium adoption (M4R): a pool pushed before any observation — the M5-SEC-4 reproducer's atomic, self-financed `[buy_v2(rT), migrate_v2]` with the pool at 3.63–3.79× the last curve EMA — forces no exit before eight honest buckets exist (`m5_sec_curve_it::m5_sec_4_an_atomic_complete_and_migrate_graduates_the_market_onto_its_pool`, `graduation_e2e::the_atomic_self_financed_*`: liquidated on the pool 9 s after the transition, lenders whole). The owner kept the warm-up before the first PumpSwap open (OWNER-M6R-2) and accepted the exit delay it brings (OWNER-M6R-4: a keeper exit on a graduated position lands 8–12 s after the migration, §5.4). **Third-party LP (OWNER-M6R-1, decided):** canonical pools accept third-party deposits (R-VEN Update H11), so a deposit between `migrate_v2` and the transition raises `lp_supply` and with it the anchor; as built after M6 `L_slow` then kept the curve's value (≈ 1.35× the pool's depth) for about an hour. Since row 56 the first executable PumpSwap observation — the keeper's own crank in tx3, or the next instruction — reads the pool's LP mint and caps `L_slow` at the locked depth `D` of the burned creation LP (above), which no deposit moves: the push is gone before any decision reads `L_slow` (the transitioning instruction evaluates nothing, and exits and opens wait for the warm-up; `attacks/pumpswap_lp.py` part 2: `L_slow`/depth 1.353 as built, 1.000 now). The inflated anchor's `L_ema` and ring entries are replaced by the warm-up's seed and post-change entries, as after a Raydium adoption.

**Precedence (D1).** A pump coin with a live curve or a canonical PumpSwap pool always uses those venues, even if a deeper Raydium pool exists; `create_market` and `propose_pool` reject Raydium candidates for such markets (`PumpVenuePrecedence`; on a list-only market `propose_pool` runs `classify_pump` on the stored detection set, and `execute_pool_switch` cancels a window once it shows a pump venue). **An unreadable canonical pool counts as a pump venue** (`PumpClass::PumpPoolUnreadable`, M5-SEC-5): the Raydium hint, `propose_pool` and `execute_pool_switch` fail closed on it (`PumpVenuePrecedence` / cancelled), and an `Auto` listing or a re-detection leaves it list-only without the `graduated_elsewhere` flag. A `None → pump venue` transition also clears a collection window (`fp_*`) and both route chains: M4's carry-over, **built in M5** in `crank_price`'s re-detection (`pump_it::graduation::a_none_to_pump_redetection_clears_the_collection_window`; the I16 hook requires both chains cleared). Whether a deeper Raydium pool should ever win is part of owner item O18 (§10); the build keeps D1 precedence.

**Raydium-graduated pump coins and other Raydium tokens.** These map to `RaydiumV4` / `RaydiumCpmm`, not to `None`. The frontend and the keeper run `eligible()` off-chain (same `shortwin-venue-state` code) and always pass the eligible candidate with the highest `D` as `venue_hint`; `Auto` is for tokens with no eligible pool. A market created as `None` anyway (by anyone) is moved onto its pool by the permissionless `propose_pool`. Example: Fartcoin's curve is complete with zeroed reserves and has no canonical PumpSwap pool [V3], so its market adopts AMM v4 pool `Bzc9NZfM…` (38,100 SOL real, λ 99.78 %) [R-RAY §6.4].

**★`PumpMigrating` on the post-buy pool (1.0.1, pump-final §5.4, §6.1.5; PUMP-2026-10-13-1).** Since pump's 2026-10-08 build a curve can complete past `rT` by **synthetic migration** (`buy_v3(rT + δ)`: `rT` from the curve, `δ` from the would-be pool; pump writes `pcB = δ` @150 and `pcQ` @158, and `rQ` excludes `pcQ`), and `migrate_v2` then seeds the pool with the live `curve_base_ata` and `rQ + pcQ − fee`. A `PumpMigrating` market therefore prices the pool `migrate_v2` will create: after a pool part (`pc ≠ 0`) the live `curve_base_ata` (donations included: the one exception to "donations are ignored", §4.3) and `+ pcQ`; without one the deterministic 206.9e12, bit-identical to before (§4.3, §4.5: FV ρ-scaled). Guards, each with its outcome: a **live** curve carrying `pc*` (pump writes them only in the completing buy) has no pricing — not executable, A63's cap-only risk view; a **migrating** curve whose post-complete fields are not known (one of `pcB`, `pcQ` zero, or `vQ − rQ ≠ ivqr`) keeps its curve quoter but has no FV (§4.5). A complete cashback curve is observed and priced like any other (`executable` refuses only a live one; `listable` needs `depth` 0). The keeper alerts on all three states (§7.1 duty 10).

**Is the curve complete and not yet migrated?** Test `complete && virtual_token_reserves > 0`. Just before migration a completed curve still has `vT = 279.9e12`; after migration every reserve is 0 [R-PUMP §2.1, Corrections 1]. Pump coins that graduated to Raydium before PumpSwap show exactly the zeroed state with no canonical pool [V3], and now map to a Raydium venue through the hint or `propose_pool`.

### 2.6 Raydium pool selection (A42 as amended by A60, A71; decision 7)

A mint can have many Raydium SOL pools on both programs; anyone can create one for 0.15 SOL, and neither program derives the pool from the mint [R-RAY §2.1, §2.4, §6.1]. The market must not adopt a thin pool (cheap manipulation), a pool whose liquidity can be pulled, or misread which side is SOL. v0.4 also makes the rule simpler: **a market with open positions changes its pool only when the incumbent fails** — and, since the owner's decision of 2026-09-29 (row 49), **only onto a pool whose opening caps every open position fits**.

**Verification of a candidate** (every check on-chain; every account mandatory and key-checked) [R-RAY §6.2]:

- **AMM v4 pool `P`:** `P.owner == 675kPX9…`, `data_len == 752`; `status ∈ {1, 6, 7}`; `nonce == 254` (so the authority is the constant `5Q544f…`); `{coin_vault_mint, pc_vault_mint} == {WSOL, market.mint}` recording which side is SOL (WSOL must be exactly `So111…112`); the passed vaults equal `P.coin_vault` / `P.pc_vault`, are Tokenkeg accounts with the right mints and authority `5Q544f…`; `market.token_program == Tokenkeg` (AMM v4 is SPL-Token only).
- **CPMM pool `P`:** `P.owner == CPMMoo8…`, `data_len == 637`, discriminator `f7ede3f5d7c3de46`; `{token_0_mint, token_1_mint} == {WSOL, market.mint}` recording the SOL side; the WSOL side's token program is Tokenkeg (the Token-2022 native mint is rejected), the token side's program equals the mint owner; the vaults equal `P.token_{0,1}_vault` with the right mints and authority `GpMZb…`; `amm_config == P.amm_config` (owner CPMM, discriminator `daf42168cbcb2b6f`); `observation == P.observation_key`.
- **Both:** the LP mint equals `P.lp_mint` (Tokenkeg; `supply` at offset 36).

**Eligibility** (`eligible(P)`; as built since the M4 security review, M4-SEC-1 and M4-SEC-3): verification passes; `venue_executable(P)` (§5.3) and one-way fee `φ_ppm ≤ venue_fee_cap_bps·100` (§4.2), else `PoolIneligible`; and the **locked-depth floor**, else `PoolTooThin`:

```
⌊⌊D·isqrt(P_ref)/10⁹⌋·10⁴/λ_min_bps⌋ ≥ pool_min_real_sol
P_ref = the market's P_ema when it has a price (ring_count > 0, P_ema > 0), else the candidate's own spot
        (a Raydium listing; a list-only market that never had a pool)
```

It is the pool's locked SOL at `P_ref` over `λ_min`, exactly the `D` term of rule 5's `R_eff` (§4.7). `D` moves with neither unlocked deposits and withdrawals nor swaps (but for the fee the pool keeps), and on a market with a price neither does `P_ref`, so neither one transaction nor an unlocked deposit that stays in the pool changes eligibility. The floor keeps the lasting guarantee of v0.4.1's pair `R ≥ pool_min_real_sol ∧ λ ≥ λ_min` — at least `λ_min` of the floor stays locked whatever the unlocked LPs do — and admits every pool that pair admitted at the same price (property-tested), plus fully locked pools of 12.5–25 SOL and pools with `λ < λ_min` that hold enough locked SOL; opens stay gated by the price warm-up and `R_eff` (rules 1, 5), and a collection window takes neither under 25 SOL of locked SOL (the window floor below). **v0.4.1's clauses on the live reserve `R ≥ pool_min_real_sol` and on `λ_now ≥ pool_lock_min_bps` are gone:** an unlocked deposit as large as a pool kept it ineligible for as long as the deposit stayed (no adoption, no fast path — a halted market's underwater positions stayed frozen at the pre-halt `P_ema` until S3 at their deadline; M4-SEC-1), and `[buy | withdraw LP, propose_pool / execute_pool_switch, sell | re-deposit]` passed a pool under the floor, or failed one above it, for one instruction (M4-SEC-3). `PoolLockTooLow` (6048) is kept but no longer returned. `create_market`, `propose_pool` and `execute_pool_switch` all apply this rule (the keeper and the frontend run the same `pool_select::eligible`).

**The window floor** (as built since the M4 verification, M4V-1; owner item O18). A collection window's candidate — whose adoption moves **open** positions: a Raydium market's fast path, a list-only market with open positions — must also hold its locked SOL at `P_ref` itself at the SOL floor, `⌊D·isqrt(P_ref)/10⁹⌋ ≥ pool_min_real_sol` (no `/λ_min`; `pool_select::position_floor_ok`, `eligible_with_positions`), when a proposal opens or improves the window (else `PoolTooThin`) and again at the execution (else the window is cancelled). **Where it is judged (M4R-2; PROPOSED, row 46):** a proposal that opens or improves a window judges it at `p_win = min(P_ema, P_cand)`, `P_cand = adoption.state.price()` (the candidate's pre-trade `⌊Y·WAD/X⌋` in this instruction; `P_cand` alone on a market without a price); the execution keeps `P_ema`, with no deferral. `P_ema` does not move while the incumbent cannot execute, so a floor at `P_ema` alone admitted, after a dump during the halt, a pool with only `floor·√(P_live/P_ema)` of real locked SOL — 50 % of the floor after a 4× dump, 25 % after 16× — not "slightly under a floor", as M4's residual (3) said while ECON §6.2 claimed open positions move only onto pools at the floor (the M4R re-verification's M4R-2; both documents now state the rule and its residual 4 alike). A proposer's swap moves only its own `P_cand`, so a dump wrap can only hurt its own proposal; `eligible()`'s `/λ_min` floor stays at `P_ema`. The listing floor admits fully locked pools of only `λ_min·pool_min_real_sol` (12.5 SOL): harmless where no position is carried — listings, list-only and zero-position adoptions keep it, and their opens stay gated (rules 1, 5) — but the fast path moved open positions onto 13- and 20-SOL pools without any manipulation, the harm M4-SEC-3 (b) named (M4V-1; `m4v_it::m4v_1_*`: both refused, a 26-SOL pool adopted). Like the listing floor it reads only `D` and prices, so no LP round trip moves it, and the only price a swap moves is the proposal's own `P_cand`, which can only lower `p_win` (`m4_sec_it::m4_sec_3_*` b: a 20-SOL candidate refused plainly and inside `[buy, propose, sell]`); the residual is a pump-wrapped window-opening proposal, which restores M4's judgment at `P_ema` (residual 4 below). The keeper proposes a window only with a candidate that passes it.

`λ` and `D`:

```
λ_bps = ⌊(lp_counter − lp_mint.supply)·10⁴/lp_counter⌋      AMM v4: lp_counter = AmmInfo.lp_amount @720; CPMM: PoolState.lp_supply @333;
                                                            PumpSwap (M6R-1, row 56): Pool.lp_supply @203, lp_mint = Pool.lp_mint @107
```

The internal counters change only inside the venue program, and LP burned outside it stays in the counter, so `counter − circulating supply` is LP that can never be redeemed [R-RAY §6.3]. LP held in lockers counts as circulating, which is conservative. The main pools of all seven D2 target coins have λ between 92 % and 99.8 % [R-RAY §6.4]. **PumpSwap (M6R-1; owner decision of 2026-09-30, row 56):** a canonical pool's `lp_supply` counts every LP unit ever minted less every unit redeemed by `withdraw` ("supply without burns"), and `migrate_v2` burns the whole creation LP, so `λ` = 1 at creation and falls as third parties deposit (e/acc 92.98 % on mainnet, R-VEN Update H11); a deposit or withdrawal scales `X`, `Y + VQR` and `lp_supply` together, so `D` on the pricing reserves `(X, Y + VQR)` is deposit- and withdraw-invariant exactly as on Raydium (up to λ's whole-bps floor), a swap moves it only by the LP fee the pool keeps, and the boost's zero-fee buy-and-burn keeps it (its rounding in the pool's favour). The PumpSwap rules that read `D` are the Raydium ones that apply to a market without pool selection: the size cap's `D/λ_min` term (§4.6), the tier's locked-SOL bound (§4.7), the exit reference's cap (§3.6, §3.7), a price start's anchor and the warm-up's `L_slow ≤ D` (§2.5) — each at PumpSwap's `λ_min` = `PUMPSWAP_LOCK_MIN_BPS` = 100 % since row 57 (the reference cap and the anchor since its verification's M6E-1), i.e. on `D` itself; eligibility, the floors and the carried fit have no PumpSwap counterpart (the canonical pool is the mint's only one).

**Coverage gap (V2-11; owner item O18).** Launchpads that *lock* LP in a locker program instead of burning it produce pools with λ ≈ 0 (`D ≈ 0`), which are never eligible, so their tokens are list-only despite D2. (The survey below counted pools under v0.4.1's `λ ≥ 50 %` clause; under the M4 floor a pool with `λ < 50 %` is eligible once its locked SOL reaches `λ_min·pool_min_real_sol`, 12.5 SOL — 25 SOL as a collection window's candidate, the window floor (M4V-1); the λ ≈ 0 examples stay list-only.) Live survey on 2026-09-27 [V16]: 1,668 CPMM pools with the creator fee enabled and WSOL as token 0; 311 of them hold ≥ 25 SOL of real reserve, and 67 of those have λ < 50 % — e.g. `AtqUb7Dh…` (2,024.6 SOL, λ 0.0000), `CheJUxVQ…` (608.6 SOL, λ 0.0000), `7H59ffyZ…` (465.5 SOL, λ 0.0000) — while letsbonk-style pools that burn LP pass (`FQd8z3…` 547.2 SOL, λ 0.998; `koZZXrKJ…` λ 1.000). A v1.1 option is to count LP held by the vaults of specific permanent-locker programs as locked, with each program key-checked and its irreversibility proven from source.

**Metric: locked constant-product depth** `D = ⌊λ_bps·isqrt(X·Y)/10⁴⌋` on the pricing reserves (§4.1; ECON §2.1). PROPOSED refinement of [R-RAY §6.3], which used locked SOL `R·λ`:

- A single swap leaves `√(X·Y)` unchanged except for the fee the pool keeps, so an atomic `[buy → propose → sell]` cannot inflate `D` beyond that fee growth. `R·λ` would move with the price.
- **`D` can be pushed only at fee cost** (V2-7). AMM v4 keeps the whole trade fee in the vault until a later `withdrawpnl` [V14; R-RAY §2.3], CPMM keeps the LP part (≈ 84 %) [R-RAY §2.5], so volume grows `√(X·Y)`: a trade of `A` lamports on fee `f` grows it by ≈ `f·A/(2Y)`, and raising `D` by a factor `(1 + x)` through wash trading costs ≈ `2·Y·ln(1 + x)` in fees (+25 %: ≈ 0.45·Y; measured on the real AMM v4 ELF at 1.12× this first-order estimate, `pool_attacks_it::hysteresis`). The locked share `λ` of those fees stays with burned LP, so an attacker holding the unlocked LP recovers at most `(1 − λ)` of them (v0.4.1 had `λ ≥ λ_min` for every eligible pool; since M4-SEC-1 an eligible pool may have a lower `λ` if its locked SOL clears the floor). Hence the margins below.
- Adding or removing unlocked liquidity changes `√(X·Y)` and `λ` inversely, leaving `D` unchanged. The other way to raise `D` is to burn LP, which permanently donates liquidity to the pool: an honest outcome.
- Two pools of the same pair compare correctly on `√(X·Y)`: it equals the SOL reserve divided by `√P`, so it ranks SOL depth at a common price.

**Rule.**

1. **Listing.** `create_market(venue_hint = RaydiumX)` adopts an eligible candidate (eligible at its own spot: a new market has no `P_ema`); `pool_seen_at = now`. A list-only (`None`) market with no open position adopts any eligible candidate through `propose_pool` in the same way (kind listing; D1 checked on its detection set, §2.5; a market that never had a price starts the pool's price state, as a listing does). Opens stay disabled until `pool_seen_at + pool_list_window_s` (1 h) **and until the observation state is confirmed, `ema_warm == 0`** (`EmaWarmingUp`; **PROPOSED**, M4V-5 as unified by M4R, row 46): a Raydium listing or a list-only market's first adoption starts the price state with `Observation::new_raydium` (`L = min(√(X·Y), cap)`) and marks it (`ema_warm = EMA_WARMUP_BUCKETS` = `RING_LEN` = 8), so the first open waits for 8 integrations since the start, every one of a bucket recorded after it; since M4R every Raydium → Raydium adoption marks it too (rule 4). A pushed spot seeds such a price state at no cost (residual 1 below), and without honest observations `R_eff` and the spot/EMA check read it back; the keeper therefore observes zero-position Raydium markets through and at the end of their listing window (§7.1 duty 1). The warm-up integrations re-seed `P_ema` towards the lowest post-start bucket low (§4.4), so a start price pushed up falls as soon as one warm-up bucket holds an honest observation — since M6-SEC-1 (row 56) by at most one v0.4.1 step per integration (×11/12 at `dt` = 1, ≤ ×0.4986 by the gate), the rest through the steady-state EMA inside the listing window, the safe side (opens refused on the spot/EMA check meanwhile) (before M4R, 8 honest per-second buckets moved `P_ema` only `1 − (5/6)⁸ ≈ 77 %` of the way); one pushed down recovers by at most the largest v0.4.1 step per integration (M4X-1; the safe side: opens stay refused on the spot/EMA check and `R_eff` meanwhile); the window's observations every 60 s continue it. During that window `propose_pool` adopts a candidate immediately if the market has **no open position** and `D_cand ≥ (1 + pool_list_margin_bps/10⁴)·D_inc` (5 %: `D` can be pushed only at fee cost, V2-7). The zero-position condition is the build's reading of decision 7 and I15: a listing window can follow a fast path taken with positions open, and those positions must not see a second pool change that no failure caused. After a thin listing is replaced, opens right after the window can still fail `PoolTooThin` until `L_slow` (τ = 1 h) converges, because an adoption never raises `L_slow` (rule 4; measured by the keeper and engine tracks: conservative by design, ops and the UI should expect it).
2. **Adoption without a failure — only while `open_positions == 0`** (decision 7). After the window, `propose_pool(candidate)` adopts the candidate immediately if the market has no open position and `D_cand ≥ (1 + h)·D_inc` with `h = pool_switch_margin_bps` (25 %); otherwise it fails with `PositionsOpen` or `PoolNotDominant`. As built, such a candidate is adopted at once even while the incumbent fails or a collection window runs (the adoption clears the window). The incumbent's own pool is never a candidate (`PoolNotDominant`). There is no pending switch, no delay and no `execute_pool_switch` for this path. Open positions therefore never see a pool change that they could not also see on a failure, and the v0.3 four-timer state (window, margin, pending switch with delay, fast-path window) shrinks to two.
   **Griefing path (disclosed; R4B-10; accepted as disclosed by the owner on 2026-10-09 with O18, known-issues KI-16).** One minimum-size position (0.1 SOL notional; Tier A up to 30 days, re-opened at expiry) keeps `open_positions ≥ 1` and so pins the market to an eligible but much thinner incumbent — lower caps and tier, cheaper manipulation — until that incumbent fails. No lender funds are at risk; it is a quality regression from v0.3's pending switch. Remedy without new state: Emergency pauses opens on the market (existing power, SPEC §9), the market drains within the longest open duration, and the keeper's duty 12 adopts the dominant pool at `open_positions == 0`. A delayed adoption with positions open (e.g. `D_cand ≥ 2·D_inc` for 1 h) was considered and not adopted: it re-creates the pending switch that decision 7 removed. Owner item O18 lists it.
3. **Fast path** (incumbent failure; A71; V1-7, V2-1, V2-7, R3A-4, R3B-8). The trigger is its own predicate and its own chain:
   ```
   pool_fail := !venue_executable(incumbent) ∨ φ_live(incumbent) > config.venue_fee_hard_cap_bps     (venue-side evidence only)
   chain (prologue step 8, Raydium markets): on a pool_fail observation, if pool_fail_since == 0 or
       now − last_pool_fail_obs > S3_OBS_GAP_S then pool_fail_since = now; always last_pool_fail_obs = now;
       an observation without pool_fail clears both
   ```
   The Emergency route-broken flag is **not** part of `pool_fail` (T-S3-BROKEN asserts the chain is identical with and without the flag), and the chain is not the S3 chain (which is fed by `s3_no_route`). Once `now − pool_fail_since ≥ pool_fast_route_s` (120 s) and this instruction's own observation fails `pool_fail` (the **armed** fast path), the first `propose_pool` with `D_cand ≥ pool_fast_min_bps·pool_d/10⁴` (`pool_d` = the incumbent's locked depth at its last executable observation) and the window floor at `min(P_ema, P_cand)` (M4V-1, M4R-2) opens a **collection window** of `pool_fast_window_s` (60 s) at `fp_t0 = now`, recording the candidate's keys, `D` and kind (`fp_keys`, `fp_d`, `fp_venue`; M4 also recorded `λ` in `fp_lambda_bps`, retired by M4R; event `PoolProposed`). During the window an eligible candidate with a strictly higher `D` (and still `≥ pool_fast_min_bps` of `pool_d`, and the window floor at `min(P_ema, P_cand)`) replaces the one in `fp_*`, keeping `fp_t0`; the window's own pool cannot re-propose itself (`PoolNotDominant`: an improvement must be another, strictly deeper pool). `execute_pool_switch` after the window re-verifies the recorded pool in full (the same keys, eligible and above the window floor now at `P_ema`) and adopts it only if the incumbent still fails `pool_fail` **and the chain that armed the window is unbroken**: `pool_fail_since ≠ 0` and `pool_fail_since + pool_fast_route_s ≤ fp_t0` (M4-SEC-2 — an incumbent that recovered after the window opened and failed again, or a stale window followed hours later by a one-second failure, must not move positions); any other outcome cancels and clears the window (event `PoolSwitchCancelled`), never a revert; it does not re-check `pool_fast_min_bps`. On a Raydium market improvements need the same unbroken chain; a proposal while the window has run out or its chain is broken fails `PoolWindowClosed` (6100) until `execute_pool_switch` resolves the window. Every proposal waits while **the candidate's own** Raydium program is flagged in `VenueGuard` (`VenueUpgraded`; M4-SEC-8, §2.3.2), while an upgrade of the other Raydium program — typically the failing incumbent's — holds nothing up. An execution whose window candidate's program is flagged treats it as **not adoptable now and cancels the window** (as built since the M4 verification, M4V-4): M4-SEC-8's execution reverted and kept the window, and with it `PoolWindowClosed` for every other proposal — the unflagged program's included — until the Emergency review, freezing the fast path while the halted incumbent's positions ran towards S3. The `pool_fail` chain stays armed, so a proposal on the other program opens a new window at once (`m4v_it::m4v_4_*`: adopted after 240 s of `pool_fail`, S3 wait 600 s), and after `revalidate_venue` the flagged program's pool can be proposed again. The fast path works whether or not positions are open. Its whole duration fits inside the shortest S3 window any position can have (`pool_fast_route_s + pool_fast_window_s ≤ 540 = 600 − 60`, compiled, R3A-11 b). A **list-only market with open positions** (reachable from M5, §2.5) uses the same window without arming or chain (M4-SEC-4): its first eligible proposal opens it, a strictly deeper one improves it, and the execution adopts the deepest candidate seen as kind fast, instead of pinning the positions to whichever eligible pool is proposed first.

   **Switch only if all fit** (OWNER decision, 2026-09-29; row 49; ECON §6.1, §12.12 (11)). A proposal that opens or improves a collection window whose adoption would carry open positions — this fast path, or a list-only market's window with open positions — also needs every open position to fit the candidate's normal opening caps (§4.6), else `CarriedPositionsTooLarge` (6102); the execution re-checks and cancels a window whose candidate no longer fits (the chain stays armed):
   ```
   X₀(p) = caps::conservative_x0(X_cand, min(L_slow, D), p, (D, λ_min))    the X₀ an open on the candidate has right after the
           = min(X_cand, ⌊min(L_slow, D)·10⁹/isqrt⁺(p)⌋, ⌊D·10⁹·10⁴/(λ_min·isqrt⁺(p))⌋) ≤ D/√p     adoption (L_slow' = min(L_slow, D));
                                                                          X_cand (its live token reserve) at a proposal only
   q_max = caps::carried_q_bound(max_q_hwm, ΣB_Q) = min(max_q_hwm, ΣB_Q)          (ΣB_Q alone while max_q_hwm = 0)
   caps::carried_fit(q_max, ΣB_Q, CarriedCaps { x0: X₀(p), impact_pos_bps, impact_mkt_bps (the tier the market would have on the
                     candidate at p), phi_ppm = caps::carried_phi(min_open_fee_ppm, φ_cand)
                     = min(φ_inc, φ_cand, CARRIED_FEE_CAP_PPM) (#100; the 2,500-ppm cap row 51),
                     fee_size_cap_x100, fee_oi_cap_x100 })                         position caps on X₀; OI on X₁ = X₀
   at p = min(P_ema, P_cand) (the M4R-2 floor's reference) and at p = P_ema; the first refusal wins (engine::pool_select::carried_fit)
   ```
   A lower price credits more tokens to the same depth, so judging at `P_ema` too keeps a dump wrapped around either instruction from loosening the fit's **depth terms**. The execution reads `L_slow`, `D` and the prices only — no `X_cand` — so no unlocked LP's withdrawal or buy around it can cancel a window that fits (the lever M4X-3 kept out of the execution's floor). A proposal's `X_cand` binds the honest flow, but it is not a guarantee (FIT-1, row 50): `X_cand` binds when the candidate trades above `P_ema` after a genuine pump during the halt, and `[sell ≈X_cand tokens into it, propose_pool, buy them back]` lifts it inside the transaction for two swap fees — no rule that reads the candidate's reserve or spot can be protected within one transaction, and a band on `P_cand` is met by dumping only to `P_ema`. What holds is the execution's `X₀ = min(L_slow', ⌊D·10⁴/λ_min⌋)/√P_ema`: a carried `q` is at most that, i.e. up to `λ·√(P_cand/P_ema)` × a native open's cap on the adopted pool (≈ 1.4× at a 2× move; `pool_select_it::carried_fit::fit1_*`: 1.085 / 1.109 / 1.366 at `r` 1.2 / 1.5 / 1.9), and under the pushes such a position is liquidated within a second of the control (`freeze::fit1_*`; ECON §12.12 residual 13). **The fee** (#100, FIT-2; row 51, FITS-1): the fee-scaled caps take `min(φ_inc, φ_cand, CARRIED_FEE_CAP_PPM)`, `φ_inc` = `Market.min_open_fee_ppm`, the lowest one-way fee an open paid since the market last had no position — the fee the open positions' caps and margin were computed at — so a position carried onto a higher-fee pool stays in the size class of its own fee (0.75 % of `X₀` at 25 bps, not a 1 % pool's 2.47 % impact cap), and `CARRIED_FEE_CAP_PPM` = 2,500 (compiled) keeps every carried position in that 25-bps class whatever the two fees: `min(φ_inc, φ_cand)` alone was the candidate's own 1 % on a 1 %→1 % switch, whose carried positions at 60–100 % of the 2.47 % impact cap ended in S1 under the pushes on the fork (FITS-1); such a position is now refused and settles S3 at fair value (residual 12); the impact caps do not read `φ`. An open right after an adoption is sized on the candidate's locked depth (the adoption caps `L_slow` at `D`), so a position at a λ 50 % incumbent's size cap moves only onto a candidate whose locked depth covers the incumbent's `L_slow`, its whole depth (≥ 111 % of its reserves at λ 90 %), and a thinner candidate carries a proportionally smaller position (ECON §6.1). If no candidate fits, the market stays halted: its positions exit through S3 at fair value, a healthy one at its deadline (the O14 exposure; ECON §12.12 residual 12), which the owner accepts as the intended outcome. Zero-position adoptions (rule 2) and listings (rule 1) are unaffected. The keeper proposes only candidates that fit (§7.1 duty 5). What it removes: the oversized carried position that M4F-1, M4G-1 and M4G-3 needed (a reference pushed by capital after the guard's clear blocked the liquidation of a carried position of 3–6 % of the new pool's `X` until S1). With the fee caps at the candidate's own fee it did not make every push a delay: a 25-bps incumbent's position at a 1 % candidate's fit limit (2.47 % of `X₀`, the margin posted on the incumbent's cost) ended in S1 under a held deposit pulled at a 4×/30 s pump (FIT-2); with `min(φ_inc, φ_cand)` (row 50) it is refused, and a push delays a position at the new fit limit as it delays one opened on the pool (ECON §12.12 (11) (d)); with the 25-bps cap (row 51) the same holds for a 1 %→1 % switch (residual 15, closed). **The mark** (FIT-3, row 50): `max_q_hwm` only rises while a position is open, so a position opened at the incumbent's size cap and closed at once keeps every thinner candidate refused until the market empties or the S3 exits bring `ΣB_Q` under the candidate's cap — a disclosed residual (residual 14); #100's first fix, a permissionless `refresh_max_q`, was withdrawn (FITV-1).
4. **Every adoption** — listing, listing-window replacement, zero-position adoption, fast path — may change the venue kind between `RaydiumV4` and `RaydiumCpmm`, and:
   - the pool itself is written whole: venue, pool cache (every other slot cleared, so no CPMM config or observation of a previous pool stays), SOL side, `pool_d = D`;
   - `P_ema` carries over (same asset, arbitraged) until the warm-up re-seeds it (below); a list-only market that never had a price instead starts the pool's price state, as a listing does;
   - **the adoption reads no sample of the new pool** (PROPOSED, M4R, row 46; ECON §5.2; `engine::pool_select::adopt(market, a, now, list_window_s, lambda_min_bps)`, no `l_rec`): with `D` its locked depth and `cap = pool_select::depth_at_lambda(D, λ_min) = ⌊D·10⁴/λ_min⌋`,
     ```
     a priced market:    observe::rewrite_liquidity(cap, RaydiumLocked { slow_cap: D })   // L_ema = cap, L_slow = min(L_slow, D);
                                                                                      // every ring entry's l = llo = lhi = cap, (x, y) recomputed
                         observe::mark_restart(&mut ema)                               // ema_warm = EMA_WARMUP_BUCKETS (8), ema_guard = 1
     an unpriced market: Observation::new_raydium(now, P_spot, √(X·Y), cap)            // a list-only market's first adoption: L = min(√(X·Y), cap),
                                                                                      // P_ema = P_spot, marked the same way
     ```
     `P_ema` and the ring prices carry over (same asset, arbitraged; stale after a halt), but only until the warm-up replaces them: the next 8 integrations re-seed `P_ema = min lo`, rising by at most the largest v0.4.1 step per integration (M4X-1, row 47) and, since M6-SEC-1 (row 56), falling by at most the largest step down (`price_down_bound`), and `L_ema = min(max lhi, ⌊lomed(lhi)·(10⁴ + C)/10⁴⌋)` over the post-change entries (§4.4), and while `ema_warm > 0` on an executable venue `liquidate` / `expire` fail `EmaWarmingUp`, `sol_settle` evaluates nothing and Raydium opens wait (§3.4, §3.6–§3.8); while `ema_guard = 1` the exit reference reads `min(L_ema, L_mlo)` (§3.6) and `L_slow` integrates `min(lobs, L_mlo)` (§4.4; M4X-2). No `L_live` or `L_rec` is read: `recorded_liquidity` is deleted and `record_window` stops writing `λ`. **Why** (M4R-1): M4 as built wrote `min(L_rec, √(X·Y)_now, cap)`, the smaller of two samples taken in two transactions (M4V-2; M4-SEC-5 took the record alone, v0.4.1 the adopting instruction's own sample). A deposit could not push that up, but an unlocked LP's withdrawal around either sampling instruction wrote `D`, and after the adoption the LP holds `L_ema` there with a withdraw-wrapped crank every second (directional aggregation: one observation on its own side freezes the EMA), so a position within ≈ `q/x` of `cr_liq`, healthy on the pool as it trades, became liquidatable on the EMA leg and a withdraw-wrapped spot leg — `tests/litesvm/tests/m4r_it.rs::m4r_explore_liquidation_grid` (`M4R_GRID=19700,19750 M4R_SECS=90`): liquidated 24–26 s after the adoption when wrapped, never in 90 s when not. The carried, stale `P_ema` was a second forced path (after a mild dip during the halt an honest adoption let the LP holder liquidate a healthy position at +2 s, ECON §12.12 (9)), and on a `λ < λ_min` pool M4's honest cap `D/λ_min` was already the start of such a band (ECON §12.12 (2)). The anchor reads nothing any party can wrap; the seed reads bucket **highs** for `L` and **lows** for `P`, the sides a wrapped sample cannot use to force an exit, so an honest warm-up ends with `L_ema` equal to the pool's depth for every λ (λ 10–99.78 %: 1.000 at the gate) and the box narrow from the gate on (M4V-3 and M4-SEC-6 resolved), and forcing needs all 8 warm-up buckets attacker-only (residual 1);
   - **every ring entry's `l`, `llo` and `lhi` are rewritten to the anchor and its `(x, y)` recomputed** (A72; R3B-7 a, R3A-11 d): with carry-over, the ring median kept the old pool's liquidity and the settlement box stayed more than 1 % wide in `L` for 3–4 s after each change (ECON §10.1; the fork replay of `venue_switch.py` measured 5 s without the rewrite and 0 s with it, `pool_attacks_it`). Since M4R the ring is read during the warm-up only where nothing is gated — a new pool that cannot execute (S3 reads the partly anchored ring, residual 8) — and the warm-up replaces every entry before the gate opens (`venue_switch.py` (a): 4 wide seconds with or without the rewrite, all inside the gate; since AIR-15 caps the box's `L_hi` at `D`, ECON #117, the rewritten ring has none and a carried-over one keeps its 4);
   - the current observation bucket is cleared; both route chains and the collection window (`fp_*`) are cleared (the new pool is observed afresh; the tier is recomputed by the next crank or open);
   - `graduated_at` is kept (age is the token's time on an eligible pool); open positions keep all locked terms and exit on the new pool;
   - `pool_seen_at = now` **only if the market is not already inside a listing window**, so opens wait `pool_list_window_s` after an adoption outside a window while the `D` ranking settles, and a chain of proposals cannot extend a window;
   - a list-only market takes the candidate's age start as `graduated_at` (O13, O13b) and, for a curve that graduated elsewhere, the `graduated_elsewhere` flag;
   - emit `PoolSwitched` (one event per instruction: neither pool-selection instruction emits `VenueStateChanged` or `RouteChainChanged`).
5. **Opens are sized on locked depth, not refused on `λ_now`** (V2-8). Every liquidity input of an open is bounded by the locked depth, which unlocked deposits cannot move: tier liquidity uses `R_eff = min(R_now, R_slow, ⌊⌊D·isqrt(P_ema)/10⁹⌋·10⁴/λ_min_bps⌋)` (§4.7), and the conservative token reserve for caps is `min(X_now, ⌊L_slow·10⁹/isqrt⁺(P_ema)⌋, ⌊D·10⁹·10⁴/(λ_min_bps·isqrt⁺(P_ema))⌋)` (§4.6; ECON §2.1). Opens require `R_eff ≥ pool_min_real_sol`. Withdrawing *all* unlocked LP leaves at least `λ_min` (50 %) of the depth a position was sized on. Since M4-SEC-1 eligibility and adoption do not read `λ_now` either: they test the same locked-depth term at `P_ema` (the floor above), so `λ_min` only scales that floor and these sizing bounds (v0.4.1: "`λ ≥ λ_min` is still required for eligibility and adoption"). On PumpSwap (row 56) the same terms read the burned LP's `D` at `λ_min` = `PUMPSWAP_LOCK_MIN_BPS` = 100 % since row 57 (OWNER-M6D-1): a PumpSwap open is sized on the burned depth itself, and no withdrawal takes the pool below the depth a position was sized on (§4.6, §4.7); the exit reference's cap is that depth too (M6E-1, §3.6).

| Attack | Outcome under the rule |
|---|---|
| Fake deep pool with self-supplied liquidity, pulled after capture | Unlocked liquidity adds nothing to `D`; winning requires burning LP worth `(1 + h)` times the incumbent's locked depth, which permanently deepens the market, and it can happen only while no position is open |
| Price push on the candidate at proposal time (atomic bundle) | `√(X·Y)` is invariant under swaps; no effect |
| Thin pools used for price manipulation | Never read. The market prices, observes and executes only on the adopted pool, whose keys are stored and re-checked on every instruction |
| Mint on the wrong side, fake quote mint | The SOL side is derived from the verified mint fields; the quote must be exactly `So111…112` under Tokenkeg |
| Proposal spam | A weaker proposal cannot displace the incumbent or a better fast-path candidate; each fake pool costs 0.15 SOL [R-RAY §6.3]; adoptions inside a listing window do not extend it |
| Wash trading to raise `D` (V2-7) | Costs ≈ `2·Y·ln(1 + x)` in fees (1.12× on the real AMM v4 ELF), of which the locked share `λ` stays with burned LP (`≥ λ_min` for pools v0.4.1 admitted); the 5 % listing margin and the 25 % adoption margin make flips expensive; with positions open only a failure can change the pool |
| Front-running the fast path with an own pool carrying unlocked LP (V2-7) | The collection window adopts the deepest eligible candidate seen; an own pool wins only if it is the deepest, and its locked depth `D` — the most positions are sized on is `D/λ_min`, rule 5 — cannot be withdrawn afterwards (`pool_attacks_it::front_run`: after the pull, `D`, `pool_d` and the sizing are unchanged) |
| Emergency flag used to arm the fast path (V1-7) | Impossible: `pool_fail` does not read the flag (T-S3-BROKEN) |
| Adding unlocked liquidity to block opens (V2-8) | No effect: opens do not check `λ_now`; sizing uses locked depth |
| Adding unlocked liquidity to every alternate pool, and leaving it there, to keep them ineligible: no adoption, no fast path, a halted market's positions frozen until S3 at the pre-halt `P_ema` (M4-SEC-1) | No effect since M4: eligibility is the locked-depth floor at `P_ema`, which a deposit does not move (`m4_sec_it::m4_sec_1_*`: with and without the deposit the halted market's window opens at 120 s, the candidate is adopted after it and the underwater position is liquidated there) |
| Atomic swap or LP round trip around `propose_pool` / `execute_pool_switch` (`[buy / withdraw LP, act, sell / re-deposit]`: a pool under the floor adopted, or a window cancelled; M4-SEC-3 and the implementer's two tripwires) | No effect on a market with a price: `D` and `P_ema` do not move inside a transaction (the tripwires are inverted: `pool_attacks_it::lambda_games::lp_dilution_no_longer_cancels_the_fast_path` and `…::a_round_trip_under_the_sol_floor_no_longer_cancels_the_fast_path`). Residual (disclosed): a list-only market that never had a price judges the floor at the candidate's spot, so `[buy, propose_pool, sell]` can adopt a pool under it; bounded: such a market has no position, its first open waits for the price warm-up (`EmaWarmingUp`, M4V-5) and the keeper's listing-window observations, after which `R_eff` refuses it (`PoolTooThin`, rule 5; `m4v_it::m4v_5_*`), and a zero-position adoption or the listing window replaces the pool |
| A recovered incumbent that fails again, or a stale window followed by a one-second failure (M4-SEC-2) | The window adopts only while the chain that armed it holds; otherwise it cancels, and a new failure re-arms after `pool_fast_route_s` (`m4_sec_it::m4_sec_2_*`) |
| LP moves of the winning candidate around the adopting instruction, to write its locked-only depth (or an inflated one) into the ring (M4-SEC-5) | No effect since M4R: the adoption reads no sample (rule 4); `L_ema` is the anchor `D/λ_min` until the warm-up seeds it from the new pool's bucket highs (`m4_sec_it::m4_sec_5_*`: a withdrawal around the execution changes nothing). M4 as built wrote `min(L_rec, L_live, D/λ_min)`, which a withdrawal around either sample pushed to `D` — a forcing path, not a delay (next row) |

**Residuals of the M4 rules** (disclosed; owner item O18; (a), (b) and items 1–4 and 13 accepted as disclosed by the owner on 2026-10-09, eleventh round (known-issues KI-17 … KI-21, KI-25); as amended by the M4 verification, by M4R, row 46, by #99, row 49, and by rows 50–51): (a) a list-only market without a price judges the floor at the candidate's spot, which one transaction can push; bounded by the price warm-up and the keeper's listing-window observations (M4V-5), with the sustained-bundle residual of the table above; (b) no fast-path candidate's spot is compared with `P_ema` beyond the window floor at `min(P_ema, P_cand)` (table above). M4 as built's residuals (2), (3) and (5) — the two-sample `[D, D/λ_min]` seed, the floors at a stale `P_ema`, the box delay after a `λ < λ_min` switch — are replaced by M4R's, all disclosed with O18 (ECON §12.12):

1. **Degraded mode.** If every one of the 8 warm-up buckets is attacker-only (keeper absent or censored for the whole warm-up; 7 keeper-absent seconds when the attacker executes the switch and cranks in its second), the attacker can seed `L_ema = D` with withdraw-wrapped cranks, and an 8-s genuine held drain does the same; the M4R-1 band then applies at +9 s (M4 as built was forced whatever the keeper did). On pools with `λ < 1/(1 + C)` (50 %), 4 attacker-only warm-up buckets suffice, because the seed falls to `(1 + C)·D < H`. Steady state needs 3 attacker-only seconds for the same band (10). On the price side, pump-wrapped cranks and a pump-wrapped liquidation in those seconds raise the seed by at most the largest v0.4.1 step per integration (M4X-1): a position within ≈ 2.8× of the carried `P_ema` can be liquidated at the gate at the attacker's pumped price — what the same attacker-only seconds force in steady state and forced under M4 as built (ECON §12.12 (8)), never earlier. Before M4X-1 the seed read the pump itself and 8 such seconds forced any threshold.
2. **Capital deposit freeze.** A deposit-wrapped warm-up crank, then deposit-wrapped cranks every second, hold `L_ema ≤ (1 + C)·H` (higher only if ≥ 5 of the 8 warm-up buckets are pushed), with about the pool's size in both assets re-deposited every second and no fee. The EMA leg is delayed by at most ≈ `(1 − H/L)·q/x` in price, and at a flat price for as long as the freeze lasts; the box stays wide, so S2/S3 amounts wait (the ECON §10.5 class). **While the guard is set and the keeper observes every second** (§7.1 duty 5) the reference stays at the honest lows, however long the freeze is held (the guard on the `L_ema` term and on `L_slow`'s input, M4X-2). Once the guard has cleared — at the gate, or after the keeper missed 5 of 8 guarded seconds — a push reaches the reference again, up to the §3.6 cap (`λ/λ_min` of the depth). That blocked carried positions of 3–6 % of the new pool's `X` until S1 (M4F-1 with the keeper's 30-s cadence, ECON §12.12 (4); M4G-1's missed seconds; M4G-3's held deposit pulled at a pump). **Since #99 no such position is carried** (row 49), and the push delays a fitting one by 0–1 s (0–1.4 % of price), as it delays positions opened at the caps in steady state (ECON §12.12 (11), part 4e). That held at 25 bps; with the carried fee caps at the candidate's own fee, a 25-bps incumbent's position at a 1 % candidate's fit limit (2.47 % of `X₀`, the margin posted on the incumbent's cost) ended in S1 under a held deposit pulled at a 4×/30 s pump, a freeze after the clear or one with keeper misses (FIT-2). Since row 50 the carried fee caps take `min(φ_inc, φ_cand)`: such a position is refused and settles S3 at fair value, and at the new fit limit (0.75 % of `X₀`) the pushes delay the exit by 0–1 s (ECON §12.12 (11) (d)); since row 51 they take at most 25 bps, which closes the 1 %→1 % exception (residual 15). Since row 51 the keeper also covers every second while foreign liquidity-deviating observations recur on a market with positions (§7.1 duty 2), so a freeze after the clear holds `L_ema` at its first step. Faster pumps (4× in ≤ 25 s at Tier C, ≤ 60 s at Tier A) end in S1 without any push, for positions opened on the pool as well (the fast-pump class).
3. **Withdraw contest while the guard is set.** An unlocked-LP holder who withdraw-wraps ≥ 4 of the 8 warm-up seconds and ≥ 4 of every 8 after, then withdraw-wraps a liquidation of a genuinely liquidatable position, makes the borrower overpay by at most `cost(D)/cost(H) − 1 ≈ (1/λ − 1)·q/x` of `B` (≈ 0 on λ ≈ 1 pools; +4.04 %, 1.24 SOL, in the sim, which M4 as built also allowed through its `D` seed). With the guard set it forces no exit (the reference and the seed read the honest lows). In steady state it did (FITS-2, row 51; residual 10): with the spot leg at the drained `L_live`, a withdraw-wrapped liquidation after a drag forced positions healthy at the pool's depth where `δ` covered the drained cost, and after a genuine spike's retreat with no drag at all. Since row 51 the spot leg reads `max(L_live, L_ema')` (§3.6 step 3) and the keeper's per-second liquidity-anomaly coverage holds a drag at its first step (§7.1 duty 2): no drag of attacker-only seconds forced anything in the sims (ECON §12.12 (5b)) until ★AIR-14's cap at `D`, which forces one level (2.06× against 2.065× at 0.79 × the open cap); the overpay bound above stands for a due liquidation. A genuinely reached low frozen by withdraw-wrapped cranks still forces, exactly as the LP's withdrawal for good would (FITX-1, row 52; residual 10).
4. **M4R-2 is closed only for honest dumps before the window opens.** One pump-wrapped window-opening proposal by the thin pool's backer (0.03–0.04 SOL) restores M4's `P_ema` judgment, never looser; a genuine dump inside the 60-s window, after the proposal that opened it, is judged by the execution at `P_ema` alone and adopted (M4X-3; never looser than as built). The warm-up then lowers `P_ema` towards the live price — since M6-SEC-1 (row 56) by at most one v0.4.1 step per integration: 1.86× / 7.44× the pool at the gate after a 4× / 16× dump (`switch_warmup.py` (6); the fork 1.73× after 4×, `m4r_it::m4x3_*`), on the pool about a minute later — which forces no exit (the spot leg reads the live price); an open waits out the adopted pool's listing window (`PoolListWindow`) and is then refused `PoolTooThin`. The execution does not re-read the candidate's one-instruction spot: a failure there would either revert (every other proposal held, the M4V-4 freeze) or cancel (a dump-wrapped execution then cancels windows until S3). A tracked-EMA execution floor needs a window-observation path and was not adopted; a follow-up option is a `pool_fail` clause for an incumbent below the floor at the confirmed `P_ema`.
5. **Held push during the warm-up.** Holding the pool pumped for all 8 warm-up seconds (genuine price for every observation) seeds `P_ema` high, by at most the largest v0.4.1 step per integration: the steady-state held class (ECON §12.6; +9 s vs as built +10 s by a withdraw-wrapped liquidation after the push had ended — open since row 51, the spot leg no longer reading the drained depth; with no keeper at all, for a held 3× push on a near-threshold position, 9 s and −0.38 SOL, as built 8 s and −0.27). Atomic bundles in attacker-only seconds are residual 1.
6. **Paid down-push of the price seed.** One dump-wrapped warm-up crank lowers the seed without bound; after the gate `P_ema` recovers at ≤ +16.7 %/s, a delay of about `ln k/ln(7/6)` s — paid, the ECON §12.9 class.
7. **Exit latency.** Adoption + 9 s, usually faster than as built because `P` is fresh (2.2×: +9 vs +13 s; 3× S1: +49 vs +61 s; λ 99.78 % at 2×: +9 vs +26 s; the big position: +9 vs +14 s); slower only where as built was already right (5× / 16× S1: +49 vs +48 s).
8. **A new pool that halts inside the warm-up.** Nothing is gated on a venue that cannot execute: positions are frozen until S3 or the next fast path, as built, and S3 reads the partly anchored ring; the price seed stays where the step bound left it (M4X-1), so after a genuine move during the halt larger than the seed reached before the new pool halted, an S3 that needs the position liquidatable waits for its deadline, as with M4 as built's carried `P_ema` (`switch_confirm_it::a_new_pool_that_halts_in_the_warm_up_is_not_gated` halts at +6 s, when the seed has reached the pool's 2.5×).
9. **Rent during the warm-up** accrues on the running-minimum `P_ema` for ≤ 8 s (lender-unfavourable, negligible).
10. **The steady-state withdraw drag (FITV-2, FITS-2, FITX-1; closed by row 51 for drags of attacker-only seconds, up to missed keeper seconds and, since ★AIR-14, one level; a genuinely reached low, frozen, is left — bounded by a withdrawal for good; O18).** Withdraw-wrapped cranks in the keeper's quiet seconds (29 of every 30 on a healthy market) took `L_ema` to the locked depth `D` and held it there through the keeper's own observations, and a withdraw-wrapped liquidation — its spot leg at the drained `L_live` — forced positions healthy at the pool's depth: where `δ` covers `cost(D)/cost(H) − 1` (25 bps; at 1 % below about half the cap) after a 30-s drag (the fork: `FITV_QPM` 500, 2.025×), at 1.9 % of `X` after 25 min (the fork's cap-sized regression position), and at the cap once `L_slow` had followed (0.79 h at λ 50 %, 1.80 h at λ 25 %, 3.19 h at `λ_min` 2,000: 2.01–2.07× against the honest 2.078×). #100's residual 3 ("never forces an exit") and this residual's "0.79 h" understated it (FITS-2). **Row 51:** the spot leg reads `max(L_live, L_ema')` (§3.6 step 3) and the keeper covers every second of a drag after its first (§7.1 duty 2), so `L_ema` holds at one step (≈ 0.917 of the depth). Until ★AIR-14 no drag of attacker-only seconds forced anything in ECON §12.12 (5b) — every pool and size, drags of 30 s to 3 h, the probed level not within 8 h (a λ 99.78 % pool's one level at its threshold is the attacker's attempt landing first, under every rule). Since AIR-14's cap at `D` the one step forces one level (2.06× against 2.065× at 0.79 × the cap). The spike-and-retreat case (the spot leg's veto overridden by the withdrawal, 2.01–2.07× under #100) is closed too. **Left:** each covered second whose keeper observation does not land is another attacker-only step, and they add up while the attacker keeps wrapping (the M4G-1 class; 3 isolated misses in an hour force a half-cap 1 % position at 2.03× against 2.039×; since ★AIR-14 one miss forces a cap-sized one at 2.07×, and 20 force it at 2.01–2.07×, where only 20 forced it before, at 2.06–2.07×); and **a genuinely reached low, frozen (FITX-1, row 52)**: the per-second coverage holds `L_ema` where it is and cannot lift it, so an unlocked LP that withdraws for real for 3–20 s (cranking at the drained depth, which the keeper reads too — nothing foreign), re-deposits and withdraw-wraps a crank every second keeps the spot leg (at `max(L_live, L_ema')`) and the EMA leg at that low, and `L_slow` follows the drained lows. On the fork (`freeze::fitx1_*`, a 20-s held drain) that forces both FITS-2 reproducers again — the 1 % position at 500 ‰ of its cap at 2.025× (+71 s), the cap-sized one after a 25-min freeze at 2.05× (+67 s) — and the 25-bps position at its open cap at 2.005–2.010×, where the honest keeper leaves them open; in the sim 1–5 hold levels at half the cap and below and at 25 bps, and 2.01–2.07× at 0.79–1 × the cap after 25 min – 1 h (ECON §12.12 (5b) (vii)). Since ★AIR-14 the sim also forces 0.79–1 × the cap from a 3-s held drain on, and the 640- and 792-SOL pools' caps (1.95–2.03× against 2.039×; 1.85–1.95× against 2.082× after a 20-s hold). It is bounded by the LP's withdrawal for good: every forced liquidation is one the honest keeper makes when the same LP withdraws at +1 s and stays out (the fork: the same second, price and buyback cost; the sim: 181 of 181 levels since ★AIR-14, 69 of 69 before, never earlier) — the attacker saves having to keep its capital out after the held seconds. Closing it is an owner decision (O18; the analysis floors of ECON (5b) (vii): the spot leg also at `L_mhi` closes it but lets a capital deposit freeze hold a position 0.5–2 % above its threshold open while it lasts; at `min(L_mhi, L_slow)` it costs nothing measured but leaves the long freezes). A genuine withdrawal delays a due liquidation by 0–3 s after a dip and 0–8 s under ±1 % noise (0–10 s before the AI review's fixes). At a 1 % pool's open cap it waited for `L_slow` (V2-14); since ★AIR-14's cap at `D` it is liquidated at the drained depth (ECON §12.12 (5b) (vi)). ★AIR-14 thus moved this residual both ways; the owner accepted it (O18) on the figures before the AI review's fixes, and AIR-14's widening on 2026-10-13 (SPEC §14 fourteenth round). The attacker pays one transaction a second and holds the pool's unlocked LP; λ ≈ 1 Raydium pools have nothing to withdraw — a canonical PumpSwap pool does not have that protection: its creation LP is burned (λ = 1), but anyone can deposit and withdraw (row 56; ECON §1.2, §12.12 residual 16).
11. **Evidence.** The sims (ECON §12.12, `switch_warmup.py` parts 4d, 4e, 5b, 11) and the LiteSVM regressions on the fork (§8.2 ★T-SWITCH-CONFIRM: `m4r_it`, `switch_confirm_it`, `m4v_it`, `m4_sec_it`, `pool_select_it::carried_fit`, the keeper scenarios `freeze::*` and `pool_select::*`, with the M4R verification's M4X-1–3, row 50's FIT / FITV regressions, row 51's FITS regressions and row 52's pinned FITX-1 residual, `freeze::fitx1_*`); CU as measured in `m3_cu` (§6.1).
12. **No candidate fits (#99).** A halted market whose positions no eligible candidate can carry stays halted: healthy positions are frozen at the pre-halt `P_ema` until their deadline and settle S3 at fair value then (the expiry fee as `p'`, O15; ECON §10.3's frozen rows: lenders +6.9–7.1 % over `q` at that price, −46 % against the rows' 2× move), liquidatable ones after the S3 chain — the O14 exposure, which the owner accepts for positions a thinner pool cannot carry.
13. **Where the fit is judged (#99; FIT-1, row 50).** At the frozen `P_ema` at the execution, without the candidate's live `X`: after a genuine `k`× pump during the halt a carried position can be up to `λ·√k` × a native open's cap on the adopted pool — the honest proposal, which reads `X_cand`, refuses it, but a dump wrapped around the proposal lifts `X_cand` for two swap fees and the execution adopts (the fork: q/cap 1.085 / 1.109 / 1.366 at `k` 1.2 / 1.5 / 1.9) — and it is that much nearer its own liquidation (liquidated under the pushes within 1 s of the control, `freeze::fit1_*`); after a genuine dump a position the new pool could carry at the live price can still be refused and settle S3 at the pre-dump `P_ema` (lender-favourable) (ECON §12.12 residual 13).
14. **The mark (FIT-3, row 50).** `max_q_hwm` bounds every open `q` and resets only when `open_positions` reaches 0: one borrower opening at the incumbent's size cap and closing a second later (0.013401 SOL on the fork) keeps a thinner candidate that every open position and their OI fit refused (`CarriedPositionsTooLarge`) while any position stays open. The positions then settle S3 at fair value, each at its own deadline (the S3 timer, at most the tier's term after its open: 30 / 14 / 7 days at A / B / C; `carried_fit::fit3_*` on the fork: exactly at the deadline, lenders at FV), and because the fit bounds `q` by `min(max_q_hwm, ΣB_Q)` the next proposal carries the rest once those exits bring `ΣB_Q` under the candidate's per-position cap (ECON §12.12 (11) (e): adopted at +19.00 d instead of +210 s). The owner accepts this fallback. #100's first answer, a permissionless `refresh_max_q`, was withdrawn: anyone could reset its shared scan between the keeper's chunks (FITV-1).
15. **A switch between pools of the same high fee (FIT-2 at the impact cap; row 50) — closed by row 51 (FITS-1).** `min(φ_inc, φ_cand)` changed nothing when the incumbent's fee is at least the candidate's: a 1 %→1 % switch carried up to the candidate's 2.47 % impact cap, on a margin posted on the deeper incumbent's cost, and at 60–100 % of that limit (1.48–2.46 % of `X`) a genuine 4×/30 s pump under FIT-2's pushes ended in S1 on the fork (lenders −4.716 to −7.824 SOL; row 50 had 70–100 % from the sim). Since row 51 the carried fee caps take at most `CARRIED_FEE_CAP_PPM` = 2,500: those positions open no window and settle S3 at fair value (residual 12), and one at the new limit is liquidated within 0–1 s of the control under every push (ECON §12.12 (11) (d) (iii)).
