## 5. Liquidation and settlement paths

### 5.1 Keeper and program decision tree (per position, every second near a threshold)

```
if market.venue == PumpMigrating:
    keeper : pump migrate_v2 top-level in its own transaction (A15); then crank_price → PumpSwap
             (M5 as built: the → PumpSwap transition is M6's and the keeper's migrate duty is off by default, §7.1)
    program: liquidate / expire / S1 / S2 revert VenueMigrating; S3 only after max_migration_pause_s (§5.3)
elif !venue_executable(market):                          # halted pool, admin disable, vault below counters, reader failure
    keeper : crank_price every ≤ 30 s (continuous S3 chain); Raydium: after pool_fail ≥ 120 s, propose the deepest
             eligible candidate and execute the fast path when its 60 s window closes (§2.6; it adopts only while the
             chain that armed the window holds, M4-SEC-2, else cancels and the keeper proposes again once re-armed)
    program: sol_settle(S3) once the timer allows and the position is liquidatable or expired;
             healthy positions stay frozen (close impossible) until the route returns or their deadline (§5.3)
elif s3_no_route(market):                                 # executable venue, but route-broken flag or fee > min(global hard
                                                          #   cap, market.min_open_hard_cap_bps) (AIR-19)
    keeper : as usual (closes, liquidations, expiries and settlements run where their bounds allow);
             crank every ≤ 30 s so the S3 chain stays continuous; fee > global hard cap also feeds pool_fail on Raydium
    program: sol_settle(S3) for positions liquidatable (spot leg evaluated normally) or expired that have no route now
             (fee > min(global cap, the position's locked cap), or the flag), once the timer allows;
             the amount must be box-consistent
elif market.ema_warm > 0:                                 # PROPOSED, M4R: post-change warm-up on an executable venue
    keeper : crank_price every second until ema_warm == 0 (8 integrations after the adoption / price start)
    program: liquidate / expire fail EmaWarmingUp, sol_settle evaluates nothing, Raydium opens refused (§3.6–§3.8)
elif !liquidatable(pos) and !armed(pos):                  # nothing to do; keep observing (ECON §5.8)
                                                          # (to 1.0.0: `elif curve live && q > rT:` the straddle bundle with
                                                          #  complete_curve, §5.4; ★removed in 1.0.1, pump-final §7: such a
                                                          #  position follows the branches below on B̂_v3 — buyback_allowed
                                                          #  and σ included, C5 — and its liquidate / expire completes the
                                                          #  curve by synthetic migration in one instruction; the keeper then
                                                          #  sends migrate_v2 and the transition in the same tick)
elif lb stale (lb_sec < now − ref_max_age_s):             # crank_price this second, act next second
elif normal buyback allowed (B̂_live + ert ≤ V − K_s ∧ σ_live ≤ σ_max):
    if now ≥ deadline && !cr_liquidatable:  expire()      # when B̂_live ≤ max_in (expiry reference, δ_exp); else retry next second
    else:                                   liquidate()   # when B̂_live ≤ max_in (fixed δ_liq = 2 %), via Jito bundle; retry on ExitBoundNotMet
else:                                                     # S1/S2 legs hold, or the position is armed: sol_settle every second;
                                                          #   it arms, keeps the clock, disarms only on box-robust evidence,
                                                          #   settles (kind chosen at execution) or waits for a consistent amount
```

A keeper's `liquidate`, `expire` or `sol_settle` for a market is that second's observation for the market; it sends no separate crank (§7.1).

### 5.2 Waterfalls

These are ECON §8 exactly. Each is a pure `math::waterfall` function whose legs are non-negative and sum to `V` (property-tested, ECON I-E4). All keeper, split, fee and rent-share terms are the position's **locked** values. `B` is the measured spend; `r = min(R_due, V − B)`; `base = min(B̂_live,risk, B̂_ref)` (quotes, never the measured spend).

| Path | Order of payment from `V` |
|---|---|
| **close** | 1. `B` (`max_in = min(max_buyback_cost, V − R − ert)`). 2. `R_due`: `⌊R·rent_protocol_bps_pos/10⁴⌋` to protocol, the rest to lenders. 3. Remainder to the borrower |
| **liquidate** | 1. `B` (`max_in` of §3.6). 2. `r` (split as in close). 3. Penalty `π = min(⌈p·base/10⁴⌉, V − B − r)`: keeper `⌊π·keeper_split/10⁴⌋`, protocol `⌊π·protocol_split/10⁴⌋`, lenders the rest (vests). 4. **Keeper floor** `top = min(max(0, K_s − ⌊π·keeper_split/10⁴⌋), V − B − r − π)` to the keeper, paid by the borrower (A74; R3B-10). 5. Remainder to the borrower |
| **expire** | 1. `B` (expiry `max_in`). 2. `r`. 3. Expiry fee `e = min(⌈expiry_fee_bps·base/10⁴⌉, V − B − r)`, 100 % lenders (vests). 4. **Keeper** `K_e = min(expiry_keeper_fixed + ⌊expiry_keeper_bps·B̂_ref/10⁴⌋, expiry_keeper_cap, V − B − r − e)`. 5. Remainder to the borrower |
| **settle** | 1. `K_s` to the keeper. 2. Lenders `x`: S1 `V − K_s`; S2/S3 `x(P_ema, L_ema) = min(V − K_s, FV)` if box-consistent (§4.5); of any take (S1, S2, S3), `x − min(x, ⌊Q·P′/WAD⌋ + R_due)` vests, `P′ = P_ema`, or 0 when the venue cannot execute (AIR-21, AIR-09). 3. `V − K_s − x` to the borrower. The protocol gets nothing (SPEC §6.3) |

- **Senior in the bound: an expiry's rent and fee, not a liquidation's** (C0-1 (3); v0.4.1, R4A-1, R4B-1). An expiry's buyback may exceed `V − R − π_ref − ert` only if the fair reference cost itself does (`max(V − R − π_ref − ert, B̂_ref·(1 + ε))`, ECON §8.2), so a sandwich cannot truncate rent or expiry fee wherever the reference leaves room (I-E2). A liquidation reserves nothing (§3.6): a reserve there blocks honest liquidations in fast pumps; a sandwich or held attacker can take rent and penalty up to the bound's slack (I-E3; 22 of 697 exits in the exit fuzz, ECON §13; 22 of 709 before AIR-22), and the held model's larger truncation on aged positions is disclosed (§8.5, O19). The payment order of SPEC §5.2 is unchanged.
- **Keeper floor** (A74; N22, owner visibility). The SPEC keeper share of a small liquidation is below the settlement reward `K_s`, so a third-party keeper would rather let a small position gap into S1 (a lender loss). The top-up closes that; it is zero above the crossover vaults (≈ 5.0 SOL Tier A, 1.8 B, 1.7 C, 1.4 D) and never exceeds what the borrower would lose in S1 (ECON §8.5).
- Lender credits go to `market_vault` (`vault.lender_sol += …`) through `pool::repay` / `pool::settle` (rent true-up against `receivable`; a negative Δ is a shortfall debit; lumps and ★the positive rent top-up vest, M10-8C-1). Protocol credits go to `vault.protocol_fees`.
- **A18: the borrower is paid through the position close.** The borrower remainder is never pushed as a separate transfer; it stays on the `ShortPosition` account, which is closed to `borrower`, so the borrower also recovers the account rent and the credit is always ≥ the rent-exempt minimum (a 0-lamport borrower cannot block its own liquidation) [V4; C0 verified].

### 5.3 SOL settlement conditions, routes and the S3 timer

- **S1 / S2** are as in §3.8 and §4.5: triple-leg (live, robust spot, and the settlement box), S1 whenever its legs hold (D3), and persistence (one eligibility clock held for `settle_persist_n` EMA updates, so ≥ 39 s, reset only by box-robust evidence).
- **Three route predicates, each with one job** (A23 as amended, A50, A71; C0-4, C0-10, V2-1, R3A-4, R3B-8):
  - **`venue_executable`** = the venue predicate in the table below (and all venue-state accounts parse, A63). It alone drives `B̂_live`, closes, liquidations, expiries, the "no route ⇒ spot leg true" rule and observation recording (A64).
  - **`s3_no_route`** = `!venue_executable ∨ market.route_broken ∨ venue_route_broken[venue] ∨ φ_live > min(config.venue_fee_hard_cap_bps, market.min_open_hard_cap_bps)` (★AIR-19; the mark 0 = unset: the global cap alone). It feeds only the S3 chain and the open gate. `sol_settle`'s "no route now" is the position's own, `route::position_no_route`: the same with the position's locked `venue_fee_hard_cap_bps` in place of the mark, so a fee above that cap is no route for the position under any global cap, and a fee within it stays a route for it however low the mark.
  - **`pool_fail`** = `!venue_executable ∨ φ_live > config.venue_fee_hard_cap_bps` (Raydium). It feeds only the fast-path chain `pool_fail_since` / `last_pool_fail_obs` (§2.6). It never reads the Emergency flag.
  - `pool_fail` uses the **global** hard cap; the S3 chain the lower of it and the market's mark, a position's "no route now" the lower of it and the position's locked cap; every risk quote and FV use the position's locked value (R3A-4 c; A26). **Why (AIR-19):** a position's keeper exits are bounded at its own locked cap and its S1 legs priced there, so after Governance raises the global cap above a position's locked cap, a fee between the two counted as a route under the global cap alone: the chain never started, `expire` / `liquidate` refused `ExitBoundNotMet`, and an expired healthy position had no exit at all. The mark is conservative by design (a closed position may have set it; it resets only when the market empties): the S3 chain can start at a fee that is still a route for every open position — they keep their route and settle nothing, and one whose own cap the fee later passes counts `s3_wait_s` from the chain's earlier start (accepted by the owner on 2026-10-12 rather than tracking each cap exactly, which needs more state; known issues).
  - T-S3-BROKEN asserts that with the flag set the set of liquidatable positions, every close outcome and the `pool_fail` chain equal those of the unflagged run, and that the flag only adds S3 for positions liquidatable (spot leg evaluated normally) or expired.

  The venue predicates:

| Venue | Venue predicate | Source |
|---|---|---|
| PumpCurve | `!curve.complete` | [R-PUMP §7] |
| PumpMigrating | false | SPEC §5.3 |
| PumpSwap | canonical pool valid ∧ `pool_base_vault.amount > 0` ∧ `!(disable_flags & PAMM_BUY_DISABLED_BIT)` where the bit is a **compile-time constant set from test gate T-DISABLE** (a hard gate before M6 closes). Until then, and for any unknown non-zero flag afterwards, `disable_flags ≠ 0` blocks opens and alerts but is **not** S3 evidence; a real halt reaches S3 through the Emergency route-broken flag (A24; C0-10). **T-DISABLE resolved (M6, on the dumped ELF; R-VEN Update H4): `PAMM_BUY_DISABLED_BIT = 1 << 3`** (bit 3 halts `buy`, `buy_exact_quote_in`, `boost_buy_and_burn`; bit 4 `sell`, bit 0 `create_pool`, bits 1 / 2 `deposit` / `withdraw`, bits 5–7 nothing; the admin's `disable` writes bits 0–4 only). As built also: every `GlobalConfig`, `FeeConfig` and boost-ATA account parses, the pool's vaults are the cached ones, `vault + VQR ∈ (0, u64::MAX]`, and the fee resolves on the mint's supply | [R-VEN §7; V6 of v0.1; Update H4] |
| RaydiumV4 | `(status ∈ {1, 6} ∨ (status == 7 ∧ now ≥ pool_open_time))` ∧ `coin_vault ≥ need_take_pnl_coin` ∧ `pc_vault ≥ need_take_pnl_pc`. Status values above 7 revert in the venue, so they are "no route" | [R-RAY §5.3] |
| RaydiumCpmm | `(status & 0b100) == 0 ∧ now ≥ open_time` ∧ `vault_i ≥ protocol_i + fund_i + creator_i` for both sides ∧ (`t + c_eff > 0` ∨ the creator fee is not on the buy's input): at `t + c_eff = 0` with the fee on the input every buy reverts `ZeroTradingTokens` (`update_amm_config` accepts `t = 0`; M3-SEC-1) | [R-RAY §5.3] |
| None | false | — |

  A "no route" that exists only for one position (`Q ≥ X`) is S2 territory, not S3. The Raydium predicates come from source, not from guesses [R-RAY §5.3]; today none of 705,975 AMM v4 pools and 236,265 CPMM pools is swap-disabled.
- **Venue interface breakage (C0-4 (d); V1-8, V2-6).** If a venue changes its interface so that our CPI fails, every exit reverts and the failure cannot be recorded on-chain. The keeper detects it in simulation, alerts, and pages the Emergency multisig, which publishes an extras template set (additive change, including new per-mint or per-pool PDAs) or (once O6 is recorded) sets the route-broken flag, which starts the S3 chain. If the change breaks the layout of a venue-*state* account instead, `crank_price` and `sol_settle` see "not executable" (A63) and the chain starts by itself. Test gates: T-REPLAY-0428 replays pump's 2026-04-28 account change against the exit paths with extras configured; T-REPLAY-PDA adds a synthetic "new per-mint PDA remaining account" change and recovers it with a template; T-S3-BROKEN checks that a flagged route reaches S3 after `s3_wait_s` and changes nothing else.
- **Liveness without a route (V2-5; disclose).** While the venue cannot execute — an AMM v4 admin halt (status 2–5, or 7 with a future open time), a CPMM status bit, a venue interface break — **no position can close**, **liquidatable positions reach S3 after the chain**, and **healthy positions stay frozen until the route returns or their deadline** (up to 30 days for Tier A): S3 requires "liquidatable" (SPEC §5.3), the halted pool is no longer observed, so the EMA leg cannot fire from price moves elsewhere. At the deadline the position is expired and liquidatable, S3 applies and FV is priced at the last pre-halt `P_ema` (the event reports its age); if the token rose elsewhere meanwhile, a borrower who would have been underwater can still receive `V − K_s − FV`. The Raydium fast path helps only if another eligible pool exists: of Fartcoin's nine Raydium SOL pools only the adopted `Bzc9NZfM…` (38,176 SOL real, λ 0.9978) is eligible [V15], so one 2-of-3 admin action [V14; R-RAY §5.1] freezes every Fartcoin position until its deadline. Options that shorten the bound are owner decisions (§10, O14); none is in the MVP default.
- **Continuous timer (C0-16; ECON §10.3).** Every prologue observes `s3_no_route`. On a no-route observation: if `no_route_since == 0` or `now − last_no_route_obs > S3_OBS_GAP_S` (60 s, a constant), set `no_route_since = now`; always set `last_no_route_obs = now`. Any observation with a route clears both. S3 is allowed iff the position is liquidatable (spot and EMA legs; the spot leg is true without evaluation only if the venue is not executable) or expired, `s3_no_route` holds **now**, the chain is unbroken, and

  ```
  now ≥ max(no_route_since, graduated_at + grad_grace_s, migration_seen_at + max_migration_pause_s·[venue == PumpMigrating]) + s3_wait_s
                                                                     (the position's locked grad_grace_s, max_migration_pause_s, s3_wait_s)
  ```

  The in-house keeper cranks every market without a route at least every 30 s (§7.1). A lender-keeper that cranks only during outages can no longer add up separate outages (ECON §10.3 self-test: S3 moves from 600 s to 1,020 s).
- **Graduation in progress** (SPEC §5.3): all liquidation-class instructions pause while `PumpMigrating`; rent accrues and the EMA keeps integrating the completed curve's price. Anyone (including our keeper) can call `migrate_v2`, so the pause is normally 0–6 slots [R-PUMP §7.4]. If migration never completes, S3 becomes possible `max_migration_pause_s + s3_wait_s` (70 min) after `migration_seen_at` (ADOPTED Q5). After graduation, S3 cannot start until `graduated_at + grad_grace_s`; the graduation rewrites the ring's liquidity (A72), so the settlement box is not widened by the curve's larger `√(vT·vQ)`. ★Since 1.0.1 such an S3's FV prices the pool `migrate_v2` will create — ρ-scaled after a synthetic pool part — and is **undefined** when the curve's post-complete fields are not known, so the lenders then get the whole take: the one exception to A63's cap-only view, whose "FV at the last pre-halt `P_ema`" above otherwise stands (§4.5; PUMP-2026-10-13-1).

### 5.4 Graduation-specific cases

1. **Buyback completes the curve** (`q == rT`; ★since 1.0.1 `q ≥ rT`): allowed; the venue becomes `PumpMigrating` after the leg (ECON §10.2).

★**Since 1.0.1 (pump-final; owner D1 (a), D2, D3 of 2026-10-13) case 2 is one instruction.** pump's 2026-10-08 build buys past `rT` by **synthetic migration**: `buy_v3(q, max_in)` takes `rT` from the curve and `q − rT` from the would-be PumpSwap pool `(curve_base_ata − rT, rQ + n₁ − fee)`, both parts at the curve's fee, all or nothing, and completes the curve (`pcB`, `pcQ` written). short.win trades every curve leg on v3, so a close, liquidation or expiry of `q > rT` is an ordinary exit priced `B̂_v3` (§4.3) that completes the curve and moves the market to `PumpMigrating` in the same instruction (`sync_after_leg`, `migration_seen_at = now`, `VenueStateChanged`); the keeper then sends `migrate_v2` (still top-level, A15) and the transition in the same tick, and the market's other positions exit on the pool after the warm-up. σ is judged on `B̂_v3` at once (above `σ_max`: S2, C5). A buyback beyond the would-be pool (`q − rT ≥ X_s`) is unreachable under the per-market cap (C8); a close refuses it `CurveStraddle`, a keeper exit gets `UseSolSettle`. A curve trade between the keeper's read and its exit is re-quoted at execution and lands within `max_in` or reverts (pump 6002 / `ExitBoundNotMet`); a third party's completion first makes the exit refuse `VenueMigrating` with no state change. Under a `create_pool` halt (PumpSwap bit 0) a synthetic exit still runs and completes the curve; the market's other positions then wait in `PumpMigrating` until the migration resumes or S3 at 70 min on the post-buy pool's FV (§4.5; T-MIG-HALT), as after a third party's completion. Tested: T-SYNTH-1 … -6, T-SIGMA, T-MIG-* (§8.2). **Measured** (pump-final P3, §6.1): a synthetic `close_short` 135.8 k CU, the keeper's `[CB ×2, crank, liquidate]` past `rT` 184,881 CU (worst ring 192,601) and `[…, expire]` 188,021, 12 trace entries for the exit, peak height 3. The straddle bundle below, its helper `complete_curve` (A66) and the keeper's `Plan::Straddle` are **retired** (D2; the M5 / M6 text stays as the 1.0.0 record).

2. **Straddle** (curve live, `q > rT`; A14, ADOPTED Q14, C1-1, R3B-11; ★1.0.0 only, superseded above). Pump rejects any buy above `rT` (6021) and never fills partially [R-PUMP §7.3] — unless the caller appends pump's undocumented trailing cap byte (R-PUMP Update U7), which short.win's adapter and the helper never send (§3.12). The MVP has no in-program two-leg execution. The keeper (or the borrower's client) sends a **Jito bundle of at least 3 transactions** (at most 5 per bundle, sequential, all-or-nothing, tip required [R-PUMP Review corrections 1]):
   - **tx1**: ComputeBudget ×2 + **`complete_curve(max_sol_cost)`** of the helper program (A66): it reads `rT` from the bonding curve **at execution**, and if the curve is not yet complete it CPIs pump `buy_v2(rT_live, max_sol_cost)` with the transaction's own signer as `user`; if the curve is already complete it succeeds as a no-op. v0.3's tx1 named `rT` as read before the bundle, so any curve trade that landed in between made pump reject the buy (6021) or left the curve incomplete for `migrate_v2`, and the bundle reverted while the price ran (R3B-11). The helper is a separate, stateless program (≈ 150 lines, no accounts of its own, audited with the core, Governance upgrade authority) because it forwards a user's signature to a venue, which the core program never does (A4). Stack: helper 1 → pump 2 → System/Token/pfee 3; ≈ 11 trace entries. **As built (M5; `programs/complete_curve`, ≈ 400 lines, Anchor 1.2.0, program id `4B5mGykX…`):** it takes exactly pump `buy_v2`'s 27 accounts in pump's order and forwards any trailing accounts unchanged (an additive pump interface change needs no helper upgrade); `user` must sign; the CPI target must be pump and executable (8000 `NotPump`), the curve pump-owned and parsing (8001 `BadCurve`) and the curve PDA of `base_mint` (Anchor seeds; needed because the no-op path makes no CPI, so pump never checks it there); a complete curve (or `rT = 0`) is a no-op with no CPI (`CurveAlreadyComplete`), otherwise `buy_v2(rT_live, max_sol_cost)` with exactly 24 bytes of data (no cap byte), after which the curve must be complete (8002 `NotCompleted`) and `CurveCompleted{tokens, lamports}` is emitted (`emit!` log events, no trace entries; errors offset 8000, so pump's 6002 through the helper is unambiguous). It never names a short.win account. Measured (T-STRADDLE, `straddle_it`): tx1 is **12** entries (the completing `buy_v2` is 9 with pump's completion event), 13 when pump creates the completer's UVA, 18 with the completer's ATA created in the same transaction, 3 as a no-op; 106–141 k CU (the helper's own logic ≈ 10.4 k; the no-op transaction 10.7 k), 667–763 B as v0 through A28 (`straddle_it` 667–708 B, the `m5_cu` bench's table 763 B).
   - **tx2**: ComputeBudget ×2 + `migrate_v2` top-level, with its 2 remaining boost accounts (51 + 2 = 53 entries, 54 with the tip on the bundle's last transaction; measured on the fork: peak height 4, 292–330 k CU — ECON T7/T8: 322–358 k on mainnet — and 896–912 B as v0); `migrate_v2` is idempotent (on an incomplete curve it fails with pump 6006; on a migrated one it is a no-op, 56.7 k CU, 4 entries, so the bundle survives a third party's migration). tx1 and tx2 merged, with the tip and the completer's UVA already existing, measure **exactly 64** entries (1,205 B, 440 k CU), one over the limit when pump also has to create the UVA: zero headroom, so they stay separate transactions.
   - **tx3**: ComputeBudget ×2 + pAMM `init_user_volume_accumulator(payer = keeper, user = trader)` if needed + `crank_price` (transition) + `liquidate` / `close_short` on PumpSwap (≈ 2 + 3 + 2 + 17 ≈ 24 entries), + the tip when it is the last transaction. No `extend_account` is required: the pool `migrate_v2` creates is 271 B and trades as such (R-VEN Update G4); the SDK extends it to 301 B first, and the M5 harness's tx3 stand-in did (the PumpSwap adapter must not require ≥ 300 B). **As built (M6; the delay accepted by the owner on 2026-09-30, OWNER-M6R-4, row 56; the tx3 bucket OWNER-M6SK-1, open):** the transition marks the post-change warm-up (§2.5), so a keeper `liquidate` / `expire` in tx3 fails `EmaWarmingUp` and reverts the whole bundle (tested). The keeper's tx3 is therefore ComputeBudget ×2 + the missing pool accounts (§3.12's existence requirement) + `crank_price` on the curve's ReadSet (the transition) + `crank_price` on the pool's ReadSet (the pool's first bucket, which nobody can wrap) + the tip: measured 17 entries, 86.5 k CU, 900 B v0 through A28 (30 accounts), 1,174 B without the ALT (since row 56's LP mint; M6 as built 83–91 k, 867 B / 29). Its exit lands at **T + 8** with a crank every second (T + 9 without tx3's own bucket, one second more per second with no observation). The **borrower's own** tx3 — the accounts, the transition crank and its `close_short` (the warm-up gates keeper exits only) — lands inside the bundle and buys at exactly `B̂_str` (604,827,436 lamports; 30 entries, 229 k CU, 1,077 B v0; the `m6_cu` form without the accounts 23 entries, 1,096 B).
   - Pricing uses `B̂_str` on-chain (§4.3, V1-9): the position buys all of `Q` on the post-migration pool, which is exactly tx3, so CR, S1, S2 and the exit bounds describe the path that executes. The γ = 50 % open cap makes straddles rare (ECON §10.2); since M5-SEC-3 it reads the curve's reserves at the EMA price (§4.6), so a sale wrapped around the open cannot lift it. Completing the curve is self-financing for the keeper (it keeps the `rT` tokens and can sell them after the +45.66 % boost push) [ECON §10.1].
   - **Keeper fallback** (V1-9): if tx3 would fail (its simulation returns `UseSolSettle`, `ExitBoundNotMet` or `InsufficientVault`), the keeper sends tx1 + tx2 only and then treats the position as an ordinary PumpSwap position in the following seconds (crank, liquidate or `sol_settle`). **M5 (flagged):** with no tx3 and no `→ PumpSwap`, tx1 + tx2 would freeze the position in `PumpMigrating` instead of exiting it, so the M5 keeper sends them only with `send_without_exit` (default false) and otherwise calls `sol_settle` (§7.1); M6 revisits the default. **As built (M6):** tx3 holds no exit, so any tx3 pre-flight failure falls back to tx1 + tx2 followed at once by the keeper's own move onto the pool; `send_without_exit` defaults to true (§7.1). **T-STRADDLE, curve part — verified on the fork in M5** (`straddle_it`, 10 tests; keeper scenarios): tx1 completes a live curve at the `rT` it reads when it runs, to the lamport of pump's charge; it is a no-op on a curve a third party completed (before and after that curve's `migrate_v2`); the bundle lands with a buy, a sale, a third-party completion or a completion plus migration injected between the keeper's read and the bundle, `X_p` exactly as read, where v0.3's stale tx1 failed the whole bundle (6021 after a buy; pump 6006 at `migrate_v2` after a sale); `max_sol_cost` caps the spend (6002, nothing committed); the straddled position's close refuses `CurveStraddle`, the bundle leaves every short.win account unchanged, the next crank moves the market to `PumpMigrating`, and the venue leg of tx3 (a stand-in buyer's PumpSwap `buy` of `q`) costs exactly `B̂_str` (604,827,436 lamports, unchanged by a curve buy between the read and the bundle: the post-migration pool does not depend on the path and `X_p = curve_base_ata − rT` is invariant under curve trades). **Still UNVERIFIED:** the bundle's submission to a live block engine, and pre-flight of tx2 / tx3 on a plain RPC node. **M6 part verified** (`straddle_it` 13: `the_exit_on_the_pool_lands_exactly_at_the_warm_up_gate`, `the_three_transaction_bundle_survives_a_curve_trade_before_it`, the borrower's tx3 in `a_straddled_position_prices_the_bundle_it_waits_for`; `graduation_e2e::{econ_10_2_the_borrowers_own_bundle_closes_a_straddle, a_borrowers_self_made_straddle_is_liquidated_after_the_keepers_bundle}`; the keeper's `graduation` scenarios, including the fallback and a curve trade between its read and the bundle).
   - A `migrate_v2` CPI from inside short.win is rejected: the top-level call already reaches stack height 4, so a CPI'd one reaches exactly the maximum of 5 — it works (117 mainnet calls from other programs do, R-PUMP Update U8) but leaves no headroom (short.win itself could no longer be wrapped), and its 51 trace entries leave room for nothing else in the transaction, the binding reason (A15) [V2 of v0.1; R-PUMP Corrections 3].
   - v1.1 option: an in-program `ExitInProgress` state that buys `rT`, records the partial buyback and finishes on PumpSwap in a later instruction.
   - **What the M5 build cannot do (M5-SEC-4; why the curve bit is not enableable in it, §2.3.2).** Anyone, a borrower included, can complete a curve and run `migrate_v2` in **one** transaction (58 inner instructions, ≈ 412 k CU; roughly self-financing, the completer keeps the `rT` tokens), so short.win never observes the completed curve: without the `→ PumpSwap` transition the market stays `PumpMigrating`, exits refuse `VenueMigrating`, the EMA stays at the last curve price while the pool trades on (the reproducer: `P_ema` 1.625e14 against a pool at 6.164e14 after one PumpSwap buy, ×3.79), and only S3 at the deadline or on the frozen EMA pays FV at that frozen price. A borrower whose `q` is close to `rT` can also buy `rT − q + 1` to make its own position a straddle (`CurveStraddle` on the curve). M6's transition must cover both: the atomic, self-financed `[buy_v2(rT), migrate_v2]` with the pool at 3.79× the last curve EMA before any observation, and the self-made straddle, which the bundle must liquidate. The tripwire `m5_sec_4_tripwire_an_atomic_complete_and_migrate_freezes_an_m5_market` pins the M5 behaviour and M6 inverts it. **Closed in M6:** the transition runs in the first prologue that reads the valid pool (§2.5), `VENUE_BITS_UNFINISHED` is empty, and the tripwire is inverted as `m5_sec_curve_it::{m5_sec_4_m6_can_enable_the_curve_venue, m5_sec_4_an_atomic_complete_and_migrate_graduates_the_market_onto_its_pool}` (the pool pushed ≥ 3.5× the last curve EMA before any observation: → PumpSwap, liquidated on the pool only after ≥ 8 s). The atomic, self-financed attack on the fork (`graduation_e2e::the_atomic_self_financed_complete_and_migrate_is_liquidated_on_the_pool`: 407–418 k CU, the pool at 3.63×) is liquidated 9 s after the transition, the lenders get `Q` back plus 0.1018 SOL; the self-made straddle (`rT − q + 1`) is liquidated 9 s after the keeper's fallback bundle (`straddle_it`, `graduation_e2e`, the keeper's `graduation` scenarios).
3. **Boost window** (A13): opens are refused while `boost_vault.amount > boost_dust_lamports ∧ now < graduated_at + boost_window_s`. The boost is proportional (20.69 % of migrated SOL) and pushes the price ×1.4566 within ≈ 6 minutes; positions opened late on the curve that survive graduation are liquidated normally by that push [ECON §10.1]. There is no extra liquidation grace.
4. **Creator changes mid-position:** `creator_vault` is re-derived from the live curve or pool on every trade [R-PUMP §8]. **PumpSwap (M6-SEC-4, fixed):** pAMM's `set_coin_creator` and `migrate_pool_coin_creator` take no signer (U32), so anyone can move a pool's `coin_creator` to its metadata / curve creator or its sharing config (one way; `set_coin_creator` verified with only the fee payer signing on the dumped ELF, the pool ≥ 271 B). After such a change every PumpSwap trade fails `VenueAccountMismatch` until the new creator vault's WSOL ATA (T11) exists (the existence requirement, §3.12) — an exit already in flight fails once — and, until the cache is rewritten, every trade re-derives T11 / T12 (+3,077 CU per close even at the best bumps). As built: `crank_price` re-caches a changed creator (`pump_amm::refresh_coin_creator`, §3.9; 34,976 CU), and the keeper's liquidate / expire transaction starts with `create_idempotent(T11)` whenever the live creator differs from the cached one (`venue::pamm_creator_vault_prep`, §7.1 duty 3). pAMM's permissionless `transfer_creator_fees_to_pump` and `collect_coin_creator_fee` leave T11 in place (re-created inside the instruction), so T11 cannot be removed repeatedly. A one-time delay, not a lock (`pamm_it::creator::m6_sec_4_*`).

An admin fee hike between `venue_fee_cap_bps` and `venue_fee_hard_cap_bps` makes exits more expensive for borrowers (the venue charges it) but cannot inflate FV beyond the hard cap. This split of the value transfer is part of owner item O18 (§10); the alternative is FV at `min(current fee, fee at open)` [R-RAY §9.4].

## 6. Compute, instruction-trace and transaction-size budget

The math figures below are **measured** primitives of the current `shortwin-math` crate on SBF v3, multiplied by the number of calls each v0.4 procedure makes [V18]. Runtime and account-handling overhead was an **estimate** built from Agave's fixed costs [V19] — ★since measured for every instruction class (U4, M1–M7: `m1_cu`, `m2_cu`, `m3_cu`, `m5_cu`, `m6_cu`, `m7_keeper`; re-baselined after each M10 program batch). Venue CPI costs are measured on mainnet (research notes). Everything is replaced by Mollusk/LiteSVM measurements under the mainnet feature set (p-token) in the milestones that build each path; CI fails if a measured value exceeds the limit column (T-CU, T-CU-MATH, T-TRACE, T-SIZE).

### 6.1 Compute units

**Measured primitives** (sbpfv3, platform-tools v1.57, `shortwin-math` as built for M0 against v0.3; per call, loop overhead subtracted; Tier A PumpSwap magnitudes) [V18]:

| Primitive | CU | Primitive | CU |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mul_div` u128 fast path | 691 | `mul_div` 256-bit fallback (Knuth D) | 783 |
| `mul_div_u64` (via u128 division) | 267 | native u64 `a·b` then `div_ceil` | 76 |
| PumpSwap `buy_exact_out` (3 fee components) | 1,452 | CPMM / AMM v4 `buy_exact_out` | 1,872 / 959 |
| `reprice(L, P)` | 843 | `isqrt(X·Y)` u128 / via U256 | 734 / 624 |
| `rent::due` / `rent::credited_for` / `rent::accrue` | 1,287 / 2,637 / 1,109 | `record` + `integrate` (one EMA roll) | 2,990 |
| `obs_median` (8 + 8 values; v0.4.1 sorts 4 × 8 bucket extremes ≈ 3.2 k, by scaling) | 1,604 | `sigma_xy` | 1,473 |
| **EMA-leg entry, v0.3** (reprice + quote + CR) | **2,289** | **EMA-leg entry, v0.4** (cached `(x, y)` + quote + CR) | **1,468** |

Two consequences. First, R3B-3's projection of ≈ 0.9–1.0 M CU of math per liquidation assumed a bit-by-bit 256-bit divider (≈ 8.8 k CU per `mul_div` in the reviewer's bench); the crate never used one — it takes the u128 path first and falls back to Knuth D, which costs only 13 % more — so that projection does not apply. Second, what v0.4 removes is real but modest: caching the reprojection saves ≈ 820 CU per ring entry per position, and dropping the executable-run scan removes up to 8 more entries, so a worst-case liquidation's math falls from ≈ 67 k to ≈ 35 k CU.

**Math per instruction** (PumpSwap quotes, the costliest family on the pump path; `docs/design/arch/cu_budget.py` reproduces the numbers): prologue with a roll ≈ 11 k (accrue, vest release, lender credit, roll with the cached reprojection, spot price, `√(X·Y)`, fee tier); `open_short` ≈ 24 k; `close_short` ≈ 18 k; `liquidate` ≈ 35 k (v0.3 worst case ≈ 67 k); `expire` ≈ 32 k; `sol_settle` (armed, S2/S3 amount path: legs, box, refutation, three amount corners, pool settle) ≈ 46 k (v0.4.1: +1.6 k for the second pair of medians; `p'` per corner is one CR comparison each); `crank_price` ≈ 13 k; `deposit` / `withdraw` ≈ 12 k (`withdraw` + ≤ 1 k for `cal_advance`, which touches 0–1 buckets per day elapsed); `claim_sol` ≈ 3 k.

### 6.3 Stack depth (C1-8)

`MAX_INSTRUCTION_STACK_DEPTH = 5` (SIMD-0268 not active on mainnet) [R-RAY §4.3; C1-8]. short.win at height 1 → venue 2 → Token / System / pfee / event self-CPI 3. Pump's own CPIs sit exactly one level below pump [R-PUMP §6.7]; Raydium never creates accounts, so it always peaks at 3 [R-RAY §4.3]. PumpSwap `buy` creates missing fee ATAs through the ATA program (U7, resolved in M6: height 4, 13 trace entries), which would reach 4; the existence requirement of §3.12 prevents that path, so every leg peaks at 3 and **short.win keeps 2 spare levels** (it can itself be CPI'd once, e.g. by a Squads vault transaction). Without the existence requirement the headroom would be ≥ 1 level. short.win's own System/Token CPIs are at height 2. T-DEPTH runs every venue path through one wrapper level and checks that a missing fee ATA fails cleanly with `VenueAccountMismatch`. **Measured on Raydium (M3, `m3_cu` `depth.md`):** every trading path peaks at 3, so short.win can itself be CPI'd **twice** (peak 5); a third wrapper fails with `CallDepth`. `propose_pool` and `execute_pool_switch` make no CPI but the event self-CPI and peak at 2, so they run through three wrapper levels (peak 5; M4). **Measured on the curve (M5, `m5_cu` `depth.md`, `pump_it::pda`):** every curve leg and the curve listing (its ATA-program and pump-UVA CPIs) peak at 3, so two wrapper levels fit and a third fails with `CallDepth`, the helper's tx1 included. The curve's analog of the missing-fee-ATA check is the accounts pump would otherwise create under short.win's CPI: a missing trader UVA fails `VenueAccountMismatch`, a missing `trader_base_ata` `TraderStateInvalid`, both before pump runs, direct and wrapped; the fee recipients' WSOL ATAs need not exist for SOL coins. A top-level `migrate_v2` peaks at 4 (5 when CPI'd, A15). **Measured on PumpSwap (M6, `m6_cu` `depth.md`):** every PumpSwap leg and a PumpSwap listing peak at 3, so two wrapper levels fit (peak 5) and a third fails `CallDepth`; `sol_settle`, the `→ PumpSwap` transition crank, `sweep_trader` and the latch peak at 2 and fit three. The existence requirement keeps pAMM's ATA-program path (height 4 under short.win, R-VEN Update H6) out of every leg: a missing fee ATA fails `VenueAccountMismatch` before pAMM runs (`pamm_it::refusals::the_existence_requirement`).

### 6.4 Transaction size and account locks

Limits: 1,232 B for legacy/v0 transactions; 64 accounts per transaction (the lock-limit increase is not activated); v1 transactions (4,096 B, no ALTs, 64 inline addresses) are live since slot 447,120,000 [R-JUP §3.1; C1 verified].

**A28:** v0 + one **protocol ALT** holding the static accounts: programs (pump, pAMM, pfee, AMM v4, CPMM, Token, T22, ATA, System, ComputeBudget is top-level and stays static, short.win event authority); WSOL mint; pump `global`, `event_authority`, `fee_config`, GVA; pAMM `global_config`, `event_authority`, `fee_config`, GVA; the AMM v4 and CPMM authorities; the 21 CPMM `AmmConfig`s; `config`, `venue_guard`, `oracle_cache`; the 8 + 8 pump and 8 + 8 PumpSwap fee/buyback recipients and their WSOL ATAs. The venue ProgramData accounts left the ALT: only `flag_venue_upgraded` and `revalidate_venue` read them. Pump's own ALT `Hyif6eWb…` may be combined [R-PUMP §6.8]. Per-market accounts stay inline; top-level program ids must be static keys.

The alternative that costs no bytes — reading the LP mint once, at the listing, and caching the burned LP count (it can only grow) — cannot cover a graduation: the transition runs on the curve's ReadSet, and a deposit between `migrate_v2` and the transition would be cached as burned (row 56; ECON #105).

**★M7 as measured (T-SIZE's batch size; the real keeper's builder, `tests/bench/m7_keeper`):** crank batches per transaction — **v1** (all keys inline, 4,096 B, 64 addresses) at most 8 PumpSwap (2,338 B / 63 accounts), 9 AMM v4 (2,208 B / 59), 9 CPMM (2,249 B / 60), 11 curve (2,445 B / 64), 9 mixed (2,382 B / 64); a v1 batch of 6 is 1,368–1,840 B / 35–49 accounts on every venue and the mix; **v0 through A28** 3 PumpSwap (1,003 B), 4 AMM v4 (1,109 B), 4 CPMM (1,114 B), 5 curve (1,181 B), 4 mixed (1,121 B); **v0 through A28 plus a table per market** 8 / 9 / 9 / 10, mixed 8 (764–906 B, ≤ 64 accounts: the account limit binds). The keeper keeps `batch_v1` = 6 and `batch_v0` = 4 size-packed (a PumpSwap v0 batch is cut at 3): a larger v1 batch write-locks more `Market`s, so one congested market holds up more observations. **That v1 transactions land on mainnet (U25) is still UNVERIFIED**; `shortwin-v1-probe --rpc <url> --keypair <funded> --send` (≈ 10,000 lamports) settles it. **OWNER-M7-1 (the PumpSwap 4-extras open over A28), measured on 3 pools with the tables built on chain by the keeper's `alt` module** (`tsize_pumpswap.md`): only the first-time borrower's open **with a separate fee payer** is over A28 as enumerated (1,238–1,239 B); through the table `shortwin-build-alt create` / `scripts/build-alt.sh` builds — A28 plus the four `VenueExtras` PDAs, this section's "flagged addition" — it is 1,207–1,208 B (24–25 B spare); a borrower paying its own fee 1,142–1,143 B through A28 (fits); the keeper's liquidation 1,131–1,132 B and its `[crank, liquidate]` 1,156–1,157 B through A28 (fit); with the market's own table (`shortwin-build-alt market`: 21 addresses — the market's accounts, its pool's ReadSet and trade extras, the 4 extras keys — rent 4,348,480 lamports at mainnet's 5,080 lamports per byte, ≈ 0.0043 SOL, recoverable on close; 17 hand-picked addresses 3,698,240) the open is 590–622 B and v0 PumpSwap crank batches hold 8. **Recommendation (no program change):** make the build-alt table the normative A28 (it adds the four `VenueExtras` PDAs); the per-market table is the fallback; capping PumpSwap extras at 3 (P6) is unnecessary and not built.

### 6.5 ProgramData reads (C1-15)

The venue ProgramData accounts are 10,485,760 B (pump, pAMM), 948,989 B (pfee), 1,406,429 B (AMM v4) and 793,869 B (CPMM) [V9]; account-data direct mapping is not active on mainnet, so an instruction that lists one copies it into its input region. v0.3 read them in every `open_short` (and designed a per-slot `VenueSlots` mirror as the fallback). v0.4 reads them **only** in `flag_venue_upgraded` and `revalidate_venue`, i.e. once per venue upgrade, so the copy cost no longer matters for opens and the mirror, its per-slot writer and `venue_sync_max_age_slots` are gone (A7; decision 4). The copy is not metered: both instructions cost 6,032 / 8,440 CU on 0.79 MB, 1.4 MB and 10 MiB alike (M3, U5 verified for CU; 6,036–6,046 / 8,506–8,521 on the AIR build), so the 400 k request can drop to ≈ 20 k; a keeper that sets `SetLoadedAccountsDataSizeLimit` must still cover 10 MiB. ★**AIR-01:** nothing is hashed without an extension; after one, the instruction that tells it from an upgrade — a flag of a fingerprinted venue, or a revalidation at a later slot — hashes the trimmed ELF (`sol_sha256`, ≈ 0.5 CU per byte) after finding its end in the zero tail (`sol_memcmp_`, ≈ 1 CU per 250 B): ≤ 0.44 M CU measured (pump-fees 438,358 and CPMM 369,393 after one 10 KiB extension; AMM v4 with a 9.7 MB zero tail 210,386); pump-fees grown near the 10 MiB cap by a griefer's extensions (§8.5 (g)) would need ≈ 0.48 M by the same cost model (estimated, not measured). The flagger or the Emergency executor sizes its limit by simulation, at most 1.4 M (a trimmed ELF above 2 MiB is not hashed and counts as an upgrade).

### 6.6 Per-account write-lock budget (C0-17)

Leaders charge each transaction's requested CU against a per-writable-account block limit of **40,000,000 CU** on mainnet: Agave's `MAX_WRITABLE_ACCOUNT_UNITS` (24 M) scaled ×100/60 under the feature `raise_block_limits_to_100m` (`P1BCUMpA…`, active since slot 435,888,000; block limit 100 M), in Agave master (`runtime/src/slot_params.rs` `cost_limits`) and Firedancer (`fd_cost_tracker.c`; SIMD-0306's pack bound 40 M) alike [V10, ★re-checked M10; U16]. v0.4.1 and M7 read the bare 24 M constant: the figures below are restated for 40 M. Every trading instruction, `crank_price` and `sol_settle` write-lock `Market`, so about 28 transactions requesting 1.4 M CU could saturate a market for a block (17 at 24 M). Mitigations:

- `claim_sol`, `cover_deficit`, `sync_lender` and `add_margin` do not write-lock `Market` (lender SOL counters, the pot and the lock state live on `MarketVault`, A9). **This isolates lender claims from `Market` only** (V1-6): every exit and `open_short` also write-lock `MarketVault`, so claims still compete with liquidations for that account's 40 M CU per block, and the permissionless `crank_price` write-locks `Market`. A claim needs ≈ 8–20 k CU (§6.1; v0.4 said 25–50 k here, R4A-10 c), so saturating `MarketVault` takes ≈ 2,000–5,000 claims in one block at the keeper's priority price (≈ 1,200–3,000 at 24 M); the effective mitigation is the priority policy below and T-CASCADE, not the account split. A dedicated claims account that exits never touch was considered and not adopted: it would need a second SOL float and a periodic sweep between the two, for a contention that costs an attacker ≈ the whole block budget per slot.
- Keepers request tight CU limits (simulated × 1.1), escalate priority fees under contention, and submit liquidations in Jito bundles (§7.1).
- A market-censoring attacker must fill the 40 M CU budget every slot: ≈ 800× the keeper's per-slot crank cost at the same priority price (≈ 480× at the 24 M v0.4.1 assumed; ECON §12.6).
- **T-CASCADE (★M7, done; `tests/bench/m7_cascade`, `services/keeper-litesvm` `cascade`).** Baskets of minimum-notional positions (≈ 0.1 SOL, one borrower each) filling the 25-SOL launch cap — 246 on the mock venue, 245 on the PumpSwap `mature` fork (the costliest `liquidate`, ≈ 214 k requested CU on 1.0.1) — under `cascade.py`'s paths (a ×3 gap held, pumps ×3 over 60 s, ×3 and ×10 over 10 minutes), the keeper ticking every slot, each transaction's **requested** limit charged per slot against every account it write-locks. Without a policy the keeper asked one `Market` for 25.9 M CU in one slot (246 liquidations; PumpSwap 23.0 M), above the 24 M limit M7 assumed (under the 40 M that applies, ★M10, U16). **The keeper's policy (as built, §7.1 duty 14):** per market and slot it books its exits' requested CU against `market_cu_per_slot` (12 M, half the account's budget at the 24 M M7 assumed, 30 % of the 40 M that applies, so other writers of the market keep room) and every transaction against `payer_cu_per_slot` (20 M, since every keeper transaction write-locks its fee payer); the first exit of a slot always goes, the rest wait for the next slot, most under-collateralised first. Measured with it: peak 11.8–11.99 M CU on the `Market` (and `MarketVault`, pool vault, venue pool) per slot; the mock basket clears in 2 slots (113 liquidations a slot), PumpSwap in 5 (57 a slot); every basket within 1 s of the uncapped run and ≤ 2 s after its first exit; the S1 basket (the ×3 gap) settles 246 positions in 2 slots. At 12 M per market-slot that is 106 mock / 56 PumpSwap / 62 curve / 113 AMM v4 / 95 CPMM liquidations a slot — a 250-position basket in 3–5 slots. ★Re-measured on 1.0.1 (pump-final P8, `tests/bench/m7_cascade`): the same clearing times; 107 mock / 55 PumpSwap / **81 curve** (its `liquidate` 147 k since pump's v3 adapter, 192 k before) / 114 AMM v4 / 96 CPMM liquidations a slot, a 250-position basket in 3–5 slots. **Residual (OWNER-M7-8):** `payer_cu_per_slot` counts exits only; crank batches sent in the same slot also write-lock the fee payer (200 markets all due ≈ 34 v1 batches × ≈ 162 k ≈ 5.5 M on the mock, more on PumpSwap), so a cascade filling the 20 M exit room in that slot could take the payer past 24 M (★the limit is 40 M, U16, which leaves more room); a separate fee payer for crank batches, or cranks counted in the payer cap, closes it (not built). LiteSVM enforces no block limit, so the uncapped run is an optimistic bound; the per-writable-account limit is desk-checked for Agave and Firedancer (U16, M10); other clients are not checked.
- A batch of cranks write-locks every `Market` it names; the keeper builds batches from markets with no pending exit in the same slot and simulates each batch (a failing crank fails the batch; `crank_price` fails only on wrong keys, A63).
