## 7. Off-chain components

### 7.1 Keeper (`services/keeper`, Rust)

- **Stack:** tokio; `services/common` (RPC + Yellowstone gRPC clients); `declare_program!(shortwin)` through `anchor-client 1.2`; **the same** `shortwin-math` and `shortwin-venue-state` crates as the program, so CR, bounds, legs, box and arming decisions match on-chain exactly [R-TOOL §4.3].
- **Inputs:** Yellowstone account subscriptions for all `Market` and `ShortPosition` accounts, each market's venue accounts (curve, pools, vaults, fee configs, `Global`/`GlobalConfig`, AMM v4 `AmmInfo`, CPMM `PoolState`/`AmmConfig`, LP mints, boost vault), **the six venue ProgramData accounts** (the upgrade latch), and every Raydium SOL pool of each listed mint (`getProgramAccounts` memcmp on AMM v4 offsets 400/432 and CPMM offsets 168/200 [R-RAY §2.1, §6.1], with `dataSize` 752 / 637, the only lengths the verifier accepts; as built in M4 through a polling client, optionally on a separate discovery endpoint, `--discovery-rpc`); RPC websocket fallback.

**Duties** (ECON §5.8 is normative; the manipulation resistance of ECON §12's atomic model assumes them, A69, R3B-5):

1. **Observation coverage.** At least one observation **per second** on every **covered** market (duty 8: open positions and value at risk ≥ `var_floor_lamports`; owner decision A of 2026-10-01) with a position whose live CR is below 1.3·L, whose deadline is within 60 s, or that is armed, and wherever `|P_spot/P_ema − 1| > 2 %`; otherwise at least every 30 s for markets with open positions — **below the floor the 30-s idle cadence is all a market gets** (its exits still go when the program accepts them: while a position is near an exit the market is read again in the seconds its last observation's reference stays fresh, so an idle crank at `t` is followed by the exit at `t + 1`, M7D-1) (after a venue switch, per second while `ema_guard = 1`: duty 5). **Raydium listing windows** (M4V-5, as built; with M4R the warm-up is `ema_warm`): a Raydium market with no open position is observed every `listing_interval_s` (60 s) inside its listing window and every second in its last `EMA_WARMUP_BUCKETS + 2` (10) seconds — and after it until its price state has warmed up (as the next instruction's roll would see it) — so the first open after the window reads a `P_ema` that followed the pool and passes the price warm-up (§2.6 rule 1; keeper scenarios `a_listing_window_is_observed_and_the_first_open_is_warm`: 60 observations 60 s apart and 10 in the last 10 s, the first open lands; `an_unobserved_listing_window_is_warmed_up_after_it`: a window nobody observed is warmed up in the 9 s after it, the open refused `EmaWarmingUp` until then). **PumpSwap (M6 as built; OWNER-M6SK-2, recorded by the owner on 2026-09-30 as a PROPOSED O17 duty, ECON §15):** a PumpSwap market without positions is observed every second while its projected prologue still shows the warm-up running — after a graduation, a PumpSwap listing or a re-detection (whose first observation starts the price) — so the first open reads a `P_ema` seeded from honest buckets; 8 cranks per graduation or listing at the keeper's cost (M4V-5 extended to PumpSwap).
2. **Deviation bursts.** After any observation it did not make that deviates from its own view of that second by more than 2 %, observe that market **every slot for 60 s**: atomic bundles then have no second of their own, and the settlement box's deferral residual gets no consecutive attacker-only seconds (ECON §5.6, §12.11). The deviation is in **price**: the bucket's `lo` / `hi` against the spot the keeper read (`coverage::MarketTrack::check_foreign`). **★M7-SEC-2 (fixed): only an excursion that reverted starts a burst** — the deviating extreme must be more than 2 % off the keeper's own range of that second **and of the one before** (a price it saw a second earlier is the market moving away from it, not an excursion) **and** more than 2 % off its latest read, at or after that second (the snapshot that already holds the bucket); a foreign price still there at the keeper's next read is a genuine move, which duty 1's per-second coverage above `ema_dev_bps` follows (metric `foreign_moves`). An atomic bundle is exactly a reverted excursion (nobody else can see its price before or after it), so its detection is unchanged (`bursts::an_atomic_pump_crank_dump_*`, and a round trip in separate transactions of one second, `m7_sec::m7_sec_2_d_*`). As built at M7 any foreign price off the view of its second started a burst: a plain `crank_price` (5,000 lamports, no trade) after anyone's honest ≥ 2 % move, the keeper's own crank landing after a trade made between its read and its landing, or a second keeper instance on the other side of a trade each bought 116 keeper cranks charged to the O17 budget — 51 such cranks (0.000255 SOL) spent the default 0.03 SOL and paused opens for the UTC day (the review's reproducer; now 0 bursts, the spend at the control's, `m7_sec::m7_sec_2_a`–`_c`). A price burst again needs a ≥ 2 % price round trip (≈ 2·φ·δ with δ ≈ 1 % of the pool's token reserve: 0.005 SOL on a 100-SOL 25-bps pool, 0.05 SOL on a 1,000-SOL one, against the burst's 0.00058–0.00106 SOL of keeper cranks unbatched). Row 48 (M4F-1) also started bursts on a bucket's **liquidity** (`llo` / `lhi` against the `√(X·Y)` the keeper read); row 49 reverted that: an LP-wrapped crank moves no price and costs one transaction fee, so the liquidity trigger let anyone buy a 60-s per-slot burst at 25–150× below its cost to the keeper, on every covered market, and exhaust an O17 budget (M4G-2), and while it was repeated every missed keeper second was another attacker-only `L_ema` step (M4G-1). **Liquidity-anomaly coverage** (PROPOSED, row 51, FITS-2 (b); ECON §5.8 duty 2): on a market **with open positions**, a foreign bucket whose `llo` / `lhi` deviates from the keeper's own `√(X·Y)` of that second by more than `burst_dev_bps` starts **per-second** (not per-slot) coverage for `liq_cover_s` (10 s, config), extended while such deviations recur; markets without positions never get it; price bursts and the per-second coverage while `ema_guard = 1` are unchanged. It answers the withdraw drag: withdraw-wrapped cranks in the keeper's quiet seconds dragged `L_ema` to the locked depth, and with the spot leg at the drained `L_live` a withdraw-wrapped liquidation forced positions healthy at the pool's depth (FITS-2). **On PumpSwap markets too** (M6R-1, owner decision of 2026-09-30, row 56; canonical pools take third-party LP, R-VEN Update H11): the same trigger and cadence, 1:1, on markets with open positions only — the keeper's `coverage::MarketTrack::check_foreign` compares the bucket's liquidity with its own `√(X·(Y + VQR))`, venue-independent as built (ECON §12.12 (12) (d): a drag of withdraw-wrapped cranks on a λ 50 % PumpSwap pool forces a half-cap position at 2.02–2.035× against the honest 2.040× under the #99 keeper, nothing under this coverage). Under the coverage the drag's first second is its only attacker-only one, so `L_ema` holds at one step (≈ ×11/12). Until ★AIR-14 no such drag forced anything (ECON §12.12 (5b)); since AIR-14's reference cap at `D` that one step forces one level (2.06× against the honest 2.065× at 0.79 × the cap, ECON §12.12 (5b) (iii); §2.6 residual 10). The coverage holds `L_ema`; it cannot lift a low the attacker reached genuinely by withdrawing for real for a few seconds first (nothing is foreign then), and that low, frozen at 1:1, forces what the LP's withdrawal for good forces (FITX-1, row 52; §2.6 residual 10). The attacker pays one transaction per second of keeper coverage while it keeps it going (1:1); an isolated trigger buys `liq_cover_s` cranks (10:1 unbatched, ≈ 2:1 batched; ★M7 measured 8 cranks above the control, 8:1 / 1.3:1 at zero priority), against row 48's 150:1. What is left is a covered second whose observation does not land (a missed second is another step; the steps add up while the wrapping continues — ECON §12.12 (5b) (iv): since ★AIR-14 a single miss forces a cap-sized position at 2.07× against 2.078×, and 20 force it at 2.01–2.07×, where before only 20 did, at 2.06–2.07×). Since #99 no carried position exceeds the new pool's opening caps, so a push after a switch's guard has cleared only delays an exit (ECON §12.12 (11)). **Budget (owner decision A of 2026-10-01, duty 8):** price bursts and liquidity-anomaly coverage are **discretionary** charges — drawn on the market's own entitlement and then the free pool, never on another market's entitlement — and run on covered markets only: a market below `var_floor_lamports` gets neither (its idle cadence only).
3. **Liquidate** at the first executable second (fixed `δ_liq`) via a Jito bundle with tip, with a priority-fee RPC fallback; retry each second on `ExitBoundNotMet`; `expire` when the expiry bound is met. ★**Since 1.0.1 (pump-final §7):** a curve position past `rT` is planned like any other (`Plan::Straddle` is gone) on the program's own quoter — `B̂_v3` at `φ_s` on the mint's live supply, `buyback_allowed` and σ included — and its `liquidate` / `expire` completes the curve; after an exit whose event shows `PumpCurve → PumpMigrating` the keeper sends `migrate_v2` and the transition in the same tick. **The upgrade window (§15 of the design, review R-8):** the keeper carries both TradeExtras formats for one release — `pump_trade_extras_v2` (1.0.0's 20 keys) and the 10-key v3 list — and picks one per short.win ProgramData deploy slot: at start-up and at each new slot the first curve exit simulates V3, then V2 if V3 fails on account parsing (`BadRemainingAccounts` / `VenueAccountMismatch`); the format that parses is kept until the slot changes; a simulation from a bank behind the deploy slot read decides nothing; neither format → `Alert::CurveExtrasFormatUnknown`; on 1.0.0 a V2 exit refused `CurveStraddle` chains to `sol_settle` unpaged (the position waits for the upgrade). The next release deletes the V2 builder. **PumpSwap (M6-SEC-4, fixed):** the liquidate / expire transaction starts with `create_idempotent(ATA(creator_vault(live coin creator), WSOL))` whenever the pool's live `coin_creator` is not the cached one (`venue::pamm_creator_vault_prep`; §5.4 case 4). After a graduation the keeper's exit lands at the warm-up gate, 8–12 s after the migration (accepted, OWNER-M6R-4; §5.4). Always `simulateTransaction` first. `decide` evaluates CR-liquidatability as the program does. The spot leg is on `bounds::spot_liquidity` = `max(L_live, L_floor)` since row 51 (§3.6 step 3; the guarded floor at the highs' median since AIR-17). Every risk quote (the live CR, the spot leg and the EMA leg) takes `min(φ_live, cap)` with the program's cap, `VenueState::exit_risk_cap_bps` (since ★AIR-10, keeper `2c1fce9`: the position's hard cap, on PumpSwap at most the tier at `P_ema`; the keeper reads the venue with `read_state_boxed_for_exit`, as `liquidate` does). So it neither sends a liquidation the program refuses nor expires a position the program would liquidate; duty 1's near-threshold trigger keeps the live CR (a withdrawal can only make the keeper observe more). While `ema_warm > 0` (PROPOSED, M4R) neither is sent: both fail `EmaWarmingUp` (duty 5).
4. **`sol_settle` every second for armed positions** (and for positions whose S1/S2 legs hold): it arms, keeps the clock running, disarms only on box-robust evidence, or settles. The keeper judges "liquidatable" here as in duty 3, at the program's exit risk fee (★AIR-10).
5. **No-route markets** every ≤ 30 s (continuous S3 chain) and `sol_settle(S3)` when due. The keeper's projection runs the S3 chain at `min(global hard cap, Market.min_open_hard_cap_bps)` and judges a position's S3 timer on its own route (the fee against `min(global hard cap, the position's locked cap)`, `route::position_no_route`), as `sol_settle` does (★AIR-19, keeper `6a46cde`). While an S3 on an **executable** venue (flag or fee above the hard cap) is due, observe that market **once per second, not per slot** (duty 2's burst does not apply there): the v0.4.1 box takes the medians of bucket lows and highs, so several honest observations at different prices within a second only widen it (§4.5). **Raydium fast path**: once `pool_fail` has held for `pool_fast_route_s`, propose the deepest eligible candidate that every open position fits (#99, row 49: `engine::pool_select::carried_fit`, §2.6 rule 3) and call `execute_pool_switch` when its 60 s window closes (§2.6); with no fitting candidate there is nothing to propose, and the positions settle S3 when due (duty 5's no-route cadence keeps the chain). As built (M4; `services/keeper/src/pool_monitor.rs`, config `[pool_select]`): the window is opened at the first armed second, a shallower window of someone else's is outbid, and the execution is sent at the first second after the window; a cancelled window is proposed again while the fast path is still armed. No proposal of a candidate whose program the latch holds is sent — the plan ranks only the other program's pools; the execution is sent anyway and cancels a window whose candidate's program is latched (M4V-4), after which the best pool on the other program opens the next window in the same tick. A window is proposed only with a candidate that passes the window floor (M4V-1) and the fit (#99; since row 50 with the fee-scaled caps at `min(min_open_fee_ppm, φ_cand)`, since row 51 at most 25 bps, the program's own `carried_fit`); a mark `max_q_hwm` left by a closed large position can keep every candidate out while positions are open, and the plan then stays blocked (`CarriedPositionsTooLarge`) until the S3 exits bring `ΣB_Q` under a candidate's cap or the positions settle (FIT-3, §2.6 residual 14; row 50's refresh duty was withdrawn with `refresh_max_q`, FITV-1). A failing market **without** positions, which the no-route cadence above does not observe, is observed by the pool monitor (at once, then every 30 s) while a candidate is deep enough for the fast path but not for a zero-position adoption, so its `pool_fail` chain arms. Pool-selection transactions go out at the exit priority ceiling, outside the O17 observation budget. A list-only market with open positions (from M5) collects its candidates in a window the same way. **After the adoption (PROPOSED, M4R; `pool_monitor` / `decide`):** after a `PoolSwitched`, and on any market with `ema_warm > 0` and open positions, keep the per-second `crank_price` of this duty while `ema_warm > 0` **or `ema_guard = 1`** (M4F-1, row 48: `MarketNeeds.guarded`; on an honest pool the guard clears at the gate, adoption + 9 s). Skip `liquidate` and `expire` while `ema_warm > 0` (the exits that are due then execute at adoption + 9 s), and treat `sol_settle` as harmless (it evaluates nothing, §3.8). One honest observation in a warm-up bucket is all the seed needs (§4.4); there is no window-observation duty. **The reference guard and M4X-2's input guard hold only while every second carries an honest observation** (§3.6): both read `L_mlo`, which a deposit-wrapped crank in a second nobody else observed pushes up, 5 such buckets of 8 being enough. As built at M4R this duty ended at `ema_warm == 0`, and a per-second deposit freeze cleared the guard at ≈ +15 s and blocked the reference (ECON §12.12 (4): S1). Kept per second while the guard is set, the keeper leaves no guarded bucket attacker-only. A freeze from the adoption then holds the guard set, and the reference at the honest lows, for as long as it lasts, at one observation per second. After the guard clears the keeper is back on duty 1's cadence and an attacker owns its idle seconds, as on any market; since #99 the carried positions fit the new pool's opening caps (since row 50 with the fee-scaled caps at `min(φ_inc, φ_cand)`), so a push then delays their exits by 0–1 s (ECON §12.12 (11)), as for positions opened on the pool; a 1 %→1 % switch at its impact cap is the exception (§2.6 residual 15).
6. **Graduation and wipes.** Call pump `migrate_v2` top-level as soon as a curve completes (ADOPTED Q16); on the canonical pool's appearance: `crank_price` (transition, ring rewrite), create `trader_base_ata` if missing, pAMM `init_user_volume_accumulator(payer = keeper, user = trader)`; `extend_account` is not needed (a fresh pool is 271 B and trades as such; it extends to 301 B, R-VEN Update G4). Straddle bundles with `complete_curve` (§5.4) and the "tx1 + tx2 only" fallback (★**retired in 1.0.1**, D2: a position past `rT` exits in one instruction, duty 3; the keeper's `[graduation]` keys `straddle`, `send_without_exit`, `complete_slippage_bps`, `max_complete_lamports`, `tip_lamports`, `tip_accounts`, `block_engine` and `--block-engine` are refused as removed; `migrate` stays). **Right after a full wipe**, the post-wipe bundle so pre-wipe cashback reaches the wiped epoch's lenders (ECON §9.5): on the curve kinds `[pump claim_cashback(user = trader), sweep_trader]` (M5-SEC-1: `sweep_trader` sets both bits, §3.3, §3.9); on PumpSwap M6's claim path and `sweep_trader`; since v0.4.1 deposits into a live wipe record also wait for these (R4A-7), so the keeper's call is a convenience, not the only protection — a depositor's client can bundle it, both instructions being permissionless.
   ★**As built (1.0.1, pump-final P4; supersedes the bundle parts of the M5 / M6 text below, kept as the 1.0.0 record):** the curve exit's TradeExtras are the 10-key v3 list (T7 a buyback recipient of the live `Global`, from the mint's first byte), with the V2 list for the upgrade window (duty 3); `graduation.rs` keeps `migrate_v2_ix`, the transition and the trader-account builders and `completion_quote` (M7-SEC-8's hot-curve reads); duty 10 alerts once each while they last on `CurveQuoteOffsetInconsistent` (a live curve with `vQ − rQ ≠ ivqr`), `LiveCurvePostComplete` (G-3) and `MigratingFvUndefined` (§4.5), with the gauges `synthetic_completion_delta_bps` (ρ − 1) and `curve_base_ata_donation` (`A + pcB − 206.9e12`) on migrating curves and the counter `shortwin_keeper_synthetic_exits_total`; the baseline is `VENUE_GUARD_SLOTS_2026_10_13`.
   **As built (M5; `services/keeper/src/graduation.rs`, config `[graduation]`):** the keeper covers `PumpCurve` and `PumpMigrating` markets with the curve adapter's ReadSet and, for a curve exit, TradeExtras T0–T19 (a fee and a buyback recipient of the live `Global`, starting at the entry indexed by the mint's first byte; the live creator's vault), and values curve positions with the program's own quoter (`VenueState::quoter`: `B̂_str` above `rT`). `migrate_v2` goes out top-level, alone with its compute budget (27 IDL accounts + the boost vault and its WSOL ATA; `MIGRATE_CU` 400 k), at most once a second, and the market is cranked in the same second — but **`graduation.migrate` defaults to false until M6** (M5-SEC-4: without the `→ PumpSwap` transition a migrated market froze at its last curve EMA; the scenario tests opt in). The straddle (`Plan::Straddle`, planned for liquidatable positions only — an armed but not liquidatable position keeps `sol_settle`, since tx3's `liquidate` would fail `NotLiquidatable`, which is not a fallback code; a minor deviation from §5.1's order, flagged) builds tx1 (the keeper's base ATA + `complete_curve`, `max_sol_cost` = the keeper's quote of `rT` + `complete_slippage_bps` 500 + a 1,000,000-lamport rent allowance for pump's creator-vault top-up, capped by `max_complete_lamports` 20 SOL — PROPOSED ops knobs, not in ECON §15) and tx2 (`migrate_v2`), the tip (`tip_lamports` 100,000, rotated over the 8 tip accounts) on the last, pre-flights it and sends it to a Jito block engine (`--block-engine`); **tx3 is M6's** (`exit_tx` returns none), so with no exit the two-transaction bundle would freeze the position rather than exit it, and it goes out only with `send_without_exit` (default false; §5.4 fallback in M5, flagged): otherwise the keeper raises `Alert::StraddleWaiting` once and calls `sol_settle` every second. M6 revisits the default once a migrated market reaches PumpSwap. **List-only markets** (a keeper fix, M5): a `None` market is covered with its detection set as ReadSet, so a curve that graduated elsewhere with positions open is cranked and settled in S3 (duty 5); one whose detection set classifies as a live or migrating curve (`classify_pump`) is cranked (the re-detection), and every curve market is checked once for `trader_base_ata` and the pump UVA, which the keeper creates if missing (`crank_price` creates nothing; PROPOSED — this section named no such duty). **Not built in M5** (open items then): the post-wipe bundle above and duty 13's `sweep_trader`; the PumpSwap first-trade duties; bundle pre-flight of tx2 / tx3 on a plain RPC node, which cannot simulate them before tx1 lands (the options named in M5, for the owner: Jito `simulateBundle`, or "after N dropped bundles send tx1 + tx2 only"); `RpcChain::send_bundle` against a live block engine is **UNVERIFIED** (only the JSON request and the in-process backend are tested). A tipped liquidation with the largest extras set does not fit a v0 transaction (§6.4): its tip goes in its own bundle transaction or the exit goes as v1 (keeper / M7).
   **As built (M6; supersedes the M5 defaults above; `graduation.rs`, `venue.rs`, `sweep.rs`, config `[graduation]`, `[sweep]`):** `graduation.migrate` defaults to **true** again (M5-SEC-4 closed). **Moving onto the pool is a keeper duty** whether or not `migrate` is on: every curve market whose canonical pool is valid — the keeper's migration or anyone's — gets one transaction at exit priority (the missing pool accounts, `crank_price` on the curve's ReadSet, `crank_price` on the pool's: the pool's first bucket), counted as that second's observation (81.6 k CU creating 2 accounts in the scenario; `UNSIMULATED_CU` 400 k). **PumpSwap exits and lists:** the ReadSet is the adapter's `read_keys` (pool and vaults writable), TradeExtras T0–T18 with T9 / T16 the live `GlobalConfig` entries from `mint[0] % 8`, T10 / T17 the adapter's `recipient_wsol_ata`, T11 / T12 from the cache unless the coin creator changed; the keeper reads the mint with the ReadSet for its supply (`read_state_with`). **Account preparation:** the trader's base ATA (T7; a list-only listing has none, so a `None → PumpSwap` re-detection needs it), the pAMM UVA (T14, keeper paying), the coin-creator vault's WSOL ATA (T11), both recipients' WSOL ATAs (T10, T17) and on cashback coins T18, re-checked when the coin creator changes; no `extend_account`. **The straddle bundle:** tx1, tx2 and tx3 = the move onto the pool (§5.4; the exit lands at T + 8 — OWNER-M6R-4, OWNER-M6SK-1: the keeper keeps tx3's own bucket, which slows the tracking of a genuine ×3 pump right after graduation from +9 s to +16 s); any tx3 pre-flight failure sends tx1 + tx2 and then the keeper's own move onto the pool (V1-9 fallback; `send_without_exit` defaults to **true**; tx3 is booked as that second's observation). **After a full wipe** (same second, retried every second while a post-wipe bit is clear): on PumpSwap `[create ATA(trader, WSOL), pAMM claim_cashback, sweep_trader]` when the pAMM cashback ATA holds WSOL — **preceded by pAMM `init_user_volume_accumulator(payer = keeper, user = trader)` when the trader's pAMM UVA is missing** (M6-SEC-2, fixed: `claim_cashback` fails 3012 without it, and anyone can fund the ATA without the UVA; `SweepFacts` reads the UVA, `sweep::claim_ixs`) —, on the curve kinds (`PumpCurve`, `PumpMigrating`: `deposit` requires the rewards bit on `PumpMigrating` too since M6-SEC-5, §3.3) `[pump claim_cashback, sweep_trader]` when the pump UVA holds more than its rent, `sweep_trader` alone otherwise (`wipe` scenarios, `wipe::m6_sec_2_*`). The PumpSwap unlock depends on pAMM `claim_cashback` and `init_user_volume_accumulator` as they are: re-verified on every pAMM upgrade (§12 U31). Still **UNVERIFIED**: `send_bundle` against a live block engine and tx2 / tx3 pre-flight on a plain RPC node (fixed limits `MIGRATE_CU`, `UNSIMULATED_CU` 400 k).

**Operations.**

7. **Batching and counting** (R3B-5). A second in which the keeper sends `liquidate`, `expire`, `sol_settle` or `close_short` for a market **is** that market's observation: no separate crank. Remaining cranks of the same second are batched, several markets per transaction, which amortises the 5,000-lamport signature fee (ECON §5.8: 0.43 SOL per market-day unbatched, 0.07–0.10 batched, at per-second coverage of every market). **Batches are v1 transactions** (§6.4; R4B-9): `crank_price` keeps 6 per-market keys inline on PumpSwap / CPMM (5 on the curve), so a v0 transaction with the protocol ALT fits only 4 (5) cranks in 1,232 B; a v1 transaction (4,096 B, 64 inline addresses) fits ≈ 6 shared keys + 6 per market, up to 9 cranks; the keeper uses 6 and falls back to v0 batches where v1 is not accepted — measured by T-SIZE (§6.4): 4 Raydium cranks, 5 curve cranks, 3 PumpSwap cranks since row 56's LP mint (4 before); base fees per crank ≈ 6/k × v1's (+50 % at 4, +100 % at 3). Batches are simulated; a market whose crank fails simulation is dropped from the batch and cranked alone. **★M7 measured** (§6.4; `tests/bench/m7_keeper`): v1 holds 8–11 cranks (8 PumpSwap, 9 Raydium or mixed, 11 curve), v0 through A28 3 / 4 / 5, and 8–10 with a table per market; the defaults stay `batch_v1` = 6 and `batch_v0` = 4, size-packed; whether v1 lands on mainnet is U25 (UNVERIFIED; `shortwin-v1-probe`).
8. **Budget (owner item O17).** Coverage is targeted by duty 1, which costs 0.003–0.03 SOL per market-day at normal priority prices; armed positions, deviation bursts and liquidations cost fractions of a millisol each (ECON §5.8). Duty 5's per-second coverage while a switch's guard is set costs ≈ 9 cranks after an honest switch, and one a second while a deposit freeze from the adoption is paid (the attacker paying its own transaction every second). Row 48's liquidity-triggered bursts, which let anyone keep a per-slot burst running for one transaction fee a minute (1.10–1.87 SOL per market-day of keeper cost against 0.007–0.029 SOL for the attacker, M4G-2), are reverted (row 49); row 51's per-second liquidity-anomaly coverage (duty 2) costs the keeper one crank per attacker transaction while sustained, and at most 0.39–0.67 SOL per market-day unbatched against the attacker's 0.04–0.16 SOL for one trigger every 11 s (ECON §5.8), on markets with open positions only. Budget exhaustion on a market with positions is degraded mode (item 9), never a silent stop. The owner sets the daily budget (since 2026-10-01 one global budget, below), the priority-price ceiling and the markets covered; the keeper exports per-market coverage seconds, CU and lamports spent. **★M7 as built (O17, owner decision of 2026-09-30; superseded as the primary control by the global budget below):** every market with open positions covered at targeted cadence (per second only when duties 1–2, 5 or 9 need it, else every 30 s) against `per_market_daily_lamports` (0.03 SOL a UTC day per market), charged with the market's share of its `crank_price` transactions (a batch's fee split equally); the cranks exits depend on charged but **never throttled**; exits, pool selection, graduation moves, `crank_sol_usd` and `set_coverage_pause` neither charged nor throttled; an exhausted budget stopped the rest and, on a market with open positions, was degraded mode **at once** (`DegradedReason::Budget`). **Measured cost** (the keeper's own transactions, ECON §5.8, `keeper_cost.py`): a quiet market 2,880 cranks a day — 0.0024 SOL batched (v1 k = 6) and 0.0144 unbatched at 0 µlamports/CU, 0.0118–0.0143 / 0.0238–0.0263 at the 100,000 ceiling; a position near a threshold all day 0.072 / 0.432 at 0 and 0.353–0.428 / 0.713–0.788 at the ceiling (re-baselined on 1.0.1, ECON #119); an armed position 43 `sol_settle`; a price deviation 116 cranks (≈ 150 at 2.5 slots a second); an isolated LP-wrapped trigger 8 cranks above the control; a PumpSwap warm-up 8.

   **★The global keeper budget (owner decision A of 2026-10-01 on OWNER-M7-13 / -14; SPEC §14 M7-13 / M7-14; normative; config `[budget]`, ECON §5.8, §15 #109).** One daily budget `G` = `global_daily_lamports` replaces the per-market budgets as the primary control (`per_market_daily_lamports` is retired: a config that still sets it is refused). It funds markets **in order of their lenders' value at risk**; price bursts and liquidity-anomaly coverage draw on it; markets below a value-at-risk floor get the idle cadence only; a market the budget can no longer cover is degraded (duty 9) — per market, as before.
   - **Value at risk** of market `m` (lamports): `V_m = ⌊Market.borrowed_q · min(Market.ema_price, P_ACC_MAX) / 10¹⁸⌋` (U256 intermediate, saturating at `u64::MAX`), from the `Market` as the tick read it (no projection) — the lenders' borrowed inventory `ΣB_Q` at the protocol's own smoothed price, i.e. the product on which rent accrues (`P̃ = min(P_ema, P_ACC_MAX)`, ECON §7) and a settlement's immediate token value `⌊Q·P_ema/WAD⌋` (ECON §8.6; S2/S3, and S1 since ★AIR-21; 0 on a venue that cannot execute since ★AIR-09). **Why not open notional:** `total_notional_open` (`Σ N_open`) is frozen at each open's quote — a token that has pumped toward its positions' thresholds, where coverage matters most, keeps its old weight — and a sale-wrapped open records ≥ 0.90 of its honest quote (M7-11, accepted); `P_ema` follows the price within seconds (τ = 5 s) but a trade cannot move it within a transaction, and lifting it means holding the attacker's own positions' price up. **Why not lender counts:** wallets are free (the per-wallet cap is per key, M7-SEC-9). `V` is bounded by the caps: `ΣB_Q ≤ 7.5·φ·X₁` (§4.6) with `φ ≤ venue_fee_cap_bps` (150 bps), so `V` ≤ ≈ 11 % of the pool's conservative SOL depth, and `Σ N_open ≤ market_max_notional` (25 SOL in beta).
   - **Classes of market**, re-evaluated whenever the keeper reads the market — every tick for a covered market, every `idle_interval_s` below the floor (and in the seconds after an observation while a position is near an exit, M7D-1), and in the tick its set of open positions changes (the tick's first read, the open positions, shows it): **covered** (tier 1) — open positions and `V_m ≥ var_floor_lamports`, ranked by `V` descending (ties: the older `Market.created_at`, then the smaller market key, bytewise); **below the floor** (tier 2) — open positions and `V_m < var_floor_lamports`: **the idle cadence only** — one `crank_price` every `idle_interval_s` (30 s), the market read in that tick (not every tick: junk with positions does not grow the per-tick reads, M7-SEC-8), no per-second coverage of any kind (near a threshold, armed, warm-up, guard, duty 2's bursts and liquidity anomalies) — and its exits (`liquidate`, `expire`, `sol_settle`, `close_short`) still sent whenever the program accepts them on those reads. **★Reads near an exit (M7D-1, fixed 2026-10-01):** an exit needs a completed bucket at most `ref_max_age_s` (2 s) old, so while a position is near a threshold or its deadline, expired, armed, waiting only for a fresh reference, or has a plan other than `Idle` / `Watch`, the market is read **every second the reference of the keeper's last observation is still fresh** (the crank at `t`, then reads at `t + 1` and `t + 2`); cranks stay at the idle cadence, and a landed exit is itself an observation, so a cascade — or an armed position's `sol_settle` calls — go on second by second (as built at decision A each read came 30 s after the last observation and found its own reference stale: no below-floor position was ever liquidated or expired, and a cascade stopped where its market fell below the floor); **without positions** (tier 3) — duty 1's warm-ups and listing windows only, as before.
   - **Classes of charge** (a charge = the market's share of a `crank_price` transaction's fee, a batch's fee split equally): **exit-critical** — the as-built never-throttled set (per-second coverage of a position near a threshold, armed or warming up; a liquidatable or expired position waiting for a fresh reference or its bound; the S3 chain; a market without a route) — **at most one crank per market a second** (M7D-4: a burst's further per-slot cranks in a second the keeper already observed are discretionary; as built at decision A every slot of a burst on a market near a threshold was exit-critical, ≈ 2.5 a second, overdrawn without limit) — and **below the floor the idle crank an exit waits on** (M7D-2: a position expired or whose EMA leg holds with its live CR below `L`, waiting only for a fresh reference; a `*Wait` or `SolSettle` plan; armed; the S3 chain; a market without a route — the tail, then the overdraft; as built at decision A every below-floor crank was baseline, so junk that spent the tail stopped every below-floor exit's reference); **baseline** — the idle cadence, duty 5's guard coverage after a switch, and the warm-ups and listing windows of markets without positions (duty 1; a market with positions warming up is exit-critical); **discretionary** — duty 2's price bursts (every crank of a second after its first) and liquidity-anomaly coverage. Not charged and never throttled (the global lines, as before): exits, pool selection, graduation moves, `crank_sol_usd`, `set_coverage_pause`.
   - **Balances** (lamports; reset at 00:00 UTC): the free pool `F` (starts at `G`), each covered market's unspent entitlement `U_m`, the day's tier-2 spend `T`, the overdraft `O`. A covered market's **entitlement** `R_m = ⌈ĉ_m · ⌈86,400 / idle_interval_s⌉ · (10⁴ + reserve_margin_bps) / 10⁴⌉` — twice its quiet day by default — where `ĉ_m` is what its last observation crank was charged — before its first, the keeper's measured average per-crank charge, and before it has measured any (a start or restart) `⌈5,000 / batch⌉` (834 at `batch_v1` = 6; M7D-5: as built at decision A the unbatched 5,000, 6× the batched charge, so a restart funded 34–70 of 100 markets that the batched charge funds in full); a market that becomes covered at second `s` of the day gets `⌈R_m · (86,400 − s) / 86,400⌉`. Entitlements are funded **in rank order**: at 00:00 UTC every covered market from the top, `U_m = min(R_m, F)`, `F −= U_m`; a market that becomes covered later takes its entitlement from `F`, then from the unspent entitlements of lower-ranked covered markets, lowest-ranked first. **★Once a day (M7D-3, fixed 2026-10-01):** a market is funded at most its day's entitlement, fixed at its first covering of the day — a market that leaves and re-joins gets nothing more —; what a join took from lower-ranked markets is **restricted**: it pays only exit-critical and baseline charges, never discretionary ones, and a market that stops being covered (its positions closed, `V` below the floor) returns its restricted `U` to the covered markets other markets took from (lowest-ranked first, up to what each lost), the rest of its `U` to `F` (as built at decision A a market was funded afresh at every join and returned all its `U` to `F`, so a higher-ranked junk market that dipped below the floor and re-joined turned every lower-ranked market's entitlement into its own bursts). **★Re-estimate (M7D-5):** an entitlement funded at an estimated `ĉ` is recomputed at the market's first measured crank (prorated from the second it was first covered); what the market holds above it is released (restricted lamports back as above, the rest to `F`); and whenever `F` grows that way or a market leaves, the covered markets still short of their entitlement are topped up from `F` in rank order, up to what the rest of the day needs. Rank changes move no balance; every lookup of "lower-ranked" uses the current ranking.
   - **Admission of a charge `c` on market `m`**, in this order until `c` is covered: (1) `m`'s own `U_m` (a covered market; a discretionary charge only its unrestricted part, an exit-critical or baseline charge its restricted part first); (2) `F` — for a tier-2 market only while `T + c ≤ ⌊G · tail_share_bps / 10⁴⌋`; (3) for an exit-critical or baseline charge of a covered market — **never a discretionary one** — the unspent entitlements of lower-ranked covered markets, lowest-ranked first; (4) what is still uncovered: an exit-critical charge (covered or below the floor), and a tier-3 warm-up or listing-window charge (a listing or a graduation, ≥ 0.035 SOL or ≈ 85 SOL of curve buys, buys its 8–70 cranks ≥ 100× over, so draining `F` must not stop them: M4V-5, OWNER-M6SK-2), is sent anyway and booked to `O` (never throttled — OWNER-M7-6 (a), lender safety first; metric `budget_overdraft_lamports`, alert `ExitOverdraft` once a day); any other charge is **refused** (the crank is not sent; nothing is booked). Within a tick charges are presented exit-critical first, then baseline, then discretionary, each in rank order, then tier 2 (exit-critical first), then tier 3.
   - **Degraded mode:** a refused charge on a market with open positions degrades it at once (`DegradedReason::Budget { spent, budget: G, rank }`; duty 9: opens paused through the coverage role, alert; exits continue), and the recovery is duty 9's (`recovery_s` of met coverage — at the latest after 00:00 UTC funds it again). Below the floor nothing per-second is required, so a tier-2 market degrades only on an outage over `COVERAGE_GAP_S` or a refused idle crank (the tail spent).
   - **What it guarantees:** a covered market keeps its entitlement against every lower-ranked market and against every other market's bursts; only higher-ranked markets' exit-critical and baseline spend can take it (priority) — a higher-ranked market takes it once a day at most, and what it takes pays none of its own bursts (M7D-3). Bursts and liquidity-anomaly coverage on `m` spend `U_m`'s own (unrestricted) part and then the free pool — a storm on one market cannot degrade another market's baseline; the free pool itself is drainable by bursts on any covered market (ECON §5.8: by three hovering junk markets bursting from a self-LP pool for ≈ 0.6 SOL a day at `V` 1 SOL, OWNER-M7-17 (3)). Junk below the floor costs at most `tail_share_bps` of `G` a day in idle cranks, however many markets are listed, and never a covered market's entitlement; below-floor exits' cranks (M7D-2) overdraw beyond the tail — at most a few per position that exits. To take a real market's coverage through junk, an attacker must hold more value at risk than that market on each junk market (ECON §5.8 tables). The keeper's spend is bounded by `G + O`, `O` growing only with exit-critical cranks — one a second per market at most (M7D-4) — that `G` cannot fund at their rank.
   - **Config (`[budget]`; PROPOSED defaults, owner item OWNER-M7-17; adopted by the owner as v1.0.0's defaults on 2026-10-09 with O18, ECON §14 N25):** `global_daily_lamports` 1,000,000,000 (1 SOL a UTC day; 0 = no budget, every charge admitted), `var_floor_lamports` 1,000,000,000 (1 SOL of `V`; bounds [0, `market_max_notional`]; 0 = every market with positions covered), `reserve_margin_bps` 10,000 (bounds [0, 100,000]), `tail_share_bps` 2,000 (bounds [0, 10,000]); the priority ceilings and the T-CASCADE knobs unchanged. **Metrics:** per market `V`, class, rank, `U` and the day's spend per charge class; globally `F`, `T`, `O` and the day's spend; **alerts:** `BudgetExhausted { scope: global }` at the day's first refused charge, `ExitOverdraft`, and duty 9's per market.
   - **Numbers** (`keeper_cost.py`, ECON §5.8): 1 SOL funds 208 covered markets' entitlements at 0 µlamports/CU batched, 139 at 10,000, 35 at the ceiling (34 / 32 / 19 unbatched) — from a start or restart too, at the batched first-crank estimate and each market's first measured crank (M7D-5; as built at decision A a restart funded 34 at 00:00 and 69–70 at 12:00 UTC, the rest degraded until the next day). Price bursts with 20 covered markets: degrading the first market takes 1,567 round trips at 0 µlamports/CU (7.8 SOL on a 100-SOL 25-bps pool; as built 48, 0.24 SOL), 434 at the ceiling (2.2 SOL; as built 15, 0.07 SOL); once that has spent the free pool, each further market 9 / 27 round trips (0.045 / 0.13 SOL) — all 20 markets 8.6 / 4.7 SOL against 4.8 / 1.5 SOL as built. LP-wrapped liquidity triggers: the first market 22,720 triggers (0.11 SOL; 69 market-hours at one per 11 s) against an unbatched keeper, 136,320 (0.68 SOL) batched; each further market 120 / 720 (0.0006 / 0.0036 SOL). Junk below the floor: at most 0.2 SOL a day (84 junk markets fill it at 0 µlamports/CU, ≥ 2.94 SOL of listings + 0.066 SOL a day; 15 at the ceiling). Junk above the floor hovering near a threshold: 14 (0 µlamports/CU) or 3 (the ceiling) junk markets, each holding `V` above the target's, spend `G` in a day — at `V` 1 SOL 40 / 8.5 SOL of capital and 0.076 / 0.016 SOL a day against the keeper's 1.0 / 1.3 SOL, at 25 SOL 995 / 213 SOL of capital and 1.9 / 0.41 SOL a day; hovering **and** bursting on their own pools (one round trip a minute; since M7D-4 the bursts are discretionary — their own entitlement and the free pool, never another market's —, so they drain the free pool and the hovering must still take the 20 real markets' entitlements), 3 / 2 junk markets — at `V` 1 SOL 8.5 / 5.7 SOL of capital and 0.61 / 0.41 SOL a day of round trips on a self-LP pool (11.4 / 7.6 at the full fee) against the keeper's 1.13 / 1.34 SOL (as built at decision A a burst on a hovering market was all exit-critical, ≈ 1.08 SOL a junk market-day: one junk market spent `G`). **Open (owner):** OWNER-M7-17 (its options (3) and (4); the defaults adopted by the owner with O18 on 2026-10-09, ECON §14 N25), OWNER-M7-2 (liquidity triggers under the global budget), OWNER-M7-6 (the overdraft) (§10).
9. **Degraded mode** (A69; ECON §5.8). When the keeper cannot meet duties 1–2 on a market (the budget can no longer cover it — since 2026-10-01 the global budget refusing its charge at its rank, duty 8 —, outage, contested blocks), throttling must be visible, not silent: without an honest observation in a second an attacker's atomic bundle achieves what ECON's held model assumes, so the §12.6 held-model numbers become that market's exposure.
   - **Opens pause** on that market with reason `KeeperCoverage`: by default the keeper pages the Emergency multisig, which calls `set_pause(market)`; if the owner approves O17's narrow role, the keeper calls `set_coverage_pause(true)` itself (pause-opens-only key, `coverage_authority`). The pause lifts after coverage has been restored for 10 minutes. **★M7 as built (O17 approved the role; `coverage.rs`, `alerts.rs`, config `[coverage_pause]`):** a market with open positions degrades on an outage over `COVERAGE_GAP_S` (40 s since the owner's decision of 2026-10-01, OWNER-M7-12; the program's `CoverageGap`), 3 consecutive missed required seconds (`degraded_after_misses`; isolated misses do not count — OWNER-M7-4), or a refused charge (duty 8: the global budget can no longer cover it at its rank); the **designated pauser** — one instance, `enabled = true`, holding the `coverage_authority` key (`--coverage-keypair`, never the fee payer) — sends `set_coverage_pause(market, true, 1)` in that tick (simulated, exit ceiling, outside the budget, retried each second until the flag matches) and `false` after `recovery_s` (600 s) of restored coverage (seconds that require nothing count as met, seconds the keeper was down do not); a flag it finds set (a restart, another instance) starts the market `Recovering` and is never lifted at once, so two instances never flip-flop it; markets without positions are never coverage-paused; without the key, with the role unset or rotated, it raises `CoveragePauseUnavailable` and the page to the Emergency multisig is the path; a refusal raises `CoveragePauseFailed`. `coverage_authority` sets and clears the flag, and **the Emergency multisig (`pause_authority`) can clear it too** (OWNER-M7-3 (b), owner decision of 2026-10-01; §3.1; never set it); opens resume `COVERAGE_CLEAR_DELAY_S` (5 s) after either clear. **The keeper and an Emergency clear:** the pauser sets a flag again in the tick it finds it cleared only on a market **it degraded itself and still holds degraded** (`CoveragePauseCleared`); a flag it found set and did not set (a restart, another instance, a compromised key) that the Emergency clears stays clear, the alert raised. A flag that turns set while the pauser runs without its having sent the set (seen clear, then set) raises **`CoveragePauseForeign`** (page: a compromised or second coverage key) and the market starts `Recovering`; a flag already set at its start is a restart's, as before. **Neutralising a hijacked coverage key** (runbook): page the Emergency, which clears each market the key paused (one `set_coverage_pause(false)` per market, ≈ 8,000 CU) and every later set the same way, while Governance rotates the key with the timelocked `Authorities` change (≥ 86,400 s); to override a pause of the honest pauser itself, first stop it (`[coverage_pause] enabled = false`, or restart it without `--coverage-keypair`), then clear (runbook in `services/README.md` "Degraded mode: runbook and drill"). **★Timing tolerances (M7-SEC-1, fixed):** the program measures a `CoverageGap` between two integrations' **landing** seconds while the keeper schedules its idle crank from the second it **read** (a `confirmed` clock), and on mainnet a tick that sends waits ≈ 1 s for its confirmations, so as built at M7 (a) an idle crank landing one second later relative to its read than the previous one was a 31-s gap in the keeper's own transaction — degraded, opens paused for ≥ 600 s — and (b) the recovery restarted at every tick that followed the previous one by more than a second: with 0–1-s landing jitter a quiet market with one healthy position was coverage-paused 99.7 % of two hours, and after a real outage the pause never lifted when the sending ticks were slow (the review's reproducers). Now (a) a `CoverageGap` in the keeper's own transaction degrades only above `max(idle_interval_s + gap_tolerance_s, COVERAGE_GAP_S)` (`CoverageConfig::gap_degrades_above`; metric `coverage_gaps_tolerated`) — 34 s with the 30-s constant, so a gap of 35 s or more; **since the owner raised `COVERAGE_GAP_S` to 40 s (OWNER-M7-12, 2026-10-01) the program emits no `CoverageGap` at the 30-s idle cadence under 0–2-s jitter, and every one it emits (a gap of 41 s or more) degrades** —, and a crank that does not land is still a miss; (b) a tick that skips at most `tick_gap_tolerance_s` (5) seconds misses only the seconds that required per-second coverage — counted like any missed required second, `degraded_after_misses` in a row degrade (as built a skipped second was never a miss, so a per-second market could go unobserved for 30 s without degrading) — and only a longer skip is "the keeper was down" (a degraded market's recovery restarts). Measured (`keeper-litesvm` `m7_sec`): landing delays 0/1/2 s with every sending tick followed by a skipped second for 7,200 s: never degraded, 0 s paused (with `COVERAGE_GAP_S` = 30, 79 of 241 observations' integrations emitted `CoverageGap{31–32}` on chain, all tolerated; at 40 s none — OWNER-M7-12, decided); the drill's outage lifts at +601–602 s with fast, all-slow or half-slow ticks; property tests of `MarketTrack` (`coverage.rs`). **★M7-SEC-3 (keeper side):** a flag found cleared while the keeper holds the market degraded and did not clear it raises `CoveragePauseCleared` (and the pauser sets it again in that tick); a position that appeared while the flag was last seen set raises `OpenWhileDegraded` (metric `opens_while_degraded`) — page the Emergency multisig, which can `set_pause(market)` (a pause the coverage key cannot clear), clear the coverage flag itself (OWNER-M7-3 (b), 2026-10-01) and have Governance rotate the key. The drill runs in CI (`keeper-litesvm` `coverage_pause`: an outage and a budget refusal pause opens in the same tick; `close_short`, `add_margin`, liquidations, settlements, `withdraw` and `claim_sol` land under the pause; the unpause after 600 s; a restart; the role unset, rotated, or without a key; two instances; the role through the real timelock).
   - **On-chain signal**: the program emits `CoverageGap{gap_s, open_positions}` at every integration that follows more than `COVERAGE_GAP_S` (**40 s**, owner decision of 2026-10-01, OWNER-M7-12; was 30 s) without one on a market with open positions; the indexer and UI show coverage per market and need no jitter tolerance at the keeper's 30-s idle cadence.
   - Existing positions keep their locked rules (A26); their exposure is disclosed as ECON §12.6's held-model bounds, and, after a venue switch whose guard-set seconds the keeper misses (duty 5), as ECON §12.12 residual 2: a deposit freeze can clear the guard; since #99 the carried positions fit the new pool's caps, so it delays their exits as in steady state, and the §3.6 cap bounds the pushed reference at `λ/λ_min` of the depth. Raising persistence in degraded mode is **not** adopted: persistence is locked per position, and 5 updates already break Tier C liveness (ECON §5.8).
10. **Venue drift monitor and the upgrade latch.** On a moved deploy slot of a venue ProgramData account (pump, pAMM, pfee, AMM v4, CPMM, Jupiter; plus Token-2022 for alerting), apply the program's AIR-01 rule: without a recorded fingerprint the slot decides; with one, `flag_venue_upgraded`'s own simulation judges, the tick's moved venues together (one fee read and one blockhash read at the same time, then the simulations in parallel). Either way an upgrade is flagged in the tick that sees it, before the tick's exits, at a high priority price, and an `ExtendProgram` of a fingerprinted venue is only counted, never flagged or paged. The simulation's `VenueNotUpgraded` counts as an extension only from a bank at or past the deploy slot the header showed; an earlier bank (an RPC node behind), another failure, or a refusal because short.win is not deployed in that slot leaves the slot to a whole read after the exits, which pages an upgrade at once, and the flag waits for a later tick (★keeper `d2bb168`, `a1edf78`, `bf037ef`; whole ProgramData reads only after the exits, once per deploy slot: a slot that simulation could not judge, a move during a review, the record of a reported deploy, Token-2022, whose extension is not alerted either). On an upgrade: alert, run the fork suite against the new binary, and page the Emergency multisig to `revalidate_venue`, publish an extras template set or set the route-broken flag as needed (the last two once O6 is signed). Also watch Raydium admin instructions (`SetParams`, `update_pool_status`, `update_amm_config`) and PumpSwap `disable_flags` (as built, M5: the pool-admin monitor skips curve markets — the curve's fee tier moves with its market cap, and completion is graduation, not a lost route; **M6**: `AdminChange::PammFlags{from, to, buys_halted}`, severe on any non-zero value — PumpSwap opens refuse `VenueFlagged` and, bit 0 (`create_pool`) set, curve opens refuse `GraduationHalted` (row 56, §3.4) — the buy bit also as RouteLost / RouteRestored; a PumpSwap fee change is reported only when it crosses the opens cap or the hard cap, the fee moving with its market-cap tier). Always select the extras set (`none` / `current` / `previous` / `stable`, M2-SEC-2) that simulates successfully (keeper v0 tries `current`, `none`, `previous`, `stable` in that order; ★it moves on after a venue failure or `BadExtras` / `BadRemainingAccounts` / `DeniedAccount`, the refusals that depend on the set — M10 batch 3, `121adda`; the web's `EXTRAS_RETRY_CODES` are the same three).
11. `crank_sol_usd` every ≤ 30 s with retries (55 s heartbeat; C1-12). **★M7 as built** (config `[oracle]`): every `interval_s` (30 s, bound (0, 30]) the keeper reads the configured Pyth `PriceUpdateV2` and, when it is newer than the cache and passes the program's own checks (`pyth::check`: verification, feed, age, confidence, step), sends `crank_sol_usd` at once (a global cost line: 6.1–6.6 k CU, ≈ 1,560 calls and 0.0078–0.0089 SOL a day at 0–100,000 µlamports/CU), retrying every second; `OracleRefused` once per reason, `OracleAging` when the cache is older than `aging_alert_s` (**300 s**, half of `oracle_stale_s`, at which every graduated market tiers C — **600 s since the owner's decision of 2026-10-01**, OWNER-M7-15; were 1,800 / 3,600 s), `OracleUnreadable` for a missing or undecodable feed (`keeper-litesvm` `oracle`: a deep mock market is Tier A on the keeper's fresh cache and Tier C 3,700 s after the feed stops — Tier C from 601 s at the new default). The cadence stays consistent with the new staleness: `interval_s` ≤ 30 s (validated, bound (0, 30]) is twenty cranking chances inside 600 s, and `aging_alert_s` is validated in (0, 600) — below the 600-s floor of `oracle_stale_s`, so the alert precedes Tier C at every value governance can set. **★`OracleAging` once per stall (M7D-6, fixed 2026-10-01):** the alert is raised once per cache `publish_time` (and hourly while one stall lasts); as built at decision C it was limited to once an hour across stalls — which held while Tier C came at 3,600 s —, so a second stall within ≈ 50 min of an alert reached Tier C (619 s) unalerted (`oracle::a_second_stall_within_the_hour_is_alerted_before_tier_c`: both stalls alerted at 301 s).
12. **Raydium pool monitor**: track `D` of every eligible pool; on markets with no open position, `propose_pool` a candidate with ≥ 25 % more locked depth (§2.6 rule 2) — in the same slot in which `open_positions` reaches 0 when a much deeper candidate is waiting. If a market stays pinned to a much thinner pool by a standing minimum position (R4B-10), alert and page Emergency to pause opens there so it drains. **As built (M4)**, on Raydium and list-only markets:
    - *Discovery*: four `getProgramAccounts` calls per mint (AMM v4 and CPMM, WSOL on either side; memcmp + `dataSize`), at first sight of a market, then every `discovery_interval_s` (300 s), every `fast_discovery_interval_s` (10 s) while the incumbent fails `pool_fail` or a window runs.
    - *Bounded ranking* (M4-SEC-7: anyone can create pools for a mint): each discovered pool is scored once per discovery by its locked SOL `λ·R`, from its pool account and one batched read of its WSOL vault and LP mint, at most `rank_keys_per_tick` (200) accounts per tick and market; only the best `max_candidates` (8) are evaluated. Unlocked liquidity scores nothing, so junk pools rank last.
    - *Evaluation and decision with the program's own code*: each ranked candidate's fresh ReadSet goes through `engine::pool_select::verify_candidate` (`D`, eligibility at `P_ema`), a list-only market's D1 through `classify_pump`; the market is projected to the clock with the prologue and `engine::pool_select::decide` runs on the deepest eligible candidate other than the incumbent and the window's own. The keeper sends `propose_pool` exactly when `decide` accepts (a list-only market's first pool, a listing-window replacement, a zero-position adoption in the tick the last position closes, a window) — every `eval_interval_s` (30 s), and every tick while the fast path is armed or a window runs.
    - *Off the critical path*: pool selection runs after the tick's exits and crank batch, and the observation that keeps a failing market's chain goes out in a batch of its own, so its RPC work never delays duties 1–4 (300 junk pools: the adoption lands at the same second, per-tick reads stay bounded).
    - *Pinned* (R4B-10): `Alert::PoolPinned` once a candidate that clears `pool_switch_margin_bps` has waited `pinned_alert_s` (3,600 s) behind open positions (`decide` returns `PositionsOpen`); the page to Emergency is the operator's.
13. **Lender pot**: `sync_lender` for lenders holding a surplus when some lender's claim is short of its entitlement (the frontend also prepends it; §3.3). ★A surplus holder behind a rebase record is touched unsigned (the pot-only touch, KI-66) with its records from its `fwd_epoch` once it has a forward chain (KI-66 full), up to 8 per transaction (`sync_lender(8)`, read-only records), repeated until `fwd_epoch` reaches the share epoch: its surplus up to the record and after it reaches the pot; only the latent rounding units wait for its owner. Since the eighth round the frontend's claim prepends the pot-only syncs the claimant needs (KI66-R4). `sweep_protocol_fees` daily; the cashback claim weekly for cashback-coin markets (curve: pump `claim_cashback(user = trader)` then `sweep_trader`, M5-SEC-1; PumpSwap: `[create ATA(trader, WSOL), pAMM claim_cashback, sweep_trader]`, §3.9); `sweep_trader` when an `ATA(trader, WSOL)` appears. **Built in M6** (`services/keeper/src/sweep.rs`, config `[sweep]`; PROPOSED ops knobs, recorded in ECON §15 under O17 by the owner's decision of 2026-09-30): the trader side is read every `check_interval_s` (60 s) and `sweep_trader` sent when something sits there; the cashback claimed at most every `cashback_interval_s` (604,800 s) once it reaches `cashback_min_lamports` (0.01 SOL), with the pAMM UVA created first when missing (M6-SEC-2); a PumpSwap claim costs the keeper the ATA's rent, which the sweep passes on to the lenders.
14. **CU and priority policy** (C0-17): `SetComputeUnitLimit` = simulated × 1.1; priority fee from recent per-account fees on `Market`, escalated when a transaction misses a slot, capped at the O17 ceiling. **★M7 as built:** limit `⌈simulated × 1.1⌉`; the price the p75 of recent per-account fees, ×1.5 per consecutive missed second, capped at **100,000 µlamports/CU** for observations and exits alike (O17); **per-slot CU policy (T-CASCADE, §6.6):** a market's exits book their requested CU against `market_cu_per_slot` (12,000,000, PROPOSED) and all of the keeper's against `payer_cu_per_slot` (20,000,000, PROPOSED); the first exit of a slot always goes, the rest wait for the next slot, most under-collateralised first (`ExitResult::Deferred`); **U28 telemetry:** a histogram of `⌊B̂_live·10⁴/B̂_ref⌋` at landed liquidations and expiries and at waits (`shortwin_keeper_exit_b_live_over_ref_bps`, 9,700–11,000 bps buckets).

- **Keys and ops:** a hot fee-payer key with a small SOL float and no protocol authority (the optional `coverage_authority` is a separate key that can only pause opens; ★M7: loaded on exactly one instance, the designated pauser; the others alert only). Two regions run concurrently; duplicate liquidations fail harmlessly. **★M7 load (K8, in-process, UNVERIFIED on a live RPC):** a tick takes 18.6 ms with 50 markets all due (9 v1 batches) and 73.7 ms with 200 (34 batches), every due market observed (`tests/bench/m7_keeper/results.md` "Load"); the keeper awaits its RPC calls one after another, so one instance keeps every market observed every second up to ≈ 650 markets at 5 ms RTT, 365 at 10 ms, 123 at 30 ms, 69 at 50 ms, 27 at 100 ms (targeted coverage makes only a share due in any second); beyond that, concurrent calls (not built) or instances with disjoint market sets (each its own sets' pauser; OWNER-M7-9). **★M7-SEC-8 (fixed, the per-tick reads):** as built every discovered market — list-only and junk ones included — was read in full every tick (`Market`, `MarketVault`, ReadSet, extras), its sweep facts in a read of its own each minute and its pool discovery (four `getProgramAccounts`) in the tick that first saw it; listing is permissionless (≈ 0.047 SOL a junk market by the review's count; ≈ 0.035–0.038 SOL at §3.2's rent), so junk markets slowed every tick of the only keeper (4.1 / 9.1 / 24.1 / 54.1 sequential requests a tick at 0 / 100 / 400 / 1,000 junk markets, 4 more per junk market in the tick that saw them). Now the tick reads the open positions first (one `getProgramAccounts`) and in full only the markets that need it — every covered market with positions (★decision A, duty 8: a market below `var_floor_lamports` every `idle_interval_s`, staggered, in the tick its positions change, and — M7D-1 — in the one or two seconds after an observation while a position is near an exit), every PumpSwap and Raydium market (real liquidity to exist), a curve within `hot_curve_completion_lamports` (20 SOL) of completion, and any market with something time-critical pending (a per-second, no-route, listing-window or warm-up need, a guard, a burst or liquidity window, degraded mode or the coverage flag, a graduation step, a post-wipe sweep, a pool-selection window, chain or ranking) —, the other list-only and curve markets every `cold_interval_s` (30 s) at a phase staggered by key; the due sweep checks of a tick are one read; at most `pool_select.discoveries_per_tick` (2) markets are discovered per tick (the fast cadence first, then markets with positions), a discovery's four calls in parallel; `RpcChain` sends a read's 100-key chunks in parallel (8 at a time). Measured (`m7_sec::m7_sec_8_*`): reads per tick 3.0–3.5 (max 4) at 0 to 1,000 junk markets, requests 4.2 / 7.2 / 12.9 / 14.2 a tick (mostly the bounded discoveries), the real market's idle cadence kept. A cold market without positions loses the per-tick burst detection it got as a side effect (its EMA bounds only its first open, which the spot–EMA guard and `X₀`'s minimum already hold), and a re-detection, a pool appearing or a curve completing from far away is seen within 30 s. Economic side (OWNER-M7-14, **decided 2026-10-01 — the global budget, duty 8**): as built at M7 a min-notional position on a self-lent junk market kept it hot and cost the keeper 0.0024–0.026 SOL per market-day against ≈ 0.001 SOL/day for the attacker, with no bound on the number of such markets; now such a market is below the value-at-risk floor — read and cranked at the idle cadence only, its cranks drawn from the free pool within `tail_share_bps` (0.2 SOL a day at the defaults), never from a covered market's entitlement. Prometheus metrics; alerts on missed liquidations (CR below L for more than N seconds), armed positions not re-checked, no-route markets not cranked, coverage SLO misses and budget burn. **★AIR-18 (keeper `8945087`):** a refusal "Program is not deployed" of a program whose ProgramData, read as of the refused slot, shows a deploy in that slot (two slots of slack) — the accepted bounded `ExtendProgram` griefing, §8.5 (g) — is counted (`not_deployed`) and sent again at the next tick, a later slot, with no alert or back-off; such refusals of one program, at most 5 s apart, are paged once when they have lasted 30 s (`ProgramNotDeployed`); the same refusal of a program that stays undeployable is alerted as any refusal.

### 7.2 Indexer and API (`services/indexer`, Rust)

- **Ingest:** Yellowstone transaction stream filtered on the short.win program id (until pump-final P6 also on the `complete_curve` helper, whose `CurveCompleted` / `CurveAlreadyComplete` were `emit!` log events decoded from its program logs; the helper is retired, owner decision D2, and no longer ingested), plus `getSignaturesForAddress` / `getTransaction` backfill; `emit_cpi!` events decoded from inner instructions and `CoverageGap` from program logs. Also every trade of every listed mint on its venue, for charts and **gap-frequency calibration** (ECON §11.6, G37): pump and PumpSwap events; AMM v4 `ray_log` (base64 bincode `SwapBaseInLog`/`SwapBaseOutLog`); CPMM `SwapEvent` (discriminator `40c6cde8260871e2`, **filtered by emitting program**, because Raydium CLMM and other programs emit an event with the same name and discriminator) [R-RAY §3.1–3.2].
- **Store:** Postgres via sqlx 0.9: `markets`, `market_snapshots` (from `PriceCranked`), `coverage` (gaps, pauses), `pools` (candidates, `D`, λ, switches), `positions`, `position_events`, `lender_positions` (incl. `lock_until`, pot draws), `lender_events`, `share_epochs`, `settlements` (incl. box corners), `fees`, `venue_events` (upgrades, latch flags, admin actions, route changes), `oracle`, `venue_trades`.
- **API:** axum 0.8 REST with OpenAPI plus WebSocket push: `/markets`, `/markets/{mint}`, `/markets/{mint}/pools`, `/markets/{mint}/positions`, `/markets/{mint}/coverage`, `/positions/{pubkey}`, `/lenders/{owner}`, `/stats`, `/events` (WS). Search by mint and ticker, always keyed by mint [R-MINT §10.11]. Analytics per SPEC §8/§13: TVL, utilisation, OI, fees, liquidations, S1/S2/S3 counts, **realised lender loss**, creator-wallet deposits (SPEC R1), **creator-fee income from short.win volume** (C0-18) and keeper coverage.
- The indexer runs the same byte-level mint filter and pool-eligibility checks to show reasons before "Create market" [R-MINT §10.10].
- **M8 contract:** [`docs/design/INDEXER.md`](INDEXER.md) — sources, commitment and rollback, idempotency and ordering, the event → table catalog, projections, venue ingest, the analytics formulas and SQL views, the API (`services/indexer/openapi.yaml`), abuse limits, deployment, the embedded-Postgres tests and the replay of LiteSVM-recorded sessions against the chain (the exit criterion's session; Surfpool optional), and the three tracks' file ownership. The byte-level mint check above is deferred to M9 (INDEXER.md §14 IX-7).
- **★M8 as built** (2026-10-01; INDEXER.md v1.1, changelog row 63): `services/indexer` (`shortwin-indexer`, one binary: `migrate`, `backfill`, `live`, `serve`, `rollups`, `run`, `replay`, `rebuild`). **Ingest:** the RPC backfill (`getSignaturesForAddress` + `getTransaction` at `maxSupportedTransactionVersion: 1` — keeper batches are v1) at `finalized`, live through `logsSubscribe` at `confirmed` with gap-fill, slot release in block order and a finality tracker that promotes or rolls back (cascade delete, rebuild, rollup reset); **Yellowstone is deferred to v1.1** (its client resolves but adds 33 packages and changes 6 lockfile entries; INDEXER.md IX-4); one Postgres transaction per Solana transaction, idempotent on `(signature, ix_index, ev_source, ev_seq)`, a single writer (advisory lock). Every short.win `emit_cpi!` event (parent checked), log events attributed through the invoke stack (a forged `Program data:` line is rejected), every short.win instruction's arguments at any stack height, complete_curve's events (until pump-final P6, which retired the helper's ingestion), the four venues' trades (pump `TradeEvent`, PumpSwap `Buy`/`SellEvent`, CPMM `SwapEvent` from the CPMM program only, AMM v4 `ray_log`), venue program upgrades; each event decoded by the program's own type and by the IDL, a disagreement quarantined. Inputs no event carries (the `ShareEpoch` record donation, a pool proposal's candidate kind, a config proposal's payload) are stored with the event (`events.derived`). **Store:** Postgres 17 through sqlx 0.9, 8 migrations (u64/u128/i128 as exact `NUMERIC` domains served as decimal strings). **Analytics:** 13 views and hourly rollups — TVL, utilisation, OI, fees by type, exits and rates, S1/S2/S3, realised lender loss (by condition), creator-wallet deposits and creator-fee income, keeper coverage and failures, slippage. **API:** axum 0.8, 31 paths under `/v1` (`openapi.yaml`, OpenAPI 3.1) plus `/v1/ws` (channels per market, position, lender, liquidations, admin, coverage, trades, stats; resume by event id; rollback messages); keyset pagination, RFC 9457 errors, GCRA rate limits with API keys, a query semaphore and timeouts, a read-only database role. **Tests:** PostgreSQL 17.11 embedded in user space (no Docker, no root); the API contract on a seed and on replayed sessions; the M8 exit's replay harness `services/indexer-litesvm` (§9). **Deployment:** `services/indexer/deploy/` (docker-compose, Dockerfile, roles; validated in CI, not run).

### 7.3 Frontend (`apps/web`)

- **Stack:** Vite + React 19 SPA; TanStack Router/Query; `@solana/kit` 8.3, `@solana/react`, `@solana/kit-plugin-wallet`; the Codama client `@shortwin/client` (zero-copy decoders generated from the IDL's `PodU128` fields, so offsets match the program, A67); `@shortwin/math-wasm` for quotes, CR, liquidation price and bounds. No web3.js v1 [R-TOOL §3].
- **Flows:** market search; create market (filter verdict, venue detection, Raydium candidate pools with `D`, λ, fee and eligibility, cost); lend, withdraw (pro-rata allowance, lock and `lock_until` shown), claim (vesting balance and pot shown; `sync_lender` prepended when the pot must be refilled), cover deficit; open short (Q, slippage → `min_proceeds`, D4 margin preview → `max_margin`, CR at spot and EMA, liquidation price, fees, rent estimate, max duration); position dashboard (SPEC §8 fields plus arming state and box width); `add_margin`; market page (tier and why — including "age counted from listing" under O13 —, adopted pool and fast-path state, inventory, utilisation, rate, OI, caps, keeper coverage, recent liquidations).
- **Transactions:** v0 with the protocol ALT; simulate before signing and show the effects (SPEC §9); detect CPI Guard [R-MINT §8.4]; randomise pump fee recipients from the on-chain lists; prepend idempotent ATA creation and `extend_account` when needed.
- **Disclosures:** SPEC §5.3's exact sentence with a required checkbox; ECON §11.6 break-even numbers; the ECON §9.3 run residual as a function of utilisation (up to ≈ 11 % of a runner's fair value at 50–60 % utilisation); lender lumps vest over 6 h and locks last until the positions they stand for have expired (+1 day); SOL that arrives while a market has no lender goes to the protocol; **the no-route freeze** (V2-5); the borrower-veto residual (ECON §12.9); the fixed 2 % liquidation bound (a keeper can take up to ≈ 2 % of the reference cost from a liquidated borrower, ECON §12.2) and the held-model residual (ECON §12.6); small positions depend on the in-house keeper, and a liquidation keeper is paid at least `K_s` from the borrower's remainder; a market whose keeper coverage lapses pauses opens; venue trust assumptions per market (pump upgrade key; **Raydium: no-timelock 3-of-4 upgrade multisig, unverified builds, 2-of-3 pool admin that can halt swaps or raise fees**); **R1: the coin creator earns the venue creator fee on every short.win leg** (C0-18 (2); ECON §12.8); geo-restriction at the CDN edge per legal advice (SPEC R6).
- **v1.1:** Jupiter quote proxy (the backend holds the API key) [R-JUP §8.6].
- **★M9 as built** (2026-10-02; FRONTEND.md v1.1, changelog row 64): `apps/web`, a Vite 8 / React 19 SPA (TanStack Router / Query, Kit 8.3 with `kit-plugin-wallet`, no web3.js v1 or wallet-adapter) on the Codama client and `packages/math-wasm` (the wasm-bindgen `--target web` build of `crates/shortwin-math-wasm`); dark-terminal design. **Money paths read the chain** (RPC at `confirmed`, the WASM math; previews held to `pool_model.py` vectors and to what the program booked on LiteSVM), **browsing reads the indexer** (REST, WebSocket with resume, an RPC fallback while it is down). **One transaction pipeline:** Codama builders and the venue layer (a TypeScript port of the keeper's account lists, checked against keeper vectors and `tests/fixtures`) → v0 with the protocol ALT → `simulateTransaction` (`sigVerify: false`, `replaceRecentBlockhash`, the watched accounts) → the review (the instructions decoded from their bytes, decoded deltas, compute and fee, the disclosures with their checkboxes; a review older than 20 s is re-simulated) → Wallet Standard signing with the pinned top-level allowlist and an intent check (only compute-budget changes within the fee ceiling pass) → confirmation → error mapping (short.win 6000–6104, ★M10: 6000–6105 with `AuthoritiesNotDistinct`; Token / Token-2022 incl. CPI Guard 42 and NoMemo 36). CPI Guard deposits are blocked with an opt-in bracket `[DisableCpiGuard, deposit, EnableCpiGuard]` (FE-1); a memo-required destination gets `memo_program`. Create market: the mint check ported from `shortwin_venue_state::mint::check`, venue detection, Raydium candidates with `D`, λ, fee and eligibility, the cost. Every SPEC §5.3 / §12 disclosure from one file, held to the spec by tests. Owner items FE-1 … FE-6 (FRONTEND.md §0) are built as recommended.
- **M9 contract:** [`docs/design/FRONTEND.md`](FRONTEND.md) — the information architecture and routes, every disclosure with its exact copy, the transaction lifecycle (Codama builders → simulation with `sigVerify: false` and `replaceRecentBlockhash` → decoded deltas → Wallet Standard signing with an intent check → confirmation → error mapping; CPI Guard and memo-required accounts; compute budget and priority fee), the data layer (indexer REST and WebSocket, RPC fallback, staleness), the dark-terminal design system, accessibility, security, the test plan (Vitest; Playwright on `solana-test-validator` with an injected Wallet Standard wallet), the `data-testid` contract and the four tracks' file ownership. Scaffold: `apps/web`, `packages/math-wasm`.


### 7.4 ★Governance tool (`services/ops`, `shortwin-gov`; M10 WP-7b)

A host-only CLI in the services workspace (package `shortwin-ops`; runbook in `services/README.md` "Governance"). It creates the two Squads v4 multisigs of §2.3.2 (autonomous: no config authority, no spending limits, each multisig's rent collector its own vault 0), runs `initialize_config` with their vault PDAs (it refuses a guard slot that differs from the live ProgramData), and stages vault transactions — the checked upgrade-authority transfer of both programs (`SetAuthorityChecked`, never the unchecked form), `Authorities` changes, upgrades (refused until the program's upgrade authority is the Governance vault 0), every admin instruction — through the stager's transaction buffer for a message over about 700 B (the worst-case `set_venue_extras` is 1,243 B staged directly), which an interrupted run resumes and `close-buffer` reclaims; every transaction is legacy, at most 1,232 B, paid by the acting member and simulated first; staging refuses a duplicate of the newest open transaction. `status` decodes every instruction of a staged transaction (short.win names with arguments and accounts, every `ConfigChange` value against the live config, loader and System instructions, the co-signers); `verify` asserts every derived address, fails on drift and warns on every Active or Approved proposal (an Approved one never expires, §8.5). **Members approve and execute in the Squads app**; the tool only stages and verifies (owner decision of 2026-10-03; no hardware-wallet support). Tests: `services/ops/tests/gov_e2e.rs` (T-OPS) on the mainnet Squads ELF.

## 8. Testing and security strategy

### 8.1 `shortwin-math` (host `cargo test`)

- **Unit tests plus proptest** (2,000 cases in CI): round trips never create value; `B̂` monotone in q for every venue family; `reprice` gives `Y/X ≥ P` (R3B-7 c); kinked-rate continuity at the kink; basis-index rent equals the direct integral; `receivable` returns to 0 with no open position under random `rent_protocol_bps` changes (I-P7); fee and penalty splits sum exactly; waterfall legs non-negative and sum to `V` including the keeper top-up (I-E4, I-E10); EMA step bounds and "own observation never read" (I-E7); directional aggregation (+0.00 % with one honest observation); the cached `(x, y)` of every ring entry equals `reprice(l, p)` after every integration and every `rewrite_liquidity`; the EMA leg reads only the newest `liq_persist_n` entries; **settlement box**: every predicate evaluated on the box equals its value at the named corner, one pushed second cannot change a box decision, and in a sustained uptrend the S1 corner is `P_ema` (I-E5, I-E8; §4.5); exit-bound properties with the fixed δ, the `lo_x` cap, no reserve in the liquidation bound and rent and the expiry fee senior in the expiry bound (v0.4.1; I-E1–I-E3, I-E11); S1 take = `V − K_s` and S1 whenever its legs hold on the box (I-E5); `D = λ·√(X·Y)` changes under swaps only by the retained fee (V2-7) and not under unlocked LP; lender pool: pot draws never exceed the own deficit, repeated claims pay 0, liveness after a full wind-down (I-P6), no lock effective at or after `lock_until`, vest release linear and complete at `vest_end`, credits with `S = 0` to the wipe record or the protocol; cap closed forms against brute force; U256 against num-bigint; `params::validate` equals `shortwin_sim.validate_params` on random configs, every compiled edge and the config gate's configurations, and `params::validate_econ` bounds exactly the parameters the sim does not model (T-CONFIG).
- **Differential tests against mainnet** (fixtures in `tests/fixtures/txs/`, every amount to the raw unit):
  - curve: `5hRKzXWt…`, `3pu4FB7r…`, `3QHQnT3S…`, `38PUmRjY…`, `cHHjJZFF…`, `535njpqh…` [R-PUMP §4.1];
  - PumpSwap: TX-BUY `udGBnNtp…`, TX-BUYQ `41XkmCLx…`, TX-SELL `2oSvEbDT…` [R-VEN §2.4];
  - Raydium (T-RAY-MATH): every signature in [R-RAY §0, §3.5, §4.1] — TX-V4-OUT2 `27EekaMR…`, TX-V4-OUT2-TOP `4PvobD1K…`, TX-V4-IN2 `4s6yJp8B…`, TX-V4-OUT1 `5Y8sTSnT…`, TX-V4-IN1 `5mXDiWRq…`, TX-CP-OUT `4dijJfUL…`, TX-CP-OUT-TOP `dR9wZQZw…`, TX-CP-IN-TOP `3Pp4LzfN…`, TX-CP-CFIN `qzC7eoYk…`, TX-CP-CFOUT `5vjTcH3h…` — plus the research's program-wide samples (388 AMM v4, 285 CPMM swaps);
  - ECON T1–T11.
- **Differential tests against ECON's models — v0.4.1, no exceptions** (R3A-3): port `sim/pool_model.py` **v0.4.1**'s fuzz (60,000 ops per configuration: continuous rent at 90 % and 100 % utilisation caps, repeated wipes with and without the post-wipe sweep, covers, governance changes of `rent_protocol_bps`, claims ×N, churn, sweeps) and its lock-heavy `lock_fuzz`, and assert **identical state traces** after every operation (lock calendar included), including the untouched-state I-P4 and the wind-down liveness check every 2,000 operations (I-P1–I-P7); compare `sim/shortwin_sim.py` **v0.4.1** quotes (incl. `B̂_str`; `B̂₂` only as a v1.1 unit test), observation/EMA/ring traces (incl. the cached `(x, y)` and venue-change rewrites), exit bounds, settlement-box decisions and waterfalls on the deterministic scenarios of ECON §11.2, the fast-path scenarios of ECON §10.3 and the 1,000-path exit fuzz of ECON §13 (S2 and S3 exits, noisy and freezer runs). Rent is compared **exactly**: the sims use the program's three basis indices, so the v0.3 "≤ 1 lamport per accrual" tolerance is gone; the settlement lump is computed from `⌊Q·P′/WAD⌋ + R_due` in both (v0.4.1, R4A-5; S2/S3, and S1 since ★AIR-21; `P′ = P_ema`, or 0 on a venue that cannot execute since ★AIR-09). The attack scripts of `sim/attacks/` provide the named traces (`fixed_delta.py`, `refute_push.py` with push-then-freeze and widening, `fv_push.py` with the S2 → S1 flip, push-then-freeze, consecutive-push and `p'` veto cases, `ptf_sandwich.py`, `venue_switch.py`, `pool_r3.py`, `cascade.py`); the config gate's 1,655-run battery is T-CONFIG's host part.

The differential vectors: `settle/trace_attacks_3.json`'s `venue_switch/RA` trace carries the adoption as `rewrite t R l_new slow_cap` (rewrite to the anchor, then `mark_restart`) followed by 8 warm-up rolls; `risk/exits.json` re-samples `FAST_SCENARIOS` (ECON changelog #96).
