- **Adversarial suite** (C0-12; each runs on the mock venue in M2 and on every real venue as it lands):
  - wrong, forged or **omitted** venue accounts on every instruction (C0-2, C0-15); non-canonical PumpSwap pool; spoofed curve owner; wrong creator vault; sensitive accounts as fee recipients or extras; a thin Raydium pool in place of the adopted one; a wrong ProgramData for `flag_venue_upgraded`;
  - trader griefing: lamport donations to the trader and to the `trader_wsol` address, token donations to `trader_base_ata`, a pre-created `ATA(trader, WSOL)` with WSOL (C0-3, C1-3); dust donation to the boost-vault ATA (C1-2);
  - **sandwich around `liquidate` and `expire`** at the fixed bound, acting at once and after waiting (ECON §12.2 `fixed_delta.py`); **held-model sandwich** (the penalty reserve keeps lenders whole, ECON §12.6); **atomic `[pump, crank, dump]` every second**, near-threshold pushes, fresh-position pushes, OI-basket forcing (ECON §12 scripts ported);
  - **round 3** (ECON §12.10–§12.11): S2 → S1 flip with 1–2 pushed seconds plus `[pump → sol_settle → dump]` (must fail; R3A-1); a borrower's one-second refutation push before maturity, repeated each cycle (S1 ≤ 4 s later; R3A-6 a); spot-leg vetoes of 12–20 s (clock keeps running; R3A-6 b); amount push up and down (≤ `fv_dev_bps`); deferral by repeated attacker-only seconds (keeper duty 2 bounds it); Emergency-flag S3 raced against an honest expiry (O15);
  - second round: block the spot leg with one low observation per second (it can no longer widen the bound); the borrower's defensive veto and "contrary observation every second" (V1-2, V2-14); atomic `[dump → sol_settle → buy back]` and `[deposit LP → sol_settle → withdraw LP]` every 20 s for 10 min (V2-4); unlocked LP added to the adopted pool (V2-8); fast-path front-running with an own pool and wash trading to raise `D` (V2-7); a venue that over-delivers tokens on a buy (V2-10); forced EMA-parameter adoption with positions open and the kink adopted only at 0 positions (V2-13, R3A-9);
  - lender: JIT deposit around rent and **around lumps** (`[deposit → expire / liquidate / claim_venue_rewards / sweep_trader → withdraw → claim_sol]`: 0 at `h = 0`; R3B-2); first-depositor inflation; **repeated full SOL settlements** (C0-6); **withdraw-then-settle in one transaction** (C0-9); early claim then shortfall and **exit with negative pending** (C0-13); **`claim_sol` ×N in one transaction** (V2-2); **withdraw between accrual and realisation, then wind down** (nothing stranded beyond dust; R3A-2); **open/close churn between a runner's withdrawals** (locks never decrease before `lock_until`; V2-3) and **steady borrowing after a withdrawal** (the lock clears at `lock_until`; R3B-1); **SOL credited after a full wipe** and a dust deposit (V2-12); **all lenders withdraw, then a sweep and a dust deposit** (the SOL goes to the protocol, not the depositor; R3A-10); **`rent_protocol_bps` changed with positions open** (no phantom receivable; R3A-5);
  - config: adversarial in-bound parameter changes with positions open (snapshots hold; C0-8); every compiled corner passes `config_check.py`; a change of the global hard cap moves only S3 / fast-path timing (A26); fee-config changes up to the venue's maximum; Raydium admin disable/fee hikes (the liquidatable set is unchanged above the hard cap; V2-1);
  - venue: ProgramData slot change (the latch refuses opens after `flag_venue_upgraded`; exits work), **venue ABI change with positions open** (C0-4), a venue-state layout change (not executable, S3 reachable; V1-8), completing buyback, straddle (tx3 priced by `B̂_str`, fallback without tx3, trade before the bundle), stuck migration (S3 at 70 min), boost window, creator change mid-position, mayhem and USDC curves at listing, zero-lamport borrower; small positions liquidated with the keeper floor (R3B-10).

(d) **Guard:** `ema_guard` goes 1 → 0 only at an integration with `ema_warm = 0` after it and `L_ema·10⁴ ≤ L_mlo·10,100`; an integration after the warm-up with the guard set never lifts `L_slow` above `max(L_slow before, L_mlo after)` (M4X-2); while it is 1, `Liquidate.b_ref` / `Expire.b_ref` equal the risk quote at `reprice(max(L_live, min(max(min(L_ema, L_mlo), L_slow), cap)), p_ref)`; while it is 0, at V2-14's `L_b` with the same cap (checked on every Raydium or PumpSwap market, and on any market while the guard is set); `cap = ⌊pool_d·10⁴/λ_min⌋` on Raydium (M4F-1, row 48; `λ_min = pool_lock_min_bps`) and ★PumpSwap (M6R-1, row 56; `λ_min` = 100 % since row 57's M6E-1, written out in the hook: `cap = pool_d`, so `L_b = L_live` — the pre-M6E-1 build fails it on `part_3a` / `part_3e`), none elsewhere. (e) **Spot leg** (FITS-2 (a), row 51): every `Liquidate` on an executable Raydium or ★PumpSwap venue is CR-liquidatable with its spot leg judged at `max(L_live, L_floor)` — `cr_spot_bps` recomputed from the risk quote at `reprice(max(L_live, L_floor), P_rs)`, `L_floor = min(L_ema, L_mhi)` while `ema_guard = 1` (★AIR-17; `min(L_ema, L_mlo)` before), else `L_ema`, at the exit risk fee cap (★AIR-10) — and below the position's `L`. (f) **PumpSwap warm-up depth** (★M6R-1, row 56): on a PumpSwap market whose post-instruction `ema_warm > 0` and `pool_d > 0`, `L_slow ≤ pool_d`, and a warm-up instruction without an integration moves `L_slow` only to `min(L_slow, pool_d)`. Lives in `tests/litesvm/src/invariants/confirm.rs`, wired into `check_ix`; mutants in `pool_select_it/hooks.rs`: skip the gate, seed from `max(cap, ·)`, never clear the guard; and in `m4r_it::m4x2_*`: `L_slow` lifted to the frozen `L_ema` |
| I19 ★ | **The open's terms, differentially** (★M7-SEC-6, added after the M7 security review: no hook recomputed an open's terms, so a mutant build that dropped D4's EMA leg, doubled the fee-scaled size cap, removed the wallet cap and assigned Tier C as B ran 15 minutes of the fuzzer with 0 failures). Every `Open`, from the state just before its instruction, the harness's own venue views and `shortwin-math` (never the program's glue): the locked terms are `config.tiers[tier]`'s and the config's (`lock_terms` field by field), `t_open = now`, `deadline = now + max_duration_s`, `V = S + M`; the tier is `tier::assign` on the post-roll market, the pre-trade real SOL and the cached oracle with its confidence (the curve: D); `q` within the per-position impact and fee-scaled caps on `X₀` (the curve's at `P_ema`; `conservative_x0` with Raydium's `λ_min` and PumpSwap's 100 %) at `min(φ_live, φ at P_ema)`, `ΣQ + q` within `OI_cap(X₀ + q)`, the wallet within `wallet_cap_bps` of it, Tier D's γ, `q ≤ T`; `N_open` the venue's buyback of `q` after the sale, `min_notional ≤ N_open`, `total_notional_open` up by exactly `N_open` and within `market_max_notional`; `B̂_ema` the buyback on the ring's newest cached reserves at the post-sale fees and `M = max(0, ⌈cr_open·max(N_open, B̂_ema)/10⁴⌉ − S)`; `fee_open = ⌈open_fee_bps·N_open/10⁴⌉`. Lives in `tests/litesvm/src/invariants/open_terms.rs`, called for every open from `positions::check_ix` (so in every program test and in the fuzzer); mutants in `invariants_m2_hooks::i19_the_open_terms` (D4 without its EMA leg, a tier one step better, the fee, the deadline and `N_open` off by one, a wallet beyond its cap); the review's mutant builds are `scripts/mutants.sh` |

**The M1 hooks** (`tests/litesvm/src/invariants.rs`, `invariants/lender.rs`; the LiteSVM `Env::send` runs them on every transaction). "After every instruction" is literal: a transaction of several instructions is replayed prefix by prefix on a clone of the VM, and instruction `k` is checked against the state after instructions `1..k−1`, with its own events and signers, so a latch set earlier in the same transaction counts for a later open and "admin-signed" (I4) is decided per instruction (M1-FID-3, M1-FID-5). Two hooks: **`check_all`** (per market, after each instruction and after a failed transaction): I1 in both directions (claims ≤ `T + ΣB_Q`, and the unclaimed rest ≤ the virtual and rebase-orphan shares' part plus one unit per lender; M1-FID-1), I2, and I8 on the state the program sees — every lender touched as `pool_model.check()` does, I-P4 also on the untouched state, the calendar, the wind-down liveness, and **`S = 0 ⇒ ΣB_Q = 0`** (M1-SEC-3); **`check_ix`** (per instruction, against the state just before it): I4, I17, and the lender bounds — each withdrawal within the allowance its lender had just before it, no share reduction with `pending < 0`, each claim ≤ the claimant's entitlement just before it, token conservation of deposits and withdrawals, and locks never decrease before `lock_until` (M1-FID-1, -4, -9). Each check has a mutant test (`lender_it/hooks.rs`). M2 adds its invariants to the same two hooks and completes the parts marked `TRACK:` (positions in I2 and I4, opens in I17). **M4** adds I15 (`invariants/pool_select.rs`, in `check_ix` against the state just before the instruction and its own `PoolSwitched` / `PoolProposed` / `PoolSwitchCancelled` / `Open` events; the adopted pool is read by the harness from its own accounts) and I17's pool part (listings, adoptions and window candidates); an adoption exempts its market from the one-step `L_ema` bound (I13) and the chain rules (I16), which I15 replaces; mutant tests in `pool_select_it/hooks.rs` (`i15_adoption_rules`, `i15_window_rules`, `i15_fast_adoption_needs_the_arming_chain`, `i15_open_sizing`). Only the `pool_model` trace replays relax `S = 0 ⇒ ΣB_Q = 0` (`allow_shareless_borrow`), because the model borrows orphan tokens with no shares, which `open_short` refuses (§9).

### 8.4 Fuzzing, static analysis, fork E2E

- **The invariant fuzzer (★M7 as built; OWNER-M7-5, §10: not Crucible).** `tests/fuzz` (package `shortwin-fuzz`, in the root workspace): seeded **action sequences** on LiteSVM 0.16 through the program-test harness, so every transaction runs `Env::send`'s hooks — I1–I13, I15–I19 and A26 after every instruction and after every prefix of a bundle (§8.3; I14 structurally, plus the fuzzer's omit / replace check) — against the test-venue build and the sha-checked mainnet forks; six profiles (`mock`, `mixed` on the test-venue build; `curve`, `pumpswap`, `amm-v4`, `cpmm` on the release build); `replay` and `tmin` (delta debugging over the recorded action list) are deterministic; crash files hold profile, seed, action list, signature and logs; a corpus of minimised reproducers replays in CI (a finding marked fixed must pass). **Why not Crucible** (the v0.4 plan below said "Crucible via `anchor fuzz`, invariants I1–I17"): Anchor 1.2.0's `anchor fuzz` embeds crucible-fuzz-cli 0.2.1, whose harness crates pin `litesvm =0.15.2` and `solana-program-runtime ~4.1.1`, while this lockfile pins LiteSVM 0.16.0 and the Agave 4.2.2 line (C1-14): the two runtimes cannot share it, so a Crucible harness could not link the ≈ 5,200 lines of I1–I18 hooks and the fork fixtures without a rewrite on a second Agave line, and its default stateful depth (15 actions) is short for the clock-driven paths (a run here is 100–400 actions, warping up to 3 d each). The public RPCs refuse Surfpool's batched reads (HTTP 403), hence the forwarder; a CI job would need network access, so it is not in CI. ★pump-final §14's once-before-the-release fork run of a synthetic close (`graduation_surfpool.rs`, which still names the 2026-10-02 builds) has **not** run for 1.0.1 (no Surfpool on the machine that built it; AUDIT §13).

### 8.5 Security posture and trust assumptions (disclose)

- **Upgradeable dependencies.** pump, pAMM and pfee share upgrade authority `7gZuf…` and ship several upgrades a month [R-PUMP §1; R-VEN §7]. Raydium AMM v4 and CPMM share a Squads v4 upgrade multisig (3 of 4, **no timelock**) and have **no verified builds** on verify.osec.io (★M10: CPMM's 2026-10 redeploy, 452,376,460, was rebuilt byte for byte from `raydium-cp-swap@bdeee23`; AMM v4 stays a behavioural match, U12); the pool admin (Squads v3, 2 of 3, no timelock) can halt individual pools and raise fees [R-RAY §1, §5]. Token-2022 is upgradeable by `AeLmXC…` [R-MINT §2]. Our own program is upgradeable by the Governance multisig (48 h), and since pump-final P6 it is Governance's whole upgrade set (the 1.0.0 layout also named the `complete-curve` helper, retired before it was ever deployed, owner decision D2; `shortwin-gov` refuses a layout that names it; KI-45). ★On 2026-10-02 pump, PumpSwap and pump-fees were redeployed after the M10 fixtures were dumped [V21]; the M10 pump revalidation re-dumped them (`pump_programs_2026_10`), re-ran every pump suite on them, replayed the real upgrade in T-LATCH and fixed PUMP-2026-10-1 in program batch 4 (U30); on mainnet the latch refuses opens on those venues until Emergency revalidates them at their live slots.
- ★**First-trade venue rent on short pump accounts (PUMP-2026-10-2; disclosed, the owner's decision of 2026-10-03; no program change).** Since the 2026-10-02 redeploys the first trade on a PumpSwap pool shorter than 287 B, or a curve shorter than 141 B, grows the account and charges that trade the rent: 81,280–386,080 lamports measured (a 271-B pool or 125-B curve at minimum rent 81,280; a 115-B curve 132,080; a 211-B pool 386,080). short.win nets it out of the open's `S` (`Open.venue_rent`), so an open whose 10-bps tolerance cannot cover it fails `ProceedsBelowMin` though no price moved; on a 211-B pool held at its minimum rent no open within the default wallet cap qualifies (the cap's edge, 1.814 % of the pool's tokens, has a 337,498-lamport tolerance; 2.1 % is `CapWallet`) until any trade grows the pool. On 125-B curves at minimum rent opens below ≈ 0.08 SOL of proceeds are refused likewise. The web explains such a refusal (FRONTEND §5.9). Exits pay the same rent out of the buyback (I13 nets it).
  - The venue guard pauses **opens** only, and only once the latch is set: an open that lands between an upgrade taking effect and `flag_venue_upgraded` (the keeper's reaction time, normally the next slot) is accepted. A malicious venue upgrade can still harm exits; no design can prevent that (SPEC R5). The route-broken flag (after O6) and S3 bound the time **liquidatable** positions stay frozen; healthy positions on a halted or broken venue can be neither closed nor settled until the route returns, an upgrade adapts the adapter (48 h), or their deadline (up to 30 days); owner options in §10 O14 (V2-5).
- **Admin powers of short.win** (§3.1): timelocked parameters inside compiled bounds, each proposal gated by the ECON liveness battery; Emergency: pause opens, disable a venue for opens, re-validate a venue, (after O6) the route-broken flag and bounded extras, and (since 2026-10-01, OWNER-M7-3) clear — never set — a market's keeper coverage pause; the optional `coverage_authority` pauses opens only. No fund movement; no venue-id changes. ★Since M10 the program refuses a configuration in which two of `governance`, `pause_authority`, `fee_recipient` and an installed `coverage_authority` share a key (SQ-G8, §2.3.2).
- ★**Squads v4 semantics (M10; owner layout of 2026-10-02; `squads_gov_it` T-SQ-2, -4, -6, -7).** (a) **An approved Squads vault transaction never expires**: a year later it still executes, and a `propose_config` inside it replaces whatever change is pending then. (b) It survives a member rotation and a threshold increase and executes with the approvals it had; only Active proposals and config transactions go stale. **A time-lock increase does not stale it but delays it**: Squads checks the multisig's current time lock at execution, counted from the approval. Hygiene: cancel unwanted approved proposals with `proposal_cancel_v2` (threshold votes); `shortwin-gov verify` warns on every Active or Approved proposal. (c) **Governance cannot cancel reactively inside the program window**: its `cancel_config` executes at `not_before` at the earliest, when anyone can apply; only the Emergency (time lock 0) can cancel a parameter change in time, and it cannot cancel `Authorities` or `Timelock` changes (M1-SEC-1). (d) **The Emergency cannot veto upgrades**: an upgrade needs only the Governance vault after its 48 h Squads time lock (no program timelock applies to the loader), and Emergency members cannot vote on Governance proposals. (e) A parameter change takes 96 h end to end (48 h Squads + 48 h `timelock_s`). (f) A refused vault execution stays Approved and can be re-executed later. (g) `ExtendProgram` is permissionless in Agave 4.2 (one extension per program per slot, at least 10 KiB). It is not harmless (★AIR-18): it redeploys the program at the current slot, so the program is unusable for the rest of that slot (every invoke or CPI fails `UnsupportedProgramId`), and it moves the deploy slot. Anyone can therefore block every `shortwin` instruction for the rest of a slot (the retired `complete_curve` is never deployed, pump-final D2), once per slot, for ≈ 0.052 SOL of rent per blocked slot (mainnet 5,080 lamports/byte) plus the fee, until its ProgramData reaches the loader's 10 MiB cap (≈ 867 slots, ≈ 45 SOL, if its ProgramData is allocated at its v1.0.0 ELF size; paid by the attacker); the exits that CPI an extendable venue program (pump-fees, AMM v4, CPMM, Token-2022; pump and PumpSwap sit at the cap) likewise, ≈ 887–947 slots and ≈ 44–49 SOL per venue at the fixtures' sizes (the loader charges only the shortfall below rent exemption: on AMM v4 and Token-2022 the first ≈ 34 / ≈ 50 extensions cost only the fee). That is at most ≈ 5.8–6.3 min of blocked slots per program at 400 ms a slot (≈ 5.1–5.5 min at SIMD-0525's 350 ms). These bounds rest on SIMD-0431's 10 KiB minimum extension (active on mainnet; with 1-byte extensions they would be millions of slots). No program change can stop third-party extensions. The owner accepted this bounded griefing on 2026-10-12 instead of extending short.win's ProgramData to the 10 MiB cap at deployment (≈ 45 SOL of rent): the keeper sends a blocked transaction again at its next tick, a later slot, without alerting (keeper `8945087`, §7.1; known issues KI-73). An upgrade to a larger ELF needs an extension first, or it fails at execution after the full time lock. For the venues' latch, AIR-01's content rule keeps an extension from latching opens (§2.3.2). (h) **No spending limits** are created on either multisig (`shortwin-gov` creates none and `verify` checks the config authority is unset), so no member can move vault funds outside a time-locked proposal. Members sign in the Squads app; `shortwin-gov` only stages and verifies (owner decision of 2026-10-03), and the Emergency runbook does the worst-case `set_venue_extras` as 3 single-signer transactions.
- **Creator self-dealing (R1):** the coin creator earns venue creator fees on every short.win leg (§7.3; ECON §12.8).
- **Residual economic risks** (ECON §8.2, §9.4, §12.2, §12.6, §12.9–§12.11): the fixed 2 % bound lets a keeper take up to ≈ 2 % of the reference cost from a liquidated borrower at the first second (Tier A +1.50 SOL over an honest keeper, borrower −2.02 SOL; v0.3 +0.71 at once but +3.86 after 4 s); under the held model a keeper takes the remainder of a borrower already being liquidated (Tier A +8.36 SOL, borrower −19.5 SOL; +5.66 SOL before ★AIR-22's lower-median growth, with which two held seconds do what took three, ECON #117) and, because a liquidation reserves nothing (v0.4.1), lenders and protocol lose the penalty and — on positions whose rent due exceeds `K_s` — the rent that the bought-down vault no longer covers (Tier A −3.34 SOL fresh, −4.54 SOL aged 25 days at 90 %; −2.06 / −8.02 SOL before ★AIR-22; v0.4's claim that "lenders are never worse off thanks to the penalty reserve" was wrong: that reserve blocked honest liquidations and did not hold on aged positions, and since ★AIR-22 it only trims the loss on fresh ones); low-fee Raydium baskets stay marginally profitable at the OI cap (+0.5–8.5 SOL); the borrower's paid veto of its own liquidation; a settlement-amount push of at most `fv_dev_bps` (±1 %), a settlement deferral of ≈ 13 s per attacker-only second, and (v0.4.1) an indefinite, paid deferral of S1 or an S3 on an executable venue by a contrary observation every second (0.002–0.21 SOL/s); **5 consecutive attacker-only seconds** (degraded mode, a censored keeper) move the box's medians and flip a capped S2 into S1 on the drained-RA model cases (+2.37 to +5.58 SOL for 1.1–2.0 SOL); a lender that exits forfeits its unreleased vest to whoever stays; a standing minimum position can pin a Raydium market to a thinner pool (§2.6); the ECON §9.3 run residual (up to ≈ 11 % of a runner's fair value, depending on utilisation); rebase-orphan dust (negligible except in dust-sized pools, ECON §9.5; ★in such a pool, if every real lender leaves while a vest runs, the orphan shares take the whole unreleased vest — the rebase-orphan vest, found by the final tree's 24 h fuzz, 0.054 SOL in its triaged reproducer and up to ≈ 0.218 SOL of orphan credit in one wind-down not yet classified; a lender avoids it by waiting for the market's `vest_end`; KI-65); in degraded mode, a market's exposure is the held-model bound. ★**Measured on the real venues in M10 (WP-8b; owner decision of 2026-10-03 on O19: accepted and disclosed, no program change):** the §12.6 held sandwich at cap size, 3 s held at +15 % before the sandwich — AMM v4 net **+61.27 SOL** (borrower 237.67 → 101.74 SOL; +22.72 for the atomic sandwich), PumpSwap **+10.20 SOL** (+2.55 atomic), CPMM USELESS +37.33 SOL (+13.95 atomic; the atomic sandwich's extra over an honest keeper, the figure the owner's decision cites, is **+5.34 SOL**); the loss falls on the **liquidated borrower** — the lenders' and protocol's legs are the honest run's within a few thousand lamports (the front-run's fees lower `B̂_ref` by ≈ 1e-7) and rise under the held model, because the reference is lifted; I11 holds over the lifted reference; keeper competition is the M11 lever. *(These real-venue figures were measured before AIR-22. With the lower-median growth two held seconds open `κ_eff`, so the sim's held plan on RA is 2 s at +15 % instead of 3 s (+2.839 SOL instead of +1.981; ECON §12.6); the real venues have not been re-measured under it (O19 re-measurement open).)* ★**Late-depositor shortfall (ECON §9.4; owner decision of 2026-10-03):** a shortfall is debited pro rata to the shares holding when it lands, so a lender that deposits while a position carries a large credited receivable can owe more SOL than it received (the fuzzer's FUZZ-M7-24H-3: ≈ 1,044 SOL after 3 days without a keeper on a near-cap position) and must cover a negative `pending` with `cover_deficit` before withdrawing; no program change — the web's deposit review shows the receivable the deposit meets (the stored `receivable` plus the credit its own prologue books first) and this deposit's part of it, ⌈receivable·shares/(S + shares)⌉, warning at ≥ 1 % of the deposit's value at `P_ema` or ≥ 1 SOL (`lender.unpaidRent`, FRONTEND §3.6, §4.2). ★**Extras denylist residuals** (M10 batch 3, §2.4 rule 4). All disclosed; ★accepted by the owner on 2026-10-03 (fourth round; §10; KI-54 … KI-57).
- Before mainnet: external audit (SPEC §9), `security.txt` / `security.json` [R-TOOL §5.1], verifiable build, bug bounty. ★**As built in M10:** both release ELFs embed security.txt (§1.1; the CI release gate `check-security-txt.py --forbid-placeholders`; none in the test-venue ELF); the web serves RFC 9116 `/.well-known/security.txt` with the same contacts (Expires 2027-09-30, rotate before 2027-08-31) and a `/security` policy page; `SECURITY.md`. Anchor 1.2.0 has no `security.json` / `--security-metadata` (unreleased upstream), so a PMP `security` upload through Squads is M11's. The verifiable build is §1.1. **The audit package:** `docs/AUDIT.md`, `docs/audit/{scope.txt, known-issues.md, findings.md}`, `scripts/audit_scope.py`; the owner books one full private audit plus a public contest (Sherlock or Cantina) on the fixed code, then a bounty at beta (Q2, 2026-10-02); the keeper's core subset (≈ 4.7k nLOC) is in scope.

## 9. Milestones

Each milestone is small, merges behind CI, and has testable exit criteria. **M0, M0b and M1 involve no venue at all; M2 builds the whole position engine against a test-only mock venue.** Real venues then arrive one per milestone, Raydium first because it is the simplest adapter (no venue-side rent, no fee tiers, 3 trace entries per swap, no graduation).

**Carried-over model notes** (implement exactly as `pool_model.py` v0.4.1 and keep the pinned vectors): (1) the lock term `⌊lock·WAD/Π⌋` can exceed u128 after deep reductions because Π resets only at `ΣB_Q = 0` and, ★since AIR-12, at each lock era's first lock (`Π = WAD` with `b_min = ΣB_Q` once `lock_norm` is 0 — the effect of the fix proposed here, rolling the Π epoch whenever `lock_norm` reaches 0, without the roll), refusing a withdrawal (`Overflow`) until then; within one era Π telescopes to `≈ WAD·ΣB_Q/b_min`, so this needs an open inventory below ≈ 5·10⁻¹⁴ of `b_min` (fewer than ≈ 53 raw units against a 10¹⁵ supply), which `min_notional` rules out below a price of ≈ 1.9 mSOL per raw unit (before AIR-12 the eras' decays compounded, `pool_model.lock_era_demo`: Π fell to 1 by the sixth era); (2) **fixed in v0.4.1**: v0.4's ceiled `locked` could exceed `Σ lock_i`, which let two one-share lenders each draw all of `T` (the reviewers' lock-heavy fuzz found it); terms and the aggregate are now floored; (3) **fixed in v0.4.1**: rolls scale every calendar bucket and each lender's `lock_term` at conversion; (4) if the last shares can leave while dust is borrowed (`S = 0 ∧ ΣB_Q > 0`), a continuous rent credit reaches the protocol sink before any SOL exists, which the program's u64 `lender_sol` would refuse; **built in M1** (M1-SEC-3): `withdraw` refuses to take the last shares while `ΣB_Q > 0` (`LastSharesBorrowed`), and M2's `open_short` must refuse while `total_shares == 0` (tokens without shares — the virtual shares' part, rebase orphans — are not lendable; `pool_model` borrows them, which is why the LiteSVM replays relax the hook's `S = 0 ⇒ ΣB_Q = 0`, §8.3). Neither (1) nor (4) is reachable by the v0.4.1 fuzz or by the round-3 and round-4 attacks.

The O1/O2 alternatives are **not built at all** (no parameters, no bounds; reserved bytes only). ## 10. Open decisions for the owner

D1–D4 are decided (SPEC v0.3). The adopted first-pass defaults Q4–Q24 appear in §11 as parameters. Eight decisions were listed; SPEC §0 and §14 now record O6, O15, O16 and N22 as owner decisions (the O15 row states the recorded scope, S2 and S3). Each has a recommendation, which is also what the build does until the owner rules, and each needs a SPEC §14 entry (SPEC §15).

Neither moves funds; the flag only refuses opens and starts the S3 chain; a bad extras set cannot brick exits (callers pick `none` or `previous`). They are not built until recorded (R3A-8 b) | building them (M2 at the earliest) |

(b) is simpler, but a lender holding for 6 h takes 90 % of a position's rent and lump, against 90 % of the lump only under (a) (ECON §9.4) | M1 |

| **O17** | Keeper operating budget per market, priority-price ceiling, which markets are covered, and whether to enable the pause-opens-only `coverage_authority` for automatic degraded mode — **✅ decided by the owner (SPEC §14, 2026-09-30) and built in M7** (§3.1 `set_coverage_pause`, §7.1 duties 8, 9, 14); **the budget redecided on 2026-10-01 (SPEC §14 M7-13 / M7-14, decision A): one global daily budget `G`, funding the covered markets in order of their lenders' value at risk `V = ⌊ΣB_Q·min(P_ema, P_ACC_MAX)/WAD⌋`, replaces the per-market budget as the primary control; bursts and liquidity-anomaly coverage draw on it; markets below `var_floor_lamports` get the 30-s idle cadence only; a market it can no longer cover is degraded, per market as before (§7.1 duty 8, the exact algorithm)**; **measured (M7, ECON §5.8, `keeper_cost.py`):** a quiet market 0.0024 SOL per market-day batched (v1 k = 6) and 0.0144 unbatched at 0 µlamports/CU, 0.0118–0.0143 / 0.0238–0.0263 at the ceiling; targeted coverage with 5 % of the day near a threshold 0.0059–0.0088 batched at 0–10,000, 0.029–0.035 at the ceiling; per-second coverage all day 0.072–0.108 batched at 0–10,000, 0.355–0.428 at the ceiling (0.432–0.788 unbatched); the open sub-items are OWNER-M7-2, -4, -6 and -17 below (-7 superseded by -17; -13 and -14 decided) | **Cover every market with open positions at targeted coverage** (≈ 0.003–0.03 SOL per market-day; measured 0.0024–0.035), **ceiling 100,000 µlamports/CU**, **enable the role**; since 2026-10-01 **one global budget, prioritised by value at risk** (`G` 1 SOL a day, floor 1 SOL: OWNER-M7-17's defaults, adopted by the owner with O18 on 2026-10-09) | Per-second coverage of every market costs 0.07–0.10 SOL per market-day batched, more than a 25 SOL beta market earns (0.005–0.04 SOL/day protocol rent); an uncovered market must pause opens visibly, and a human-paged pause is slower than the attack (ECON §5.8). The budget must include the post-switch duty (row 48): every second while a switch's reference guard is set on a market with positions (≈ 9 cranks after an honest switch; one a second while a deposit freeze from the adoption is paid). ## Appendix A. Review resolution

### Review resolution — round 4 (fourth review, `R4A-x` / `R4B-x`)

One row per finding of the fourth 2026-09-27 review. Every finding was re-checked before it was fixed: the reviewers' scripts (`scratchpad/r4/resolution/exp/*`, `scratchpad/r4/fresh/sim/*`) were re-run against the v0.4 sims and reproduced, then against the v0.4.1 sims; the new or changed evidence lives in `sim/attacks/` (`fv_push.py` (M) push-then-freeze, consecutive pushes, (V) `p'` veto; `refute_push.py` (c) push-then-freeze, (d) widening; `ptf_sandwich.py`; `sandwich.py` reserve-rule section), `sim/pool_model.py` (the R4 demos and `lock_fuzz`) and `sim/config_check.py` (the 1,655-run battery). **All 20 findings are resolved**: 16 FIXED as proposed or with an equivalent mechanism, R4A-8 / R4B-8 FIXED by a different mechanism, R4A-9 and R4B-10 as disclosed residuals. **Three contain proposals REJECTED with evidence**: the rent-only reserve of R4A-1 / R4B-1 (it has the same dead band once rent due exceeds `K_s`; a third rule — no liquidation reserve — is adopted instead), part of R4A-4 (two of its failing examples were artefacts of the withdrawn reserve and of position size), and the threshold vest flush of R4B-4 (it re-opens just-in-time sniping). Section references are to this document unless marked ECON; ECON changelog #74–#89 has the economic side.

| ID | Sev. | Finding | Outcome | Where the fix lives |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| R4A-1 | HIGH | v0.4's penalty reserve in `max_in` blocks honest liquidations in genuine fast pumps (the live cost sits a few tenths of a percent above the lagging reference, `max_in` collapses to `B̂_ref·(1 + ε)`, the position gaps into S1); it alone made τ = 6 and κ = 2,250 fail; ε became load-bearing | **Reproduced** (6 of the 960 grid cells, lenders −32 … −63 % instead of +0.4 … +3.1 %). **FIXED with a third rule:** of the two options offered, (1) the v0.3 rent-only reserve has the same dead band once rent due exceeds `K_s` — aged positions: C at 6 days and 90 % utilisation, S1 −46.1 % instead of liquidation +0.6 % on the new battery, 3–4 more runs at in-bound maximum rates; (2) as written, `max(V − R − π_ref − ert, min(V − R − ert, bound))` reduces to the rent-only reserve **without** the ε fallback (it never reserves π), so it is not an intermediate. Any reserve blocks exactly the buybacks in `(V − R − π_ref − ert, min(bound, V − K_s − ert)]`. v0.4.1: **a liquidation reserves nothing** (`max_in = min(⌊B̂_ref·(10⁴ + δ)/10⁴⌋, V − K_s − ert)`, SPEC §5.2); an expiry keeps rent and fee senior (no battery run changes with any expiry rule); ε enters only the expiry bound. Trade-off stated (ECON §8.2 table): held model on aged Tier A at 90 %: lenders + protocol −8.02 SOL (rent-only −1.92, v0.4 −5.72); fresh positions identical to rent-only (−2.06). The genuine-pump grid and per-second noise are in `config_check.battery()` (1,655 runs); τ and κ re-derived on it (τ = 6 loses 83 runs, κ = 2,250 38 — bounds unchanged, reasons new). ECON #50, §0 finding 5, §5.7, §12.6, §15 and §3.6 / §8.5 here ("lenders never worse off") corrected | §3.6, §3.7, §5.2, §8.5, I11; ECON §8.2, §5.7, §12.6, #74–#76 |
| R4B-1 | HIGH | Same dead band, shown with per-second price noise (±0.3 %: 42 S1 against 36; the sims set the price once per second, so `B̂_live = B̂_ref` hid it); asks for noise in the battery and a liveness invariant | **Reproduced** (42 vs 36 S1 at ±0.3 %; 6 cells worse). **FIXED** with R4A-1: no liquidation reserve, so the requested invariant holds exactly — a liquidatable, buyback-allowed position with a fresh bucket never waits while `B̂_live ≤ ⌊B̂_ref·(10⁴ + δ)/10⁴⌋` (ECON I-E11, I11 here; the exit fuzz counts `reserve_waits_liq` = 0 in 1,000 paths). Noise of ±0.3 % and ±1 % is in the battery (the lag-study pumps included) and in half of the exit fuzz's paths (22 sandwich truncations in 709 exits, all within the bound's slack). The reviewer's own remark — a fallback tolerance equal to δ is the same as reverting — is why no ε-widening was tried. ECON #50 and §0 finding 5 corrected | §3.6, I11; ECON §8.2, §5.7, §13 |
| R4A-2 | MED | An expired lock stays in `lock_norm` until its holder is touched, so every other lender's allowance counts it and early withdrawers take more than pro-rata (Σ allowances up to 3.0·T); `check()` touched everyone first and could not see it | **Reproduced** (92 of 954 sampled untouched states above `T`, worst 2.72·T). **FIXED**: a lock expiry calendar — 128 day buckets of lock terms on a zero-copy `MarketVault`, `lock_until` rounded up to its day's end, the aggregate drops a bucket when its day ends, whoever is touched (A75). Floored lock terms and aggregate fix a second violation the reviewers' lock-heavy fuzz exposed once expiry was exact (all lenders locked to rounding dust: two one-share lenders could each draw `T`; 1 of 954 states, 1.27·T — measured with Π kept across lock eras, before AIR-12 restarted it at each era's first lock). `pool_model.check()` asserts I-P4 on the state the program sees (each lender touched alone): 0 of 954. The stuck-lock scenario now pays the idle lender its pro-rata part (F 0.4, G 0.4, E 0.2 of `T`; v0.4: 0.5 / 0.5 / 0). The alternative (roll the Π epoch once `now ≥` the latest `lock_until`) was not adopted: while lenders keep locking, the latest `lock_until` keeps moving | §2.3.6, §3.3, I8, T-POT (A75); ECON §9.3 |
| R4B-3 | MED | Same (idle lender past `lock_until`, others withdraw first) | **FIXED** with R4A-2. Day buckets instead of the suggested weekly ones: a lock is extended by less than a day, not up to a week, at 2 KB of zero-copy state | as R4A-2 |
| R4A-3 | MED | FV's `p'` (penalty vs expiry fee) came from the raw "CR-liquidatable" flag; one contrary low observation fails its robust-spot leg and both box corners used the manipulated `p'` (S3 take −2.9 … −7.3 %) | **Reproduced. FIXED**: `p'` is decided at each evaluated state — the expiry fee only if expired and `CR(V_eff, B̂_FV(P, L)) ≥ L` there; a disagreement between corners makes the amount check wait. The veto case is in `fv_push.py` (V) (v0.4.1: take unchanged) and the exit fuzz's blocker runs exercise it. ECON #51, §5.6, §8.6; §3.8, §4.5, §8.5 and O15 / O19 here corrected | §3.8, §4.5, T-BOX (A65); ECON §5.6, §8.6 |
| R4B-2 | MED | Push-then-freeze defeats the box: a frozen second (honest keeper observation plus an attacker observation just beyond `P_ema`) records `obs = P_ema`, so 1 push + 3–4 frozen seconds move the medians; the same freeze holds the liquidation reference at a pushed `P_ema` | **Reproduced. FIXED** with the reviewer's candidate: `RingEntry` stores the bucket's `(lo, hi, llo, lhi)` (136 B; `Market` 3,104 B) and the box takes the lower median of the lows and the upper median of the highs; the liquidation reference is also capped at `lo_x·(1 + κ_eff)`. Results: the (M) flips fail with 0–10 frozen seconds (v0.4: +2.37 … +5.58 SOL after 4); push-then-freeze refutation delays S1 by 8 s (v0.4: no S1 within 600 s); push-then-freeze sandwich `B̂_ref` ×0.999 (v0.4 ×1.156; borrower −1.90 instead of −19.27 SOL); the flag-S3 amount waits while a freeze lasts. PTF cases are in `fv_push.py`, `refute_push.py`, `ptf_sandwich.py`, the exit fuzz (freezer runs), T-BOX and Crucible. New residual, disclosed: a contrary observation every second widens one side of the box and defers S1 or an S3 on an executable venue while paid (0.002–0.21 SOL/s at 1 %); on Raydium an LP add/remove widening moves `L` too little to matter. ECON §5.6, §12.10, §12.11 and §3.8 here no longer call R3A-1 / R3A-6 (a) closed without qualification | §2.3.4, §3.6, §3.8, §4.4, §4.5, T-BOX (A34, A65); ECON §5.6, §8.2, §12.10, §12.11 |
| R4A-4 | MED | The corner re-check covered 7 parameters; other in-bound values (ε, settlement keeper terms, λ_min, penalty 2,000) failed the battery, so "the compiled bounds are the simulated-safe region" overclaimed | **Reproduced on v0.4. FIXED**: `--scan` moves every `Params` / `TierParams` field with a liveness effect to each compiled extreme; `--targeted` re-derives the bounds on the full 1,655 runs; failing bounds tightened (settlement keeper terms ≤ their SPEC / ADOPTED values, `liq_persist_n ≤ 3`, SPEC CRs as per-tier minima); 128 core-box corners and a stress corner pass the full battery. Partly **rejected with evidence**: ε = 0 / 5 and penalty 2,000 failed only through the withdrawn reserve (0 runs now); λ_min = 10,000 (and the fee-scaled size cap) failed through position size alone — the defaults at the same `Q` give the same outcomes — so the gate now compares sizing parameters at equal size. The wording in ECON §5.7 / §15, §2.3.3 here and O18 says exactly what is covered | §2.3.3 (A73), O18; ECON §5.7, §15; `config_check.py` |
| R4A-5 | LOW | The sim reconstructed `B̂_FV` from FV with a ceiling division, so its S2/S3 lump differed from ARCH's formula by 1 lamport (76 of 86 settlements) | **FIXED**: the lump is now `x − min(x, ⌊Q·P_ema/WAD⌋ + R_due)` (R4B-6), which needs no `B̂_FV`; `fv_parts` returns FV, `B̂_FV` and `p'` for the other uses. The sim and §3.8 / §4.5 use the same formula; M0b regenerates the exit vectors | §3.8, §4.5, §9 M0b; ECON §8.6 |
| R4A-6 | LOW | M0b missed crate items: `switch_liquidity`, `risk::{s1_legs, s2_legs}`, `FeeBps::capped`, `ExitParams.liq_persist_s` and τ's argument, `waterfall::settle`'s inputs | **Confirmed against the crate (read-only). FIXED**: all five added with exact forms — one `rewrite_liquidity` with the Raydium variant (every entry `l = llo = lhi = L_ema`, `(x, y)` recomputed, bucket cleared); the single-point legs deleted; `FeeBps::capped` aligned to the sim (one combined fee at the cap, one ceiling); the field and the τ argument named; `waterfall::settle(v, kind, k_s, fv, q, p_ema, r_due)`; plus every v0.4.1 change | §2.2, §9 M0b |
| R4A-7 | LOW | After a full wipe, cashback and trader balances not yet swept went to the first depositor's shares; the wiping keeper could bundle `[sol_settle → deposit(2 units) → claim_venue_rewards]` | **Reproduced** (the dust depositor took 1 SOL). **FIXED** (the reviewer's first option): a deposit into a live wipe record requires `sweep_trader` and `claim_venue_rewards` since the wipe (`Market.flags` bits 7–8, `WipeSweepPending`; both permissionless and bundled by the depositor); the wiped lenders now get the 1 SOL. The round-3 row's "post-wipe bypass FIXED" was premature | §2.3.4, §3.3, §3.9, §3.11 (A70); ECON §9.5 |
| R4A-8 | LOW | An in-bound `lock_grace_s` (≥ 1 h) can release locks while a position stuck in `PumpMigrating` (pause + grace + S3 wait, up to 3 days) is still borrowed | **Reproduced** (lock day 30.04, position resolves day 33). **FIXED differently**: a relational check against governance values cannot protect positions that snapshot larger values earlier; instead `max_release` folds each position's own snapshot tail (`deadline + max_migration_pause_s + grad_grace_s + s3_wait_s`) into the lock horizon (lock day 34), and `lock_grace_s` covers keeper latency. ECON §9.3 states the condition | §2.3.4, §3.3, §3.4 (A57); ECON §9.3 |
